archive/archive.html.title: The archive
archive/archive.html.html:
Heirlooms and records

The archive

What the House keeps, and what it intends to pass down.

What is being kept

  • The Ezeme Family Archive — the intended growth of the Secretariat's holdings, alongside the cultural documentation already under way through Ozikoro.
  • The House Register and House Accounts — the permanent records of watch succession, loan transactions and the annual interest ceiling.
  • The Family Library — a ten-subject archive: religion and spirituality, philosophy and ethics, politics and government, law, economics and business, leadership and strategy, science and mathematics, history, literature, and Nigeria and West Africa — with a core reading list by age band and a 300+ book catalogue.
  • Oral histories — Igbo proverbs and folk tales recorded from grandparents, and Igbo stories recorded by the parents for the children's audio player.
  • Photographs — a family photo library, with the family's own files already referring to a generator insurance query, land survey documents, solar batteries, goats, a Brazil trip, Christmas 2025 photographs and family reunions.

The digital archive

  • Built around privacy, security, redundancy, long-term ownership and family archive preservation.
  • A document archive, a knowledge base, a photo library, private cloud files, a household media library, encrypted backup with an off-site leg, and private email.
  • Family modules intended to be preserved and served: a family corporation dashboard, farm overview, poultry management, snail farm monitoring, vehicle tracking, family inventory, family library, family genealogy, internal messaging and an AI family assistant.
  • The Ezeme Family Server is designed to sit underground beneath Akuzo Residence and serve the household — five children plus household systems — and nothing else. The wider kindred's building server is deliberately firewalled from it.

Personal technology

  • Secure Personal Hotspot Programme — twenty keychain-sized devices: two name-engraved units each for the seven family members, plus six spares branded simply “Ezeme”. GPS and Bluetooth deliberately excluded. Each member gets their own cellular identity, separate from their phone, managed from the family's own server.
  • “Private infrastructure still needs a succession plan.”

Places of significance

  • Nkpor, Idemili North, Anambra StateThe family's home and the group's base.
  • The Idemmili beltAgricultural land — cheap, and the reason production sits there rather than at Nkpor.
  • AkuzoThe residential district being planned: two production clusters, a civic centre, a community park, two mini football fields, fisheries, two colleges and an underground water spine.
  • OnitshaSchools, merchants and the financial corridor.
  • AbujaThe family's planning and logistics anchor.
  • São Paulo, BrazilA secondary base — the Brás and Lapa districts.
  • Bansko, BulgariaThe Pirin Golf & Country Club property, and the family's fixed January tradition.
  • The seven-region circuitChina, London, Barcelona, Gaborone, Singapore and São Paulo.
  • AwkaWhere the Ozi Ikoro museum, gallery and research hub is planned.

archive/calendar.html.title: The calendar
archive/calendar.html.html:
Traditions

The calendar

Everything the family does together, and how often.

Weekly

  • Saturday morning — Family CourtConvened only when a matter has genuinely been raised. It does not meet as a matter of routine.binding
  • Saturday evening — Family CouncilThe household's cabinet. Weekly, in the evening.binding
  • Saturday, after Council — informal family timeThe meal, conversation and education that follow the Council. Distinct from the Assembly.binding
  • Sunday — Igbo literacyA two-hour session with an Anambra-dialect tutor.stated
  • Portuguese SaturdayOne dedicated day a week: films, music, and one meal in Portuguese. Protected — nothing else may claim a second weekend day.stated
  • Hausa Scrabble ChallengeA weekly Hausa-language Scrabble challenge and story time, building vocabulary through competition rather than formal lessons.stated
  • One protected empty dayOne full day a week with nothing scheduled: no tutor, no lesson, no obligation — free play, friends, boredom and rest.stated

Monthly

  • Family AssemblyThe highest and most inclusive gathering. Distinct from the informal weekly gathering. Hears reports, discusses family matters, education and welfare, traditions and heritage, confirms officers, and celebrates achievements.binding
  • Family Business Board — first SaturdayFunctions as the family office and board of directors for the House's commercial interests.binding

Annually

  • Annual Family Assembly — each DecemberA larger sitting to review the year in full: what the family accomplished, how the businesses performed, how the Treasury stands, how the children progressed, what went wrong, what was learned, and the objectives for the year ahead.binding
  • January — Bansko, BulgariaTen to twelve days at the Pirin Golf & Country Club property. Described as “the one fixed, purely restorative tradition in the family calendar” and the family's shared physical tradition.stated
  • Annual immersion trip — ages 9–15Two to four weeks in a French-, Portuguese- or Spanish-speaking country during school holidays.stated
  • Annual family technology reviewEach child demonstrates one AI-built tool or insight from their own domain.stated
  • Country DayKept as a light, joyful ritual rather than a mandatory-language dinner rule, alongside the illuminated globe.stated
  • Otu Ulo refurbishment campaignThe Igbo tradition of communal self-help applied to Akuzo: one street or cluster refurbished each year, with the group supplying materials at reduced cost and residents supplying labour.stated
  • Annual Akuzo Urban FestivalCultural, educational and commercial. First held at Year 30.proposed

Once in a life

  • Pre-university projectEach child presents a domain-specific project to the Family Council before leaving for university — described as a rite of passage, not an exam.stated
  • Anglican family occasionsBaptisms, weddings and Christmas services attended as cultural and family participation, not as a claim on anyone's personal belief.stated

archive/culture.html.title: Culture and identity
archive/culture.html.html:
Igbo first

Culture and identity

Language, faith, music, food and the practices the House keeps.

Igbo first

  • “Igbo first. Every child speaks, reads, and takes pride in the Idemmili-Onicha dialect before any other language.” Described as the first inheritance, and non-negotiable.
  • Phase 1 (ages 0–4): parents speak only Igbo at home, with no code-switching.
  • Weekly Sunday Igbo literacy with an Anambra-dialect tutor.
  • Igbo proverbs and folk tales told orally, from grandparents — required ages 8–12.

Language

  • The stated goal is five core languages by fifteen: Igbo, English, French, Portuguese (Brazilian) and Spanish — with Hausa also established as a household language in Phase 2. The family's own documents disagree on the count, listing five under a heading that names six in practice.
  • Domain sixth languages: Mandarin for Isiome and Okodu; Arabic or German where a posting requires it.
  • Rules: one person, one language · model, never correct · consistency over intensity.
  • Tools: custom Igbo and Hausa tile sets including correct Igbo diacritics, a Yoto audio player, and an illuminated globe for Country Day.

Faith and ethics

  • “The household is not raised within a specific doctrinal faith.”
  • Values formation draws on Igbo cosmology and ethics — Odinani, ancestral reverence, and the proverbs and moral teaching threaded through the family's oral tradition and library — alongside comparative literacy in world religions.
  • Children take part in Anglican family occasions — baptisms, weddings, Christmas services — as cultural and family participation, not as a claim on their personal belief. Each child is free to arrive at their own convictions as an adult.
  • The Family Court is grounded in Odinani's emphasis on balance and repair over retribution. The Council is grounded in Ụmụnna.

Music, games and food

  • One core instrument, with piano recommended as the shared family baseline; one traditional instrument tied to heritage — an Igbo instrument such as ogene, ekwe or oja, or a Brazilian instrument such as pandeiro; one dance style; one sport; one performance skill.
  • Chess and Ncho — described as the family's everyday and traditional games.
  • Portuguese Saturday includes one meal in Portuguese; Country Day dinners bring other cuisines.
  • Comfort moving between a village festival in Anambra, a Brazilian festa junina, and a concert hall anywhere in the world.

Igbo in the technology

  • Hand-defined Igbo voice intents — for example “Gbanwuo oku ulo” to turn on the living room lights, and “Gosi m akuko Anambra” to show Anambra news.
  • Fine-tuning Whisper for Igbo, and training a Piper Igbo voice, are medium-term goals.
  • Translation pairs named as cultural preservation: English to and from Igbo, Portuguese, French and Spanish.
  • The dialect dictionary already under way through Ozikoro feeds this work.

archive/family-office.html.title: The family offices
archive/family-office.html.html:
The family office

The family offices

What the House keeps, controls and reports on.

The Family Treasury

The Family Treasurer

The family's collective investment portfolio; an emergency reserve for the household; family property held in common; education funds for the children and future generations; the family's ownership interests in Ezeme Group businesses and other ventures; philanthropic funds; and intergenerational wealth intended to outlast any one generation.

What it keeps and controls

  • Multiple approvals — never a single signature — for any major transaction.
  • Proper records kept at all times
  • Reports to the Family Business Board monthly
  • Reports to the Family Assembly at least annually

The Family Secretariat & Archive

The Family Secretary, with the Family Archivist

“Someone must be responsible for the family's records, or its history and decisions will be lost to memory alone.”

What it keeps and controls

  • The Charter and all amendments
  • Minutes of the Council, Court, Business Board and Assembly
  • Family agreements and Court decisions
  • The family tree, birth records and marriage records
  • Property and business records
  • Family photographs, achievements and historical documents
  • Annual reports to the Assembly

Over time these holdings are intended to grow into a proper Ezeme Family Archive, alongside the cultural documentation already under way through Ozikoro.

archive/institutions.html.title: The institutions
archive/institutions.html.html:
Governance of the House

The institutions

Five bodies and eight offices. The firewall between them is the point.

The Family Assembly

Highest and most inclusive. Sovereign.

Meets: Monthly, with a larger Annual Assembly each December.

  • Hears reports from the Council and the Business Board
  • Discusses major family matters
  • Approves major changes to family rules and to the Charter
  • Discusses the education and welfare of the children
  • Discusses family traditions, heritage and the Odinani cultural anchor
  • Celebrates achievements
  • Elects or confirms the Family Officers
  • Reviews the state of the family each year

The Family Council

A cabinet rather than a court. Closest in spirit to Ụmụnna.

Meets: Weekly, Saturday evening. Emergency sitting at the request of any two voting members.

  • Family values, traditions and the Odinani cultural anchor
  • Children's development, education and the Family Education Structure
  • Family welfare, health and wellbeing
  • Relationships, roles and responsibilities
  • Household responsibilities and family property
  • Family projects, including the Akuzo Residence and Akuzo Court developments
  • Major purchases and family travel
  • Family reputation
  • Long-term dynastic planning, including the Holding Structure and the Raising Plan

Somtoo and Ifeoma sit as founding co-chairs for the life of the Council's first generation. Each of the five children holds a seat.

The Family Court

Justice. It does not decide business questions.

Meets: Saturday morning, ahead of the Council, and only when a matter has genuinely been raised. It does not meet as a matter of routine.

  • Nine steps: Petition · Notice · Hearing · Evidence · Questions · Defence · Deliberation · Judgment · Restoration
  • Outcomes: no wrongdoing established · warning or apology · restitution or replacement · temporary loss of privilege or additional responsibility · mediation, reconciliation or a behavioural agreement · referral to the Council
  • For children, consequences are age-appropriate and educational — never humiliating, and never abusive
  • No person may be simultaneously judge, prosecutor and accused in the same matter
  • It is not for ordinary disagreements that a conversation could resolve
  • Appeal lies to the full Council at its next sitting
  • No matter heard by the Court may be raised in, or influence, a Business Board proceeding, and vice versa

The Family Business Board

Business and wealth. It does not adjudicate personal grievances.

Meets: First Saturday of each month.

  • Business strategy across the group's domains
  • Investments, assets and property
  • Budgets, financial performance and risk
  • New ventures
  • Hiring senior employees and placing family members into business roles
  • Succession planning and ownership
  • Dividends, reinvestment and business ethics
  • Oversight of family-owned ventures such as Ozikoro and Ozituma, which remain administratively distinct from the group

Somtoo chairs as founding principal until succession. Each domain heir holds a seat, with voting rights activating on admission to full membership. Akunnia, as designated Chief Investment Officer, holds standing responsibility for consolidated financial reporting to the Board and the Treasury.

The offices

Who holds what

  • Family HeadOverall leadership and external representationSomtoo, founding
  • Family ChairpersonChairs Council meetingsCouncil appointment
  • Family Judge / Justice ChairPresides over the Court; excluded from any matter in which they have a personal stakeCouncil appointment
  • Family SecretaryRecords and minutes for the SecretariatCouncil appointment
  • Family TreasurerOversees the TreasuryCouncil appointment
  • Business Board ChairChairs the Business BoardSomtoo, founding
  • Family ArchivistPreserves family history and documentsCouncil appointment
  • Children's RepresentativeGives the younger generation a formal voice in Council and Assembly before they reach full voting membershipCouncil appointment

archive/membership.html.title: Membership
archive/membership.html.html:
Belonging to the House

Membership

How a person joins, what they may do, and what nobody may be given.

The stages

A member either has not yet been admitted, or is admitted and equal

  • ObserverAges 8–12Present at the weekly family gathering and, where age-appropriate, at the Assembly. May speak when invited. Not yet a member; no vote.
  • ParticipantAges 13–17May raise matters directly, and speaks in Court, Council and Assembly proceedings that concern them. Their account and preferences are formally recorded and weighed by the Secretariat. Not yet a member; no vote.
  • MemberFrom age 18, on admission by the CouncilFull and equal voting rights in the Assembly, the Council, the Court and the Business Board simultaneously, from the moment of admission.
    “Once a person is admitted to sit in the meetings as a full member, their voice carries equal weight to any other member's, regardless of age, seniority, or how recently they were admitted. There is no partial or graduated vote.”

The rules of belonging

  • Spouses admitted into the family in later generations join as full members upon marriage, at the Council's discretion.
  • Domain-heir status is separate from the vote. Responsibilities formalise separately under the Holding Structure but do not gate the underlying vote.
  • Membership is not employment. Being a family member does not automatically make someone a business director, and does not by itself entitle anyone to a role, a title or a share of profit. Anyone who takes on work is paid for that work like any other position.
  • Amendment. The Council may amend the Charter at a regular sitting after one week's circulation, ratified by the Assembly at its next sitting. Amendments to the founding co-chairs' reserve veto, to the equal-vote principle, or to the separation of the Court and the Business Board require unanimous consent of all voting members.

archive/the-house.html.title: The House
archive/the-house.html.html:
Private archive

The House

Who the family is, what it holds to, and what it is building.

The motto

The House's own words

Onye Ayana Nwanne

Onye aghala nwanne ya

Let no one abandon their kin.

The founding

The House of Ezeme is the immediate family and lineage founded by Somtoo Ezeme and Ifeoma Ezeme, and carried forward by their children — Isiome, Akunnia, Idenze, Uli and Okodu — and their descendants. Seven people in the household.

The family states its own intention: “The House of Ezeme is not just a family — it is a dynasty in formation. Every decision we make as parents is a deliberate act of institution-building.” Set against it, in the same documents: “raising children who are genuinely well — rested, secure, playful, and free to be ordinary sometimes.”

Ezeme Group is dated FOUNDED 2025. The family's planning horizon runs to 2055.

The values

Stated as foundational principles

  • Family before personal interestThe household's interest comes before any individual member's.
  • Equality before family rulesOnce admitted as a member, a voice carries equal weight — regardless of age, seniority, or how recently the person was admitted.
  • The right to be heardEvery member may speak to matters that concern them.
  • RespectFor elders, for juniors, for the household, and for those outside it.
  • ResponsibilityEach member answers for what they take on.
  • TransparencyRecords are kept, decisions are minuted, and the family's affairs are not hidden from its members.
  • Pay for workEveryone who works is paid for that work. Membership is not itself a form of compensation.
  • EducationEducation and childhood are treated as the first investment.
  • IndependenceMembers are encouraged to build their own careers and identities rather than being forced into the family's businesses.
  • StewardshipWhat is held is held for those who come after, not only for those who hold it.
  • ReconciliationThe aim of a dispute is repair, not retribution.
  • The firewallPersonal disputes, business decisions and public commitments are kept apart, so that a disagreement in one does not freeze the others.

Dynasty principles

What the House holds to across generations

  • One marriage. One family. All five children raised together in Nigeria, for dynasty loyalty and succession clarity.
  • One protected day a week. Nothing scheduled — no tutor, no lesson, no obligation.
  • Belief is a personal inheritance, not an assigned one. The household is not raised inside a specific doctrinal faith; each child arrives at their own convictions as an adult.
  • Domain activation at Master's level. No child assumes leadership of their domain before completing a first Master's degree.
  • No sale outside the bloodline. Heirloom assets are inherited, not liquidated.
  • Education — and childhood itself — is the first investment.

Where the record is silent

Recorded as gaps, not filled in

  • The meaning of the name “Ezeme” is not stated anywhere in the family's own documents. It is recorded here as a gap rather than filled in.
  • There is no provision for a member to leave. No resignation, renunciation, expulsion or exit appears in any document. The only exit-adjacent mechanism is disengagement, which moves operational control — never ownership — after 24–36 months of inactivity; the disengaged heir keeps their economic entitlement in full.
  • No naming ceremony, New Yam festival, Ofala, masquerade or burial rite is named anywhere in the corpus. The one Anambra festival referred to is described only as “a village festival in Anambra”.

archive/watches.html.title: The watches
archive/watches.html.html:
The Horological Succession Charter

The watches

Five watches bound to offices, not to people.

Tier I — House Leadership

  • Patek Philippe Nautilus 5726/1A — Annual Calendar, SteelPatriarch of the House — Isiome Ezeme$130,000 – 180,000
  • Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Jumbo 15202OR — Rose Gold, 39 mmMatriarch of the House — Akunnia Ezeme$110,000 – 180,000

Tier II — Principal Heirs

  • A. Lange & Söhne Datograph Perpetual 410.025 — Pink GoldSenior Male Heir — Idenze Ezeme$130,000 – 175,000
  • Vacheron Constantin Overseas Perpetual Calendar 7900V/110R — Rose GoldSenior Female Heir — Uli Ezeme$120,000 – 180,000

Tier III — Senior Branch Heads

  • Patek Philippe Perpetual Calendar Chronograph 5270G — White GoldThird Son — Okodu Ezeme$150,000 – 260,000

The rules

Binding on every heir who holds a charter watch

  • The watch belongs to the office, not the person. The Nautilus belongs to the office of Patriarch. On death or relinquishment the watch passes with the office: the Senior Male Heir inherits the Nautilus and rises to Patriarch, and his Datograph passes to whoever next occupies the office of Senior Male Heir. The same cascade runs through the Matriarch and the Overseas.
  • All remaining watches are bound to their branches and not to individuals, and descend through their assigned branch.
  • No sale outside the bloodline. No charter watch may be sold, gifted outside the bloodline, donated, auctioned, pawned at any commercial institution, or transferred by any means to anyone who is not a direct blood descendant of the Founder. This prohibition is absolute and permanent. Any such act is void, forfeits the transgressor's claim to the office, and the watch reverts to the custody of the Patriarch and Matriarch.
  • No will, trust or court order may direct a charter watch outside the bloodline; the House will contest such an order.
  • Selection. Independently verifiable secondary-market value above US$100,000, and a manufacture that has shown it can survive, remain prestigious and appreciate across generations. The youngest brand on the list was founded in 1905.
  • Servicing every five years without exception, at a certified maker or authorised service centre, at the House treasury's cost. An heir who damages a watch through negligence bears the full restoration cost from their personal share of distributions.
  • Insurance at the House's expense, at replacement value no less than the current appraised value, reviewed every three years.
  • Rankings are reaffirmed by the Patriarch and Matriarch every twenty-five years and recorded in the House Register. Values are as at 2025–2026 and are reappraised independently at the time of any loan.
  • Holdings, values and Jewellery Bank terms are confidential except as the law requires.

The Jewellery Bank

The only commercial transaction permitted

  • The Ezeme Jewellery Bank is “a business owned and operated within the Ezeme Group”, and it is the only commercial transaction in which a charter watch may be involved. An heir borrows against a watch rather than ever selling it.
  • Eligibility. Only the registered holder named in the House Register. No proxy, spouse, executor or third party may apply.
  • Deposit. Physical deposit in the Bank's vault against a formal Receipt of Custody recording the reference number, serial number, condition rating and agreed loan amount, with photographs taken on deposit and before return.
  • Loan. Not to exceed 65% of the independently appraised secondary-market value, and ordinarily not less than US$65,000.
  • Interest shall not exceed the ceiling approved annually by the Patriarch and Matriarch and recorded in the House Accounts.
  • The fourteen-day rule. The entire loan must be placed into income-generating fixed-interest instruments within fourteen days of receipt — FGN bonds, Nigerian Treasury Bills, FGN Savings Bonds, sovereign Eurobonds, or other fixed income approved in writing by the House Council. No portion of the principal may be spent on personal consumption, business ventures, property, or any other purpose. Proof of investment within fourteen days, or the loan is called in immediately.
  • The coupon constitutes the heir's supplemental living income. A quarterly statement confirming the principal intact is required; failure constitutes default.
  • Redemption within five business days of full repayment. If custody exceeded twelve months, the watch is serviced by an authorised centre at the Bank's expense.
  • Default is referred to the Patriarch and Matriarch for internal adjudication. Under no circumstances may the watch pass to any external creditor, debt recovery agency or court appointee. The House may restructure, suspend distributions or transfer custody to the next senior heir of that branch — it never leaves the bloodline.
  • Every transaction is entered into the House Register and countersigned by the Patriarch, Matriarch or a designated representative.

What this is

The domains

Paired for management, not ownership

Finance & Investment Systems · Governance, Law & Security

Two sectors, paired so the work is deep rather than broad. Both are the child's from birth, and both begin trading on the day they are born.

The industries

13 businesses

Every business in the domain, and what Akunnia learns inside it. Training in all of them begins at birth — by presence first, then by hand. On the floor from six or eight, keeping the book from thirteen, deciding from sixteen.

BusinessWhat it isWhat they learn, and when

Aku Private EquityBuying whole companies and improving themThe Blackstone model the group chose deliberately. Reading a company's accounts at 10, a valuation at 13, a deal from 16.
Aku InsuranceUnderwriting and risk transferWhat risk costs and who carries it. A premium at 10, a claims file at 13, the underwriting stance from 16.

Aku TechnologyInternal infrastructure operated as a companyThe group's own systems — infrastructure, not a business with outside customers. Using it at 8, administering it at 13, owning it from 16.

When the domain transfers

Takeover at 25

The business is formed on the day of birth and runs under professional management. It is advised fully by Akunnia from sixteen. Control transfers on completion of the master's degree.

The model

How it works

Fully trained in every one of their industries from birth. Not introduced to a sector at eighteen — raised inside it.

The domain is registered on the day of birth, and the business starts immediately — formed, or bought outright from an existing small business and brought into the group. It is a going concern before the child can speak.

By ten they are already trading in their own market. The first daughter deals in the financial market before she is ten. Every child does the equivalent in theirs.

The business runs with their advice and input, fully, from sixteen. Not consulted — deciding.

It grows with them through higher education. The business is not paused while they study; they advise it from campus and work in it in the vacations.

They take over when fully ready — and readiness is defined: the master's degree, completed.

One thing this model does not do: it does not hold a title over the child. Ownership is held by the group, the business is run by a professional manager until the child is competent, and nothing about it is required of them. They may decline the whole of it without losing membership, affection or standing.

Taking over

Eight steps, in order

  • 1. Grow up inside it

  • 3. Study

    18–23

    A first degree, chosen by the person. Institutions are options, not an itinerary.

  • 4. Work somewhere else

    20–25

    Paid, time-limited placements with written roles, named supervisors and performance feedback. External experience is expected before any permanent family role. This is the evidence base for everything that follows.

  • 5. Rotate

    18–30

    At least two regions, and structured time inside a sibling's sector. Mandatory, not optional. The point is that no heir takes over a business they have only read about.

  • 6. The Master's gate

    23–25

    No child assumes leadership of their domain before completing a first Master's degree. This is the single hardest gate in the structure, and it is stated as binding.

  • 7. Take the domain

    26–28

    Control is granted by the Family Business Board against active engagement, attendance and delivery on an agreed mandate. Ownership was never at stake — it is fixed by the trust. What transfers is control.

  • 8. Hand it on

    33+

    The next generation enters the same spine at age 0. Same bands, same gates, same protections.

  • Ownership is fixed; control is earned. Beneficial ownership cannot be revoked for non-performance. Operational control is granted, not inherited.
  • Non-engagement moves control, not ownership. After 24–36 months of inactivity the Board appoints a steward. The disengaged heir keeps their economic entitlement in full. Nothing is confiscated.
  • Membership is not employment. Being family does not make anyone a director, and does not entitle anyone to a role, a title or a share of profit. Anyone who works is paid for that work.
  • Qualification before appointment. Family members meet the same standards as anyone else, and a non-family executive may lead any company where they are the strongest candidate.
  • Skills before succession. The placement record — where they worked, how long, under whom, and what they delivered — is what the appointment rests on.

THE CORPUS

Every document the family has written, what each one is, and what it describes.

Eighteen source documents sit in the Drive. From them a 60-plan library was built. This page is the map between the two: what exists, what each thing is for, and what it does or does not cover.

1. The source documents — eighteen files from the Drive

These are the originals. Everything else in the portal derives from them.

The São Paulo Course Map is written as a companion to "The Founder's Hardware & AI Curriculum" and cites "the Reference Unit". Neither appears anywhere in the Drive when it is searched directly. They are either sections inside other documents or they were never written.

2. The plan library — sixty plans for the conglomerate

Built from the sources above at a 15-year horizon with Year 1 set at 2027, in naira at ₦1,600/USD. Its own README warns: "Do not compare dollars across plans."

  • 00 The mother company — the Family Business plan

  • Fifty-four company plans — every regulated activity in its own company with its own board, licence and audit
  • Eleven companion documents — the executive summary, the operating architecture, the knowledge base, the naming architecture, the consolidated capital plans, the licence audit, the citation audit, two number reconciliations, the Akuzo cost basis and the arithmetic method note

3. Where the library stops and the Drive continues

This is the most important thing on this page. The library is a destination. The Drive is the actual plan. They do not describe the same business.

The library covers well The library does not contain
The five sector groups and 54 companies, at a 15-year horizon from 2027The furniture and soft furnishings cluster — the engine that funds the land

The hotspot import, the hardware platform, and the household infrastructure

The summary: if you read only the library, you see a conglomerate that does not yet exist and miss the businesses that are actually starting. The library has 54 company plans for companies that are not yet formed, and no plan for the one company that is.

5. Contradictions carried, not resolved

Recorded here so nobody builds on a number the family has stated two ways.

  1. The buildings. The Akuzo Development Programme's closing paragraph cites *"the full combined

$1.85M exposure"*; its own line items sum to $1,966,000. And the 30-year plan prices a storey building at ₦35–50m across 27 buildings, while these two alone cost about US$1.97m — roughly ₦2.67bn at that plan's own rate.

  1. The 30-year cost model has no line for the US$234,000 per building of standalone solar,

battery, biodigester, cistern and LPG that the Programme adds on top of the mains-plus-inverter standard the plan specifies.

  1. The hotspot. The specification says one USB-C port, no SIM tray and 2–3 clients; the

ready-to-send RFQ asks for two ports, a dual nano-SIM tray and 10–15 clients.

  1. The watches. The Horological Charter refers throughout to "the ten watches" but names five.
  2. The museum's legal form. Its letter of intent is signed "Director, Ozi Ikoro Foundation" while

the entity is Ozi Ikoro Limited.

  1. The museum's location. The plan is for Awka; the family base and every other venture are at

Nkpor and Akuzo, some 40 km away.

  1. Two structures under one name. The Master Plan is a 30-year Nigerian family conglomerate; the

11-Year Plan is a single-founder company in São Paulo. Neither document acknowledges the other.

  1. Languages. The Raising Plan lists five core languages including Hausa in one section, and gives

the baseline as Igbo, English, French, Portuguese and Spanish without Hausa in another.

  1. Akunnia's first university is UNIZIK in the Raising Plan and NUS in the Holding Structure.
  2. Two horizon and FX bases. The library runs 15 years from 2027 at ₦1,600/USD; the Akuzo plan

runs 2025–2055 at ₦1,360/USD. Anything moving between them needs re-basing.

6. Superseded

Documents or mechanisms that have been set aside, kept here so the record shows what was considered.

Superseded By Date

The furniture and soft furnishings business stands; its growth mechanism in place of Igba Odibo is not yet writtenOctober 2026
Ezeme Family Holding Structure — "all sectors owned under a single entity… one roof, one ledger, one name"House of Ezeme Corporate Architecture-2, which replaces it with the five-layer structureAugust 2026

7. Two documents derived from the corpus

Neither is a family source. Both are readings of the sources, and both are held in the portal.

Document From What it is
The strategic review (GUIDANCE-REVIEW.md)Supplied by the founder, October 2026A 141,000-character review of the 16 Drive documents. Professional and carefully hedged: nearly every paragraph is labelled source proposal, recommendation or validation required. It corrects the sources' optimism and is right to. Two things it does not know: the corpus is now 19 documents, and it names the fifth house Udeze, which the family renamed Okodu. It also treats the Igba Odibo apprenticeship model as live, which has since been scrapped.
The first two years (THE-FIRST-TWO-YEARS.md)DerivedThat review rearranged into a working sequence: the next two years, beginning with child one. It applies the three corrections above, adds the Ozi Ikoro master plan the review never saw, and states plainly where it differs from the review.

The distinction that matters. The review is an assessment of proposals. The first-two-years document is a sequence of decisions. Where they disagree, the disagreements are stated rather than smoothed — see Part 7 of the two-year plan.

EZEME — DOMAIN ACQUISITION LIST

Re-checked: 9 October 2026, against RDAP (rdap.org), following redirects to each registry, and against the live HTTP response of every name said to be held.

Status key: AVAILABLE = no registration record · REGISTERED = held by another party · HELD = already yours.

One caveat, stated because it will cost you money otherwise. RDAP proves whether a name is registered; it does not prove the price. Some registrars mark short, dictionary-like names as premium, and country registries (.ng, .africa) do not all publish through RDAP. Verify the checkout price before you commit — and never buy a name at a premium before Tier 1 is secured.

What changed in this revision

This list was materially wrong, and four of the corrections matter.

  1. It listed idenze.com as a third party's. It is not — it is live and serving family content.

It is off the "do not chase" list and onto the held list.

  1. It omitted ozituma.com, which is live. A live business was missing from the acquisition list.
  2. It described ozikoro.com as an "Igbo language and heritage platform". That is Ozituma. Ozikoro

is the culture, history and archive platform — and its own master plan is a museum and gallery.

  1. It planned public branch paths at ezeme.org/isiome, /akunnia, /idenze, /uli, /okodu.

Those paths must not exist. The children are unborn, and neither their names nor their houses may appear on a public site. The address plan below replaces that.

  1. ezeme.org was recorded as returning HTTP 522 with no origin. It serves the site now.

Also re-checked, and unchanged: every Tier 1 and Tier 2 name is still available. The delay caused by the Namecheap IP mismatch has cost nothing.

Already held

Domain State Notes
ezeme.orgHELD, liveThe institution's address. HTTP 200, serving the Ezeme enterprise site. On Cloudflare, origin on AWS.
family.ezeme.orgHELD, gatedThe private plans portal. HTTP 401 unauthenticated — server-side nginx basic auth, its own web root, own certificate.
ozikoro.comHELD, liveCulture, history and archive. HTTP 200. Its master plan is a museum, gallery and research hub to be built in Awka.

One thing to confirm yourself: RDAP shows idenze.com as registered to someone. It serves family content and you have described it as yours, so it is recorded here as held — but if you have not personally renewed it, check the registrar account, because a family domain sitting in someone else's account is a problem that only surfaces at the worst moment.

Only akunnia.com of the five branch names is still free. That asymmetry would have decided a branch-domain strategy — except the branch domains are no longer public at all (see the address plan).

Tier 1 — register this week

Address plan

Corrected. The previous plan put the five branch houses at public paths on ezeme.org. That cannot happen: the children are unborn, and their names, their order and their houses are private until they are not. Nothing on this page should be read as a plan to publish them.

    /                                        the group, the ten sectors in five domains
    /sectors.html                            what each domain covers
    /manufacturing.html                      the Nkpor furniture and soft furnishings business
    /ventures.html                           Ozikoro, Ozituma, OmaPolo
    /record.html                             dated record of what exists

GATED — its own vhost, own web root, own certificate, nginx auth_basic
  family.ezeme.org                           the plans portal
    /                                        every plan, document and source
    /library/                                73 plan-library documents
    /documents/                              the roadmaps, capital plans, governance
    /sources/                                the 18 Drive source documents
    /programme/                              the nine ventures the library omits
    /admin/                                  account management (owner only)

NEVER PUBLIC — reserved, redirect only, noindex
  ezemeholdings.com   → 301 → ezeme.org
  ezemeholdings.ng    → 301 → ezeme.org
  <branch>group.com   → reserved; must NOT resolve publicly
  idenze.com          → reserved for the Idenze child

Two rules with security consequences.

  1. ezemeholdings.com should never host anything and never be indexed. The ownership layer's

address appearing in a search result is an invitation to look for what sits behind it. Redirect only, noindex, no email on that domain.

  1. The branch domains in Tier 3 must not resolve. An isiomegroup.com that answers, even with a

holding page, publishes a name that is supposed to be private. Park them, do not point them anywhere, and keep them off any public certificate transparency log — a TLS certificate is published publicly the moment it is issued.

Blocked, and how to unblock it

The Tier 1 purchases cannot proceed yet. Namecheap's API has an IP whitelist set to 102.90.124.177, while the actual egress address is 102.90.125.55. Every call is refused.

Two ways out, either of which works:

  • Add 102.90.125.55 to the whitelist in Namecheap (Profile → Tools → API Access → Whitelisted IPs),

or

  • Remove the restriction and rely on the API key, which is scoped to your account.

The second is simpler and carries little extra risk for a personal account. Until one is done, none of Tier 1, Tier 1b or Tier 2 can be registered.

Renewal discipline

Register every Tier 1 and Tier 2 name for the maximum term the registrar allows — ten years where offered. A family institution that loses its own .org to a lapse in year seven has handed a stranger the front door. Put every domain on auto-renew and record the registrar, the account and the recovery email in the family area, not in one person's head.

idenze.com is the live example of why. A domain that the last revision of this document had filed as a stranger's, that is in fact yours and serving content, is a domain whose ownership was not written down anywhere checkable. Write it down.
