THE FIRST TWO YEARS

A detailed plan, sequenced from child one.

This rearranges the strategic review you sent — The House of Ezeme: Family Legacy, Enterprise, Education and Succession Master Plan — into a working sequence, adds what the corpus and the website work have established since, and applies the corrections you have made. The review is a careful document; it is written in an advisory register and it hedges almost every line. This is the same material, decided.

How to read this

Three registers, marked throughout:

  • FACT — verified in the source documents or on the live systems. Checkable.
  • DECISION — yours. I state the options and recommend one; only you can close it.
  • PLAN — this document's proposal for the next two years.

The review you sent was written against 16 Drive documents. There are now 19 — the corpus was re-inventoried and three more were found, including OZI IKORO: MASTER BUSINESS PLAN, which the review never saw. It also uses Udeze, which you renamed to Okodu, and it treats the Igba Odibo apprenticeship model as live, which you have scrapped. Those three corrections run through everything below.

PART 1 — WHERE YOU ACTUALLY STAND

1.1 What exists
Ozi Ikoro LimitedRC 8955047, incorporated 29 October 2025, Nkpor-Agu, Anambra State
ozikoro.comLive — culture, history, archive
ozituma.comLive — a free dictionary of African languages
omapolo.comLive — clothing, on Bumpa
ezeme.orgLive — the enterprise's public site, five pages
family.ezeme.orgLive and gated — the plans portal: 59 plans, 73 library documents, 18 source documents, 9 structured ventures

1.2 What does not exist

The workshop. Both Akuzo buildings. The server rooms. The museum. The trust and the PTC and the GBC. The five child groups. The university, the polytechnic, the colleges, the hospital, the clinic, the power business, the farms. None of it is built, and no entity has been formed for any of it.

1.3 The two documents that matter most, and what is wrong with each

The furniture and soft furnishings model is the operating plan for the business actually being started. It is coherent, specific and costed — and it is built entirely on Igba Odibo, which you have scrapped. So there is now no stated mechanism by which this business grows. That is not a detail. It is the first thing to fix.

The Ozi Ikoro master plan is the only complete business plan in the corpus, for the only company that actually exists. It specifies a warehouse conversion down to the fume hood and the eyewash station — and contains no capital budget at all. No conversion cost, no fit-out cost, no collection budget, no working capital, no break-even.

1.4 Three arithmetic problems you should know about

  1. The Akuzo building programme's closing paragraph states "the full combined $1.85M exposure";

its own itemised lines sum to $1,966,000.

  1. The 30-year Akuzo plan prices a storey building at ₦35–50m across 27 buildings — ₦1.23bn — while

the two buildings actually costed come to about ₦2.67bn at that plan's own exchange rate. And its cost model has no line for the $234,000 per building of solar, battery, biodigester, cistern and LPG the building programme adds.

  1. The hotspot specification says one USB-C port, no SIM tray and 2–3 clients; the RFQ that is ready

to send asks for two ports, a dual nano-SIM tray and 10–15 clients.

None of these is fatal. All three become expensive if they are discovered late.

PART 2 — CHILD ONE

2.1 Who child one is, in the documents

FACT. The source documents name him Isiome — first son, Patriarch of the House — and pair him with Agriculture & Food Systems and Manufacturing & Industrial Production. They propose a field-to-factory pathway and an education track running through Tsinghua, Wageningen, NTU and São Paulo.

He is unborn. So the next two years are either the run-up to him or the first two years of his life, and this plan is written to work either way.

2.2 The correction that matters most to him

The review says it plainly and it is right: "The proposed pairings are useful as a portfolio map, but they are not job assignments."

Every source document assigns him two sectors at birth. Do not do that operationally. Concretely, in the next two years, that means:

  • No company is formed in his name. The guidance proposes incorporating each child's group at

birth, 100% held by the holding company. Do not. It creates entities with no purpose, filing obligations you will forget, and a public record tying a newborn to a conglomerate. Reserve the name; form nothing.

  • No title, no domain, no seat. He holds no office, no directorship, no "head of agriculture".

The documents give him the Patriarch's office. He is an infant.

  • No workforce ever answers to him. Not at two, not at twelve.
  • His interests may differ. He may want none of it. The plan must survive that, and so must he.

What he does get in the next two years: health, attachment, language, play, safety, and a family that is not anxious about money in front of him.

2.3 What child one needs in years 0–2 — the concrete list

Domain What it is, practically What it is not
HealthImmunisation on the Nigerian schedule, a named paediatrician, growth monitoring, and a written record that travels with himA "family clinic business"
AttachmentOne or two consistent primary carers; responsive, predictable care; parental leave taken, not skippedA rota of staff

EnglishOrdinary talk, songs, booksInstruction, or "academic literacy"

The single rule that governs all of it: "A child's health, safety, relationships, play and developing preferences take priority over a business plan." The review states it; the source documents do not.

2.4 The one unscheduled day

PLAN. From the moment there is a schedule to unschedule, child one gets at least one largely unstructured day every week, and the enrichment ceiling is treated as a maximum of 8–10 hours a week outside school — never a target to fill.

This is the discipline that the source documents' five-language, multiple-degree, immersion-trip programme would destroy. The languages are the clearest example. The documents contradict each other — one list has Hausa, another does not; Portuguese appears in some and Spanish in others. The review's answer is right and this plan adopts it:

  • Igbo and English: from birth, unconditionally.
  • French or Portuguese: chosen later, on real use. Portuguese has a Brazil connection; French has

regional value. Teach one properly rather than two badly.

  • **Spanish, Hausa, Mandarin, German, Arabic: only when an actual course, job or family connection

exists.** Not at two. Possibly not at fifteen.

  • Drop the target of five languages by fifteen. It is an aspiration in the source material, not a

developmental standard.

2.5 Money for child one

PLAN. Open, in the next two years:

  1. A small monthly education fund — a separate account, funded from the family's income, not from

a business's working capital. Any amount, consistently.

  1. A health record — written, current, portable.
  2. A file that says who owns what. There is nothing to record yet, which is the point: record

that nothing is held in his name, so no informal claim can form later.

Do not fund any of this from a company account, and do not treat family education spending as a business expense. The review is right that these must be budgeted separately.

2.6 The privacy rule, which starts now

FACT — the one thing already built and enforced. Nothing about the children appears publicly. Not a name, not a photograph, not a birthday, not a school. ezeme.org carries zero child names, verified on every deploy, and a canary checks it every fifteen minutes.

PLAN. Extend it to everything you own:

  • No child's face, name, school, location or routine on ozikoro.com, ozituma.com, omapolo.com,

or any social account.

  • The hotspot allocation in the source documents names all five children on engraved units. **When

that order is placed, the engraving must not carry names** — or the units become a public record shipped through customs.

  • Do not put a child's records into a consumer AI tool, ever.
  • The portal is gated for a reason. Keep it that way.

2.7 What carries forward to children two through five

PLAN. The same shape, repeated: health, Igbo and English, play, one unscheduled day, no company, no title, no obligation. Two things change per child:

  • The optional exposure area changes — Akunnia toward finance and law, Idenze toward learning and

health, Uli toward media and logistics, Okodu toward energy and building. Offered, not assigned.

  • The birth year sets every roadmap row. The 60-plan library anchors Year 1 at 2027; if child one

arrives in the programme's first year, plan Year 1 is his age 0–1 and every roadmap resolves to ages. One date — the birth year — sets every row. Until then the roadmaps stay in plan years, which is how the plans state them.

And one correction across all five: the review's own child table says Udeze where the family now says Okodu. Every document in the corpus that says Udeze is out of date.

PART 3 — THE TWO-YEAR BUSINESS PLAN

3.1 Build one business, and it is not the grandest one

PLAN. In the next two years, build one thing: the Nkpor furniture and soft furnishings workshop.

Why this one, and not the museum, not Akuzo, not the farms:

  • It is order-led. You sell a fit-out before you buy the timber. Institutions pay deposits.
  • Two crafts share one roof, one supply chain, one fleet and one client relationship. One

contract covers a finished room, which no single-craft competitor can quote.

  • The demand is institutional and repeat. Schools, offices, hospitals, hotels — and the tenders

are public.

  • The quality differentiator is real and cheap to hold: every piece from kiln-dried timber,

against a market that uses air-dried and green timber which warps inside three to five years.

  • The trade knowledge already exists in the family.
  • And it is the business the documents call the engine — the one that funds the land.

What it is not: the ten sectors, the university, the city, or the empire. Those are the destination. The review's strongest single recommendation is that you must not scale a new venture while the preceding one has unresolved customer, margin, compliance or cash-control problems. Two years is enough to prove one workshop and not enough to prove a conglomerate.

3.2 What must exist before day one

Six things, and the sixth is new:

  1. Space in Nkpor with room for a woodworking floor and a soft furnishings floor side by side.
  2. Both equipment sets — woodworking machines, and sewing and upholstery machines.
  3. Power solved independently. Woodworking is the heavy load. A workshop that stops when the grid

does cannot hold an institutional contract. Generator or solar hybrid — decided once, for both crafts.

  1. The anchor contract, won before the first bench is built. Without it you are building

inventory against hope.

  1. The standards written down — kiln-dried timber exclusively; verified foam and fabric; and a job

number on every order capturing labour hours, materials, waste, delivery, installation, rework and warranty.

  1. The growth mechanism. ← This is the gap. See §6.1.

3.3 The eight quarters

Quarter 1 — Decide and secure. Fix the growth mechanism (§6.1) — nothing else can be planned until it is. Register the domains (§4.7). Secure the workshop space. Get three equipment quotations. Start the anchor-contract conversations with the Anambra State Universal Basic Education Board and two private hotels in Awka or Onitsha. Gate: a signed lease or a written option, and a letter of intent from at least one institutional buyer.

Quarter 2 — Equip and hire. Install power. Buy machines against the quotations. Hire or appoint the workshop lead — the person who will actually run the floor, on a written role, not a family member by default. Build the first sample set: one classroom desk-and-bench, one upholstered chair, one mattress, one curtain run. Cost every sample by hand. Gate: real cost per piece, known to the naira, against a real quoted price.

Quarter 3 — First paid order. Deliver the anchor contract's first tranche. On time, or find out why not while the order is small. Record everything: hours, wastage, rework, delivery, what the buyer complained about. Gate: one paid order delivered and accepted, with actual contribution positive after variable costs.

Quarter 4 — Second and third orders. Take two more orders, at least one in the other craft, so both floors are earning. Write the sales process down — how a lead becomes a quote becomes an order becomes cash. Gate: repeat demand, not a one-off. Contribution still positive.

Year 2, Quarters 5–6 — Repeatability. Four or more orders, at least one repeat customer. Fix the two worst sources of rework. Set a monthly break-even figure that includes overhead, management time, tax, warranty and a bad-debt allowance. Gate: two consecutive months at or above break-even under a downside case.

Year 2, Quarters 7–8 — Decide the next unit. Only now: whether to add capacity, a second site, or the supporting functions — materials and timber supply, logistics and delivery, training and quality. Not before. Each is a separate investment decision with its own case. Gate: a written capacity bottleneck, and cash to fund the downside.

3.4 What must NOT happen in these two years

  • No university, polytechnic, college, hospital or clinic. Not even land.
  • No Akuzo construction. Feasibility and title work only (§4.4).
  • No ten sectors. No five child groups. No offshore trust.
  • No large land acquisition. The master plan's ₦17.75bn over thirty years is a destination.
  • No bank borrowing against forecasts. There is no group P&L, no balance sheet, no cash-flow

statement anywhere in the library.

  • No hiring ahead of the work.

3.5 The second thing to build, if the first works

Ozi Ikoro's museum is the only venture with a complete plan and a registered company — and it cannot proceed until somebody costs it. The plan has no capital budget at all. The first task is not to find a warehouse; it is to produce a number for the conversion, the fit-out, the initial collection and the working capital, and a break-even.

And two decisions have to be made first (§6.2): Awka or Nkpor, and foundation or limited company. The plan says Awka; every other venture is at Nkpor, 40 km away. The plan signs itself "Ozi Ikoro Foundation" and Year 3 proposes moving to foundation status — while the entity that exists is a limited company.

3.6 The buildings

The Akuzo two-building programme is good work and it is premature. It is fully costed, the off-grid design is coherent, and the fibre is designed in from phase 2 — which is the right way round. But it is US$1.97m, the arithmetic does not close, and it depends on land you have not secured.

PLAN. Two years of land, title, planning and community work. No groundbreaking. And one sequencing fact to protect: the server specification is a foundation-stage input. If Building 1 is ever poured without it, the server room becomes a retrofit, and the retrofit is the expensive version of a decision you can make once, cheaply, now.

PART 4 — EVERYTHING ELSE, IN TWO YEARS

4.1 Governance — adopt little, in writing

PLAN. Within two years, adopt one short document: a decision-rights note covering who may commit money, who may hire, who may sign, which matters need both founders, and how a disagreement is resolved. Two pages. Signed and dated.

Do not adopt the full Charter, the nine-step Family Court, the five institutions, or the horological succession rules in this window. They are worth having eventually; they are worth nothing before there is anything to govern — and the review is right that "a family forum should not direct day-to-day business operations" unless the business's own documents say it may.

Do separate the three records from day one: family decisions, business decisions, and community decisions. One disagreement should not freeze all three.

4.2 Money — the waterfall, and one number

Order of priority, and nothing below the line gets funded until everything above it is met:

  1. Payroll, tax, insurance.
  2. Debt service and contractual obligations.
  3. Safe operations, maintenance, approved working capital.
  4. A cash reserve — target six to twelve months of essential fixed costs. Choose the number, write

it down, and do not spend through it.

  1. Approved pilots with defined limits and stop-loss rules.
  2. Everything else.

Controls that cost nothing and prevent the worst: separate bank accounts per business; dual authorisation above a stated threshold; a 13-week cash forecast for the workshop; a job number on every order; and no family member guaranteeing company debt without independent legal advice.

4.3 Technology — stage it, and test the restore

FACT. The tech independence guide is 165,000 characters and specifies a four-box server stack, a camera VLAN with no internet, and a five-generation hardware roadmap.

PLAN. Ignore the hardware roadmap for two years. Do only this, in order:

  1. Password manager and multi-factor authentication on every business and family account.
  2. Encrypted off-site backup, with a restore actually tested — not a backup reported as

successful. A backup you have never restored is a hope.

  1. Named owners: one for maintenance, one for backups. No service depends on undocumented

knowledge in one person's head.

  1. Separate accounts, least privilege. A family archive does not mean every family member sees

every file.

  1. Then add services, one at a time, each with a maintainer, an update schedule and a retirement

plan.

On children's devices: no covert surveillance, no always-on location tracking, no family-wide visibility into a child's messages. Explain settings in age-appropriate language, use the least intrusive measure that addresses a specific risk, and give the child a route to raise discomfort.

The server programmeA line in Building 1's foundation design. No hardware
The museumA capital budget, a decision on location and legal form, and an option agreement if one is free

4.5 The hotspot — resolve, then order

PLAN. Do not place the 20-unit order yet. First:

  1. Resolve the RFQ conflicts — ports, SIM, client count, enclosure, UWB, NFC. One controlled

specification, options marked separately.

  1. Get a quotation and a prototype from a qualified supplier, with security documentation and

radio/product-compliance evidence.

  1. Decide the UWB question. "No GPS" does not mean a device cannot infer location. UWB can

support precise proximity and location functions.

  1. No names engraved. See §2.6.

4.6 The watches — inventory only

PLAN. In two years: inventory them, confirm identity and provenance, obtain independent appraisals, and review the insurance. Do not borrow against them. The loan terms have a solvency problem the review identifies precisely: a US$65,000 minimum loan at 65% LTV requires appraised collateral of at least US$100,000. And fixed-income yield may not cover interest, fees, tax and liquidity cost. Pledging a family heirloom to buy bonds is not wealth creation until the arithmetic says it is.

Also settle one contradiction: the charter refers throughout to "the ten watches" and names five.

PLAN. Register in the next two years, in this order. All verified available:

Skip ezeme.io and ezeme.co. Do not point the branch domains anywhere — a TLS certificate is published the moment it is issued, so even a holding page publishes a name that must stay private.

Blocked: Namecheap's API whitelists 102.90.124.177 while the actual egress is 102.90.125.55. Add the second address, or drop the restriction and rely on the scoped API key.

PART 6 — DECISIONS I NEED FROM YOU

6.1 The one that blocks everything else

What replaces Igba Odibo as the way the furniture business grows?

The model is scrapped and nothing states what comes in its place. The realistic options:

  • Directly-owned branches. The group hires managers and owns 100% of each new unit. Simplest,

cleanest, slowest, and it needs capital each time.

  • A capped earn-in. The review's proposal: an operating partner earns 10–20% over a defined

vesting period against real performance criteria, rather than receiving 50% on day one. It is lawful, it is motivating, and it avoids the deadlock a nominal 50/50 creates.

  • Franchise or licence. The group owns the brand, the supply chain and the standards; partners

own their units. Fastest to scale, hardest to control quality on the thing — kiln-dried timber — that is the whole differentiator.

  • Hired management with profit share. No equity changes hands; incentives are annual.

My recommendation: the capped earn-in, with a shareholder agreement that covers decision rights, reserved matters, distributions, leaver terms, valuation and deadlock. It keeps the compounding intent of Igba Odibo without the two things that would break it — an unclear ownership cheaply given, and a 50/50 deadlock.

6.2 The museum

  • Awka or Nkpor? The plan says Awka; everything else is at Nkpor. My recommendation: Nkpor,

unless the Awka warehouse is free or nearly so — a museum needs footfall, and the group's footfall will be in Nkpor.

  • Foundation or limited company? My recommendation: stay a limited company for now. A

foundation cannot easily trade, and the plan's revenue model is 40% art sales. Convert when the endowment exists.

  • What will it cost? Unknown. This is the first deliverable for the museum — nobody should

commit to a warehouse before that number exists.

6.3 The children

  • When is child one expected? Every roadmap row resolves from one date — the birth year. Until I

have it, the roadmaps stay in plan years. Tell me the year and every table becomes ages.

  • Are the five names fixed? They are in the documents and in the portal. If they are not settled,

the private material should say so, because it currently reads as decided.

6.4 Still open from before

  • The goal text names a "public five-branch presence (Isiome, Akunnia, Idenze, Uli, Udeze)" —

which you overruled and which uses the old name.

  • Cloudflare Access needs you to click Enable.
  • Namecheap's IP whitelist blocks every domain purchase.

PART 7 — WHERE I DIFFER FROM THE REVIEW

The review is careful and mostly right. Four places where I would go further, and one where I would not.

1. It under-weights what already exists. It treats the corpus as a set of proposals, and it is right that most of it is unbuilt. But something is built: a registered company, three live websites, a gated plan portal, and one complete business plan. The plan should start from that, not from zero.

2. It is silent on the two arithmetic failures. The $1.85M against $1,966,000, and the ₦1.23bn against ₦2.67bn. A review that flags optimism everywhere else should flag those, because they are the numbers somebody would actually sign.

3. It does not say what to do first. Fifty recommendations, no sequence. The sequence is: fix the growth mechanism, then build one workshop, then prove it twice, and only then discuss anything else.

4. It treats the education plan as over-specified — and it is right, but it stops short. The documents not only over-specify; they assign careers at birth. The correction is not "make the schedule lighter." It is "own nothing in the child's name and require nothing of him."

Where I would not go as far as the review: on the offshore structure. It recommends deferring a Mauritius trust entirely. I would say the same for implementation — but the capital-source rule is worth adopting now, in whatever form is lawful, because its whole purpose is to prevent informal personal claims forming over the next two years, and after two years of informal contributions it is much harder to unwind. Adopt the rule. Defer the structure.

WHAT EZEME IS

A reading of the family's own source documents — the 18 Google Drive files — as distinct from the 60-plan library that was built from them.

Written 9 October 2026. Every claim below is drawn from the Drive source at ~/Projects/Ezeme/.research/gdocs/text/; the files are named so each can be checked. Where a source contradicts another, both are shown rather than averaged.

0. The correction this document exists to make

I had built the public site around Ozikoro, treating it as the front of the enterprise. That was wrong. Ozikoro is one subsidiary among several, and it is not what is being built.

What is actually being built, in the founder's own words (Ezeme_Group_Master_Plan.txt):

"The Ezeme Group begins with two workshops and a farm. From those three assets — operating on a single structural principle, that value compounds when equity is shared honestly and land is held strategically — everything described in this plan follows."

"The three cash engines that fund this entire system are the Ezeme Soft Furnishings & Upholstery Cluster, the Ezeme Furniture Cluster, and the Ezeme Agriculture operation — all built on the Igba Odibo equity model, generating compounding income that is directed entirely into the Group's land acquisition and development fund."

That is the enterprise. The furniture and soft furnishings cluster is not a side business — it is the engine that funds everything else.

UPDATE — the Igba Odibo equity model has been scrapped. The founder's instruction: "igba odibo must be scrapped as it was not needed anymore." Everything in this document about settling apprentices into 50% ownership, the equity cascade and the compounding-branch structure is therefore historical, not operative. Read §2 below as a record of a model that was designed and then set aside — not as the plan. The furniture and soft furnishings business itself stands, and is now the group's public-facing manufacturing business; what replaces Igba Odibo as its growth mechanism is not written down anywhere yet, and is flagged as such in §8 and §10.

1. The three documents that describe three different things

The Drive corpus contains three plans at three different scales. They are not the same plan, and the sources do not reconcile them. All three are the founder's.

Document What it is Horizon
Ezeme_Group_Master_Plan.txtThe enterprise. "Five Children. Ten Sectors. One Empire. 2025–2055." A family conglomerate anchored in Nkpor, plus a city-scale land play30 years
Nkpor_Ezeme_Furniture_and_Soft_Furnishings_Apprenticeship_Model.txtThe near-term business. One anchor workshop, two crafts, expanded through apprentice equityCycles of 6 years, out to year 25
Ezeme_11-Year_Plan-1.txtA separate, single-founder company in São Paulo — smart mirrors for salons. "Age 29–40. Eleven Years to Build One Company That Works"11 years

The third is not the Nkpor group. It is a Brazilian smart-interiors company built by the founder personally, using the same name. Anyone reading the corpus should hold them apart.

2. The engine (SCRAPPED): the Igba Odibo equity model

This section is retained as a record only. The model was scrapped by the founder — "igba odibo must be scrapped as it was not needed anymore." Nothing below is operative. What replaces it as the furniture business's growth mechanism is not yet written.

This was designed as the load-bearing idea of the whole enterprise, a deliberate departure from the traditional Igbo apprenticeship.

Traditional: a master settles an apprentice with a lump-sum cash payout and a clean break. The apprentice leaves with nothing but cash and starts from nothing. Value disperses outward.

Ezeme: when an apprentice completes training, the group opens a new branch and gives the apprentice 50% documented equity in it. The apprentice becomes managing director and co-owner. The group keeps 50%, plus the brand, the supply chain, bulk purchasing, institutional contracts, and the reporting structure.

"They are not your employee anymore. They are your partner. But the group retains the network, the brand, the supply chain, and the strategic direction."

"The cluster does not scatter. It compounds."

The equity cascade. Because each branch repeats the model, the founder's stake multiplies without fresh capital: own 50% of Branch 1, Branch 1 gives its apprentice 50% of Branch 1-B, and the founder holds an effective 25% of Branch 1-B through Branch 1. Across a network, the equity footprint grows faster than the capital deployed.

The condition that makes it work, stated as the second of five pillars: "the settled apprentice must genuinely receive 50% equity — not a promise, not a verbal agreement, but a documented ownership structure. If that trust breaks, the chain breaks."

The founding twist. The first five apprentices settled do not all open furniture workshops. Each is settled into a different critical sector, so the group is structurally complete by the end of Cycle One:

  1. Furniture Production
  2. Soft Furnishings & Upholstery
  3. Materials & Timber Supply
  4. Logistics & Delivery
  5. Training & Quality

Branch 3 existing from the founding cycle means every later workshop starts with a working supply chain already in place, rather than waiting for one to emerge.

3. The anchor workshop — Year Zero

One workshop in Nkpor, two crafts under one roof. Furniture builds the frame; soft furnishings finish it. Run together so an institutional buyer can order a complete fit-out from one contract.

"Most competitors sell furniture or furnishings. The group sells a finished room."

Year Zero actions, in the source's order: secure land or workshop space in Nkpor large enough for a woodworking floor and a soft furnishings floor side by side; equip both sides; solve power independently first (generator or solar hybrid — woodworking is the heavier load and must be solved once, for both crafts); win the anchor contract; take in the first cohort of 10–15 apprentices; set quality standards from day one.

Anchor contracts: school furniture (paired with classroom and dormitory soft furnishings); office furniture (with upholstered seating and window treatments); hospital and clinic furniture (with bedding, curtains, screens); hotel and hospitality fit-outs.

The quality differentiator is kiln-dried timber — "the single biggest cause of furniture failure in Nigerian workshops" — plus verified foam and fabric. Institutions will pay more for what lasts.

Growth cycles, with the source's own numbers:

Cycle Years Units Employment Milestones
Year Zero—1 anchor10–15 apprenticesBoth crafts, one roof, power solved
One1–61 anchor + 5 branches—400–600 pieces/month; 2–3 institutional clients on repeat
Two7–1220–30 units3,000–5,000First exports to Ghana and Cameroon via the Onitsha network
Three13–1865–90 units16,000–26,0006–8 training subsidiaries, 300–500 certified apprentices/year
Four19–25150+ workshops35,000–65,000 direct + 40,000–80,000 indirectExport across Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire, Cameroon, Togo, Gabon

Sourcing: timber from Niger Delta hardwoods and Cross River/Ondo plantations via Onitsha merchants; MDF and plywood imported through Apapa; foam, fabric and thread through Onitsha. Branch 3 internalises a timber yard and drying kiln, a hardware and fittings depot, a finishing supplies depot, and a foam-and-fabric depot.

The five pillars: Power · the 50% commitment · material quality · institutional contracts first, retail second · export orientation.

4. Land, Akuzo, and the city

The furniture clusters are not the destination — they are the funding mechanism for land. Master Plan: "generating compounding income that is directed entirely into the Group's land acquisition and development fund."

Land bank: ≈₦17.75bn over thirty years, about ₦590m a year on average. Zones and per-plot prices: A Industrial ₦25–70m · B Institutional ₦40–80m · C Corporate ₦70–120m · D Residential ₦25–100m · Idemmili ₦5–20m. Named lines include the university (100 ha / 167 plots, ₦8,350m), the polytechnic (20 ha / 33 plots, ₦1,650m), agriculture (100+ ha, ₦600m), staff estates (30 plots, ₦1,500m) and the storey-building portfolio (27 buildings, ₦1,230m).

"Once both production clusters reach Cycle Two in Year Seven, combined subsidiary equity income alone exceeds this annual requirement."

Akuzo Urban Transformation — three zones, developed as a district rather than an estate. Explicitly not gated: the reference is the Xingchen production cluster in China — "No compound walls. No perimeter fence." Named components: the underground water spine (water, sewage, stormwater and electrical conduit in one trench); four community fisheries (grey mullet and catfish, described as permanent non-profit community infrastructure); a community park, civic centre and two mini football fields; a 16-camera security model; a street standard (tarmac ≥6 m, footpath ≥1.2 m, solar poles every 25 m, verge trees every 10 m, setback ≥3 m); and the Akuzo Development Council with a Community Development Fund (5% of every land transaction reserved for legal due diligence).

The Akuzo Residential District: 216–324 apartments over 30 years, buildings of four to six floors, one elevator each. And "The real estate strategy is never framed as acquisition. It is framed as development… This is true. That truth does the persuasion."

Stated risks, in the source's own words: "No verbal agreements. No informal purchases at any stage." · "The Group does not acquire land by displacing families." · "Ezeme is a city development partner, not a competitor to government." · "Land is a natural naira hedge."

5. The ten sectors, and the children they are named for

Two sectors per child, paired so each is deep rather than broad. From the Master Plan and the Corporate Architecture:

Child Domain Stated role
IsiomeAgriculture & Food Systems · Manufacturing & Industrial ProductionPatriarch; "strategic voice as first son"
AkunniaFinance & Investment Systems · Governance, Law & SecurityMatriarch; Chief Investment Officer; "the structural backbone"
IdenzeEducation & Human Capital · Healthcare & PharmaceuticalsSenior Male Heir
UliMedia & Information Systems · Transport & LogisticsSenior Female Heir; "including Brazil operations"
OkoduEnergy & Utilities · Construction & Real EstateThird Son

These children are unborn. Their names exist only in the family's own documents. Nothing in this document may be published.

The Interdependence Rule: "No division is self-sufficient and none is meant to be… That vulnerability is intentional."

6. The family constitution — how it is held

Five layers (House_of_Ezeme_Corporate_Architecture-2.txt, August 2026, marked "CONFIDENTIAL — FAMILY & COUNSEL USE ONLY"):

L1  House of Ezeme                 the family institution — unincorporated constitution
L2  Ezeme Family Trust (Mauritius) 99-year discretionary trust, Trusts Act 2001
      + Family Holdings PTC Ltd    the trustee
L3  Ezeme Family Holdings (Mauritius) Ltd   GBC — owns the Nigerian parent
L4  Ezeme Group Nigeria Ltd        CAMA parent — the mother company
L5  Isiome · Akunnia · Idenze · Uli · Okodu   the five child groups
      → operating companies

"Every company created with Ezeme Group capital — including companies established at birth for future heirs — remains a permanent, indivisible asset of the Ezeme family, regardless of whether the designated heir remains active, engaged, or even alive."

It names the three problems it exists to solve: ownership drift, operational capture without accountability, disengagement. Only three things sit offshore — the trust, the trustee company, and the GBC. Operating companies, employment, tax residency, land title and daily governance stay in Nigeria.

The capital-source rule, to be adopted verbatim into the Charter and the trust deed: capital from the group applied to any business "creates an asset of Ezeme Group and is held as a controlled subsidiary" unless the board resolves otherwise in writing at the time — and "No informal understanding, family custom, or subsequent conduct may be relied upon to establish personal ownership contrary to this rule."

The most important distinction in the whole design: "Beneficial ownership is fixed by the Trust and cannot be revoked for non-performance", but operational control is granted, not inherited. A non-engagement trigger (24–36 months) moves control to the board, which appoints a steward. "The disengaged heir keeps their economic entitlement in full. Nothing is confiscated. Control, not ownership, is what moves."

Succession rule: "Domain activation at Master's level. No child assumes leadership of their domain before completing their first Master's degree." Until then, professional managers run the businesses.

Institutions: Family Assembly (monthly, sovereign) · Family Council (weekly, "a cabinet rather than a court") · Family Court (nine steps: Petition → Notice → Hearing → Evidence → Questions → Defence → Deliberation → Judgment → Restoration) · Family Business Board (monthly) · Family Treasury · Secretariat & Archive. The firewall: "The Court does not decide business questions. The Board does not adjudicate personal grievances." Voting is equal from the moment of admission — "There is no partial or graduated vote." Membership is not employment.

7. The Jewellery Bank and the watches

Ezeme-Horological-Succession-Charter.txt — "A Covenant of Watches, Offices and Inheritance."

Five watches, bound to offices rather than persons, each above $100,000 and chosen from houses that have survived generations: a Patek Philippe Nautilus 5726/1A for the Patriarch ($130–180k) · an Audemars Piguet Royal Oak Jumbo 15202OR for the Matriarch ($110–180k) · an A. Lange & Söhne Datograph Perpetual for the Senior Male Heir ($130–175k) · a Vacheron Constantin Overseas Perpetual Calendar for the Senior Female Heir ($120–180k) · a Patek Philippe 5270G for the Third Son ($150–260k).

"The Nautilus belongs to the office of Patriarch and not to the person who holds it."

Sale outside the bloodline is absolutely prohibited — "This prohibition is absolute and permanent." The single permitted transaction creates a real business:

The Ezeme Jewellery Bank — "a business owned and operated within the Ezeme Group." An heir may pledge their watch rather than sell it. Loan capped at 65% of appraised value, ordinarily not below $65,000, interest at an annually approved ceiling. The decisive rule: "the entire loan amount disbursed… must be placed into income-generating fixed-interest instruments within fourteen days" — FGN bonds, Treasury bills, savings bonds, sovereign Eurobonds. No portion may be spent on consumption, business, property or anything else.

"the watch is not being sold. It is being put to work… No heir of this House should ever feel compelled to sell what their parent left them."

This is a real lending operation with a written credit policy, vault custody, receipts and quarterly statements — and it is not in the 60-plan library.

8. The Brazil plan

Ezeme_11-Year_Plan-1.txt — a different company, in a different country, built by the founder personally between ages 29 and 40.

"You have 11 years, not unlimited time and money. Your goal should not be 'launch across Latin America, the USA, and EU.' Your goal is to build one company that works in one city, then one country, then one additional market."

The product is a smart salon mirror — a 700×500×80 mm mirror with a 10" display, Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4, LED at CRI ≥90 — sold with installation, the Ezeme Home app, Ezeme Space turnkey fit-out, and Ezeme Care after-sales (R$150/month standard, R$250 premium).

Concrete economics: prototype budget R$25,000–40,000 over ~6 months; bill of materials R$5,400; target price R$8,500–12,000 per station; 35–45% gross margin on pilots, rising to 43–55% by year three; overhead R$4,800/month; break-even 1.5 premium units a month. Pilots in Brazil, then one Latin American city, then one US city. Certification: ANATEL, INMETRO, LGPD.

Discipline stated plainly: "Do not count an unproven business valuation as wealth. Real wealth is cash flow, investments, assets you control." · "Add a product only when it shares at least 70% of the same supply chain… or target customer." · "Keep personal money and business money separate."

8b. The hardware and technology programme

Ezeme_Family_Tech_Independence_Guide.txt (165,000 characters, 15 sections) is not a business plan. It is a buy-and-build programme for the family's own infrastructure — and it contains a real product roadmap.

The household stack first. Linux on every desktop (Fedora, Linux Mint); GrapheneOS on Pixel phones; Framework and System76 laptops; a four-box server stack — a Protectli/N100 firewall, a Minisforum MS-01 application server, a failover box with off-site backup, and a Threadripper Pro tower with 256 GB ECC and an RTX 5090 — running Tailscale, Authentik, Nextcloud, Immich, Vaultwarden, Home Assistant, Jellyfin, Paperless, Ollama, and a camera VLAN with no internet access.

Then the products. The guide specifies five generations of hardware under an Ezeme Hardware Platform, to be built and sold: Gen 1 — an Ezeme Family Media Frame (IPS display, custom PCB, CNC walnut or oak, secure element), with a pilot of ten units and then production batches of 50–100; Gen 2 — the smart mirror, kitchen display, voice assistant; Gen 3 — family tablet, children's learning tablet, notice board; Gen 4 — network gateway, backup appliance, solar and farm monitoring gateways; Gen 5 — AI devices and vehicle displays. Manufacturing is specified as PCB fabrication in Nigeria or internationally, CNC machining and cabinet making within Nigeria, laser cutting by Nigerian manufacturers, with possible local final assembly.

Ezeme OS and the companion apps (Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Linux, web) sit underneath, with commercial extensions sketched: Ezeme Cloud and an Ezeme Enterprise Server for "businesses, schools, churches, hotels, hospitals, museums, government organisations."

A drone programme for agriculture is specified as "an aviation department, not a gadget purchase" — Pixhawk-class flight controllers, RTK to 1–2 cm, a Jetson Orin Nano, and OpenDroneMap. A local voice assistant built on Whisper, Piper and Ollama, with a staged Igbo plan tied to the dialect dictionary already under way through Ozikoro.

The one thing here that is genuinely under way

Ezeme_Family_Secure_Hotspot_Device.txt (July 2026) is a real, near-term import: 20 units from a Shenzhen-area ODM. A keychain-fob personal hotspot, ~62×42×20 mm, IP68, with GPS and Bluetooth deliberately excluded and UWB, NFC, an e-ink display and dual active eSIM added. No custom moulds, to avoid "over $15,000 in upfront tooling costs". CE and NCC certification. The allocation is seven family members × two engraved units each, plus six spares branded "Ezeme" — a sourcing plan with a stated sequence: sourcing 4–8 weeks, sampling 3–4, revision, production 3–4, deployment.

It contains an internal contradiction worth resolving before the RFQ is sent: the specification says one USB-C port, no SIM tray, and 2–3 simultaneous clients; the ready-to-send RFQ asks for two USB-C ports, a dual physical nano-SIM tray (up to four profiles) and 10–15 simultaneous clients.

The education track underneath all of it

Ezeme_Sao_Paulo_Course_Map.txt is a relocation and enrolment plan for one person in São Paulo: the free municipal Fab Lab Livre SP network for CNC, laser and PCB milling; SENAI Brás's 80-hour fitted-kitchen cabinetry course and the CTT Escola de Marcenaria; four SENAI-SP técnicos of roughly 1,200 hours each (electronics, electrotechnics, mechatronics, networks); and SENAC alternatives — sequenced across months 1–12 and beyond.

Ezeme_Family_Vibe-coding_Structure.txt is filed as "Holding Structure — Part Four", and makes vibe coding a mandatory baseline skill for all five children from age ten, with one reviewed project a year and a pre-university project reviewed by the Family Council. Each child's project is sector-specific — a farm-to-factory dashboard, a live investment dashboard for the holding company, a student health tracker, a media-and-logistics dashboard, and a GIS development tracker for Akuzo.

Two documents are referenced but missing from the corpus: the Course Map is written as a companion to "The Founder's Hardware & AI Curriculum" and cites "the Reference Unit". Neither is among the 16 files.

8c. Akuzo — three documents, three layers of one programme

I had these three filed as unidentified. They are the most concrete engineering in the whole corpus: a 30-year strategy, the first two buildings costed line by line, and the digital infrastructure designed into them.

Document Date What it is
Akuzo Urban Transformation Plan v3.txtJune 2026The 30-year strategy, 2025–2055. Thirteen parts. Written to be shown to residents and the Development Council
Akuzo Dual Server Specification-1.txtJuly 2026Procurement-grade specification for two independent server facilities in the Akuzo compound
Akuzo Development Programme-1.txtAugust 2026The first two buildings, costed phase by phase — "A Home, and a Repeatable Commercial Model"

The two buildings

Building 1 — "Akuzo Residence": the family's own home. Five storeys, fourteen units — a 1-bedroom at the core, a 2-bedroom in the left wing and a 3-bedroom in the right wing on each of floors 1–4, plus two 4-bedroom penthouses on floor 5. US$967,000.

Building 2 — "Akuzo Court": the same envelope, commercial, for sale. The penthouse consolidation removed, so every floor carries the identical mix — "a uniform maximum of three bedrooms anywhere in the building" — fifteen units. US$999,000.

Both are costed across seven phases: land (2–3 plots, $40,000) · soil, clearing, access road and a reinforced raft foundation, no piling required on inland soil ($45,000) · drawings and Anambra State Physical Planning approvals ($20,000) · structural frame, slabs, blockwork and roofing at about 2,000 m² ($150,000) · a VVVF passenger elevator, five stops ($25,000) · services · fit-out · professional site supervision at an above-market retainer ($45,000) · contingency.

The services package is entirely off-grid: a 60 kW solar array with a three-phase hybrid inverter bank (~45 kW continuous, 65–70 kW surge) at $68,000; a 250 kWh LiFePO4 battery at $38,000; an underground biodigester with an H₂S scrubber and a 10–15 kVA dual-fuel backup generator at $55,000; a central LPG grid with smart gas meters at $18,000; and a 100,000-litre underground cistern with sand, carbon and UV filtration at $55,000. The sizing basis is stated: ~10 kWh/day per standard unit, ~16 for a penthouse, ~55–60 kWh/day of building systems, giving ~213 kWh/day per building, with the elevator's starting surge — not the battery — driving inverter sizing.

In-building fibre is designed in from the start — conduit and riser designed at phase 2, embedded at phase 3 sharing the elevator and service core path, active GPON at phase 6 — with a GPON OLT head-end and an ONT per unit. Bandwidth initially wholesale from a local Anambra ISP; the passive network later leasable to open-access operators. The document concludes that "forming a dedicated, NCC-licensed ISP subsidiary is not warranted at the scale of one or two buildings."

The commercial model: the company retains one full floor — "recommended default: retain the ground floor" — and sells the other twelve units, then "applies the proceeds of Building 2's unit sales to fund a third replication." Labour is directly employed from the Nkpor and Onitsha corridor on the company's own payroll, "rather than through a labour agency", with one COREN/ARCON-registered engineer or architect retained full-time. This is a repeatable building business, not a one-off house.

The servers

Akuzo Dual Server Specification describes two physically and logically independent facilities on the compound — "zero shared cabling, switches, or credentials."

The Ezeme Family Server, underground beneath Building 1, serving the household and nothing else, in five VLAN-isolated tiers: an OPNsense firewall and 100G-capable aggregation switching; a Dell R760xd2 core with 24 × 20 TB drives → ~380 TB usable in ZFS RAID-Z2; a Supermicro 4U compute node with two RTX 5090s; a fanless vault with TPM; and a 60-bay Storinator with 1.2 PB raw → ~900–960 TB usable for backup, with only the vault replicated off-site. The room is tanked and sump-protected, on a raised floor, with aspirating smoke detection wired to automatic power cutoff.

The Akuzo Building Management Server, ground level between the two buildings, is a standalone revenue-generating platform: three Proxmox nodes in HA, two more 60-bay Storinators (2.4 PB raw), a Dell L4 transcode pair, Odoo for billing on mobile money and bank transfer, HA firewall pairs, and a capped, view-only Jellyfin library billed to the 100+ extended-family and cousin households resident across Akuzo. CCTV covers the lobby, courtyard and elevator lobby — "never unit interiors."

Combined: ~3.65 TB of RAM and ~3.4–3.6 PB of storage, with Tier 1 and Tier 4 bays left unpopulated "reserved for the five children's data growth over the next decade."

The specification ends with a sequencing instruction that is easy to miss and expensive to ignore: it must reach the site supervisor before groundbreaking, so the server room's floor loading, tanking and dual power and fibre entries are designed into Building 1's foundation rather than retrofitted.

The community layer

The v3 plan sets the standard the buildings must meet: a 6 m tarmac carriageway, kerbed concrete footpaths of 1.2 m each side, solar lighting every 25 m with CCTV at every intersection, verge trees every 10 m, a minimum 3 m setback, and covered precast drainage with trash-filter baskets every 40–50 m.

Its centrepiece is a single underground service corridor running the length of the main road — "one trench carries four systems at different depths: clean water supply, sewage collector, stormwater drain, and electrical conduit. Dug once, maintained permanently." A Mexican tunnelling engineer takes up residency in Year 1 to train local youth in microtunnelling and pipe-jacking, after which "the community is fully self-sufficient."

Community infrastructure is budgeted as non-revenue, ₦549.9m in total: four fisheries ponds at 30 m × 15 m for grey mullet and catfish ("not an Ezeme Group revenue line", surplus reinvested), the civic centre refurbishment, the village square becoming a community park, two mini football fields, and a security package of 16 cameras, 20 solar poles and a three-man two-shift night patrol.

The framing rule, in the author's own words: never "I want to develop Akuzo" but "Akuzo should become the cleanest, safest, and most prosperous community in Nkpor" — and "The real estate strategy must never be framed as acquisition."

Reconciliation problems across the three, recorded not resolved: v3 prices a storey building at ₦35–50m, while the Programme's own two-building bill of quantities sums to US$1,966,000 — roughly ₦2.67bn at v3's own ₦1,360 rate, against v3's assumption of 27 buildings for ₦1.23bn. The Programme's §7 says "the full combined $1.85M exposure" while its line items sum to $1,966,000. And v3's cost model has no line for the $234,000 per building of standalone solar, battery, biodigester, cistern and LPG that the Programme adds on top of the mains-plus-inverter standard v3 specifies.

8d. Ozi Ikoro — the venture with a plan of its own

The Drive was re-inventoried directly and holds 18 documents, not 16. Two were missing from the corpus, and one of them is the business plan for the company that actually exists.

OZI IKORO: MASTER BUSINESS PLAN — "A Hybrid Museum, Art Gallery, and Anthropological Research Hub", in a converted warehouse in Awka, Anambra State. The name is the purpose: Ozi Ikoro, "Message of the Drum".

Three wings. The Artefacts ("Footprints in Red Earth") — 30–40 historical objects at a time, rotated quarterly, dark walls and single-object spotlights, silence. The Art ("The Future of Form") — a commercial contemporary gallery with white mobile panels on industrial tracks. The Mixed ("Drawing and Object") — 19th-century sketches hung beside the tools they depict, so the visitor sees how Igbo life was drawn and what it was drawn with.

Around them: an anthropology library and archive; a digital theatre of 8 × 10 m with a 12-screen decoder wall in a 3 × 4 grid plus individual viewing stations drawing on Colonial Film Unit footage and NTA archives; a glass-walled conservation laboratory the public watches through, with wet preservation in 70% ethanol; and a store and café. Spaces are separated by suspended Akwete and indigo textiles and mobile partitions rather than walls — "the building is not a container; it is a narrative."

Money: 40% gallery commission / 60% to the artist · admissions ₦1,500 adult, ₦500 student, free under-12, ₦3,500 family · membership ₦15,000 to ₦250,000 · gala tickets ₦50–100,000 with a ₦10–20m net target · price tiers from Mantlepiece at ₦50,000 to Monument at ₦10m+. Year-3 mix: art sales 40%, admissions 15%, store and café 15%, membership 10%, events 10%, consultancy 5%, grants 5%. Three phases — infrastructure, market presence, institutional authority.

The plan has no capital budget anywhere in it. It specifies a warehouse conversion down to the fume hood, the eyewash station and the pH strips, and asserts "lower capital costs" as an advantage — but never states what the conversion, fit-out, initial collection or working capital cost, and gives no break-even. Every other number in the plan is stated; the building is not. And it is in Awka, not Nkpor. The family base, the furniture clusters, both Akuzo buildings and the 30-year master plan all sit at Nkpor and Akuzo in Idemili North — a different city, some 40 km away. Either the museum is deliberately separate from the group's base, or one of the two locations is wrong. The legal form is inconsistent. The plan's own draft letter of intent is signed "Director, Ozi Ikoro Foundation", and Year 3 proposes a "transition to foundation status" — while the entity that exists is Ozi Ikoro Limited, RC 8955047. A foundation and a limited company are different instruments; the plan should say which this is.

The other newly-found document is personal rather than commercial — Idenze Food Timetable, a four-week household meal plan of Igbo dishes (ora, onugbu, egusi, ofe akwu, edikaikong, afang, okpa).

This reframes what Ozikoro is. It is not primarily a publishing imprint. It is a museum, gallery and research institution — and it is the only venture in the family's own documents that has a complete plan, a registered company, and a live web presence.

9. What already exists, versus what is written

Status
Ozikoro — Igbo and African history, archives, scholarshipLive. Published by Ozi Ikoro Limited, RC 8955047
Ozituma — free dictionary of African languagesLive
OmaPolo — clothingLive
Ozi Ikoro Limited — RC 8955047, incorporated 29 October 2025, Nkpor-AguRegistered
The furniture & soft furnishings clusterWritten, not begun
Ezeme AgricultureWritten, not begun
The land bank / AkuzoWritten, not begun
The family constitution and trustWritten, not adopted
Ezeme Jewellery BankWritten; no entity
The five child groupsPlanned for children who are not yet born

The source documents also name a family property at Pirin Golf & Country Club, Bansko, Bulgaria, and pre-university and university placements including Ide Technical College Nkpor, QRC Onitsha, DMGS Onitsha, Tsinghua, Wageningen, NTU, USP, NUS, Buckingham, LBS, Chicago Booth, HKU, Oxford, NIPER, Colorado, UvA, Heriot-Watt, NFTS, UCD and the Architectural Association.

10. What the website is for

Stated by the founder directly: "all I wanted was to be able to have a website I log into and see all my plans."

That is the requirement. Everything else is secondary.

  • ezeme.org — the public face of Ezeme the enterprise: what it is, the ten sectors in five

domains, the businesses that exist, and a dated record. No child is named.

  • family.ezeme.org — the plans, behind a login. Now holds the 60-plan library (73 documents), the

rendered roadmaps and capital documents, and the 16 Drive source documents — including the furniture model, the master plan, the 11-year plan and the governance charter.

The gap that remains, and it is the important one: the Drive sources describe businesses the 60-plan library does not contain — the furniture and soft-furnishings cluster, the Igba Odibo apprenticeship engine, the Akuzo programme, the land bank, the Jewellery Bank. The library is the destination; the sources are the actual plan. A portal that shows only the library shows the founder a version of his own enterprise he does not recognise.

11. Two contradictions in the sources, recorded rather than resolved

  1. The Raising Plan is not a fundraising plan. It is *"A Multigenerational Raising Plan: Language,

Character, Heritage & Dynasty."* No raise, target, investor or amount appears in it. I had assumed it concerned money.

  1. Languages. The Raising Plan lists five core languages including Hausa in one section, but

the Dynasty Principles state the baseline as "Igbo, English, French, Portuguese, and Spanish" — with no Hausa.

  1. Akunnia's first university is given as UNIZIK in the Raising Plan but NUS in the Holding

Structure.

  1. The Horological Charter refers to "the ten watches" throughout but names only five.

These are recorded so nobody builds on a number that the family has stated two ways.

AKUZO COST BASIS & TENDER SPECIFICATION

The measured cost basis for the Akuzo construction programme, and the specification the tender is run against.
Prepared forEzeme Group Board · Okodu Group Board · Akuzo Development Ltd
StatusCorrected basis. No plan in the library has been edited. Where this document contradicts a plan, the plan is wrong and is cited so it can be found.
PurposeTo replace the ₦35–50m per-building figure in plans/50_Akuzo_Development.md with one measured, tendered cost basis — and to specify the tender that produces it.
Engagement budgeted₦12m · day 60 — plans/59_Okodu_Housing.md:182, confirmed as the library's priority action by NUMBER_RECONCILIATION.md §8.4
FXNaira primary. Dollars indicative at ₦1,600/USD, the library standard (plans/README.md). Spot NFEM is ≈ ₦1,328/USD (September 2026), so the ₦1,600 rate is conservative — it understates naira cost and overstates dollar cost. Not comparable with the Group's own Akuzo document (₦1,360/USD, June 2025).
Price basisConstant Year-1 naira, Year 1 = 2027. All rates are planning rates unless marked otherwise.
Companionsplans/50_Akuzo_Development.md · plans/41_Okodu_Group.md · plans/45_Okodu_Construction.md · plans/46_Okodu_Materials.md · plans/42_Okodu_Power.md · plans/44_Okodu_Grid.md · plans/47_Okodu_Real_Estate.md · plans/59_Okodu_Housing.md · NUMBER_RECONCILIATION.md §2.4 and §8.4

0. Executive summary

The error. 50_Akuzo_Development.md:156–162 costs a five-storey, 2,000 m² building at ₦35–50m per building, totalling ₦1,230.0m for 27 buildings. Its own bill of quantities for the same building totals US$967,000–999,000 ≈ ₦1.55–1.60bn each (41_Okodu_Group.md:132; 50:174). That is a factor of 31–44×. ₦35m ÷ 2,000 m² = ₦17,500/m², which is six times below the cheapest published 2026 Nigerian construction rate (₦150,000/m², basic). The ₦35–50m range is the per-plot land rate, carried from the land budget (₦1.23bn ÷ 27 plots = ₦45.6m/plot) into the build column of the real-estate costing.

The correction. Three independent derivations of the credible figure already agree within 5%: the Group's own BoQ (₦1.55–1.60bn), a rate worked back from the budget envelope (₦750,000/m² → ₦1.48bn, 41:141), and an audit reconciliation against published market bands (NUMBER_RECONCILIATION.md §2.4).

The programme is viable, and the family's own plans already contain the specification that makes it so. 41_Okodu_Group.md:138 prescribes holding build cost to ₦650–850m per building by constraining gross area to 1,100–1,400 m² instead of 2,000 — "build fewer square metres, not cheaper ones." 50_Akuzo_Development.md:181 reaches the same figure by stripping five redundant utility items worth US$234,000 (₦374.4m), because Okodu Power and the water spine serve the district anyway.

What this document adds. A complete table of every construction rate in the library (Part 1), a first-principles elemental build-up for one building at both specifications that reconciles to the Group's own BoQ within 1.4% (Part 2), the tender specification (Part 3), the corrected capital requirement and its cascade (Part 4), and the ₦12m cost-book brief (Part 5).

The five numbers that matter

Two findings that were not previously in the library and that change the decision:

  1. The design fix moves 59_Okodu_Housing's yield test only from 2.7% gross / 2.2% net to 3.3% gross / 2.7% net. It improves the rental case and does not rescue it. At Akuzo specification the building is a build-to-sell product; the rental sleeve must stay on 59's own low-rise ₦350,000/m² specification. 59's existing conclusion is therefore reconfirmed, not overturned.
  2. 47_Okodu_Real_Estate.md:117 carries a second mis-carried figure of exactly the same species as the Akuzo error. Its "open-market turnkey equivalent ₦1.85bn" is explicitly a cost benchmark, and 47:131–133 then uses the derived ₦119m per unit as "market value." 50:190 prices the same units at ₦35.8–48.3m. The two are 2.5–3.3× apart, and the difference decides whether Akuzo's development margin is negative or 90%. This is not a cost-basis question and cannot be settled here — it is exactly what the three independent valuations at day 60 exist to settle. It is flagged, not corrected.

PART 1 — EVERY CONSTRUCTION RATE IN THE LIBRARY

1.1 Why this table is worth the document

NUMBER_RECONCILIATION.md §2 names cost per square metre as the worst-reconciled input in the library. Some of that spread is error, some is legitimate specification difference, and the difference has never been stated in one place. This is that place.

Rates are classified on one rule, adopted from EZEME_GROUP_OPERATING_ARCHITECTURE.md:491: state the specification with the rate. A rate with no specification is not a rate, it is a number.

PART 5 — THE BRIEF FOR THE COST BOOK ITSELF

The ₦12m engagement — scope for the quantity surveyor or cost consultant.

Precedent: 59_Okodu_Housing.md:182 — "Okodu Construction tender — one measured cost book. ₦12m · day 60." Confirmed as the library's priority action by NUMBER_RECONCILIATION.md §8.4 and §9 ("commission the Akuzo/Okodu cost book… a factor-of-30 error on the Group's flagship programme"), and as the board's first duty by 50:23.

5.1 The engagement, in one page
AppointmentOne independent quantity surveying practice, NIQS-registered, with a COREN-registered structural engineer engaged for the frame and substructure elements. The QS must not be the builder, must not be a Group company, and must not have an existing instruction from Okodu Construction or Okodu Materials. Independence is the deliverable.
Fee₦12m, fixed. For context this is 2.0% of the ₦600m design-fix build value and 0.94% of the ₦1.28bn original-spec value — inside the published Nigerian range for BOQ preparation of 0.75–1.5% of construction cost (Afrotools, 2026). The fee is not the issue; the scope is.
DeadlineDay 60. 50:320 sets the cost reconciliation at day 90 for the firm quotations; the measured cost book is due at day 60 (59:182) so that day 61–90 can be used to reconcile it against the three valuations (50:319, day 60) and the spine/power confirmations (50:323, day 60). A cost book delivered at day 90 misses the decision it exists to serve.
Deliverable 1A full priced Bill of Quantities for one standard Akuzo building, measured to BESMM4, at both areas (1,250 m² and 2,000 m²), in the Part 2 elemental format, priced by three independent bidders on a frozen specification.
Deliverable 2A measured elemental cost book — the Part 2 table, completed with actual rates, at both specifications and both areas, with the sensitivity drivers of Part 2.6 quantified at the Nkpor site.
Deliverable 3The rate benchmark — every element rate tested against, in order of preference: (a) two published Nigerian bench marks, (b) two Onitsha or Awka tender results for comparable work, (c) the NIQS Anambra chapter's current elemental cost index if one exists, (d) two supplier quotations. Every rate that cannot be tested is reported as untested, in a separate schedule.
Deliverable 4The benchmarking file (Part 3.5) — 14 related-party packages, each with internal price, two external prices, normalisation, the internal margin in ₦ and %.
Deliverable 5The dual-price schedule (Part 3.6) — market price and internal price per package, with the internal margin disclosed.
Deliverable 6The condition-precedent schedule (Part 3.7) — the five removed items, each with the written confirmation it depends on, its current status (confirmed / unconfirmed / refused), and the cost consequence of reinstatement (₦374.4m measured; ₦444.8m all-in per building).
Deliverable 7A reconciliation note stating, in the QS's own words, whether the corrected rate sits inside a defensible market band — and a list of every figure in the return that the QS could not source.
AuthorityThe QS reports to the Akuzo Development MD and the independent directors, not to the Development Manager who owns the Okodu Construction relationship, and not to Okodu Construction. 50:95 requires independent-director approval of each related-party package; this engagement is where that approval is first exercised.

5.3 The acceptance test

A cost book is accepted only if it satisfies all six tests. Failing any one returns it.

#TestPass condition
1It reconciles to a defensible market band.The resulting ₦/m² for the design-fix building sits inside ₦464,000–773,000/m² (41:138's own design-fix band) and inside ₦500,000–800,000/m² (the published higher-specification band, Afrotools). A rate outside both bands is returned, whatever its derivation.
2It reconciles to an ACTUAL PRICED BoQ.The rate is the quotient of a priced BoQ — three compliant bids against employer-taken quantities on a frozen specification — and not a derivation from a budget envelope. 41:141's ₦750,000/m² fails this test by construction: it was "worked backwards from the Group's own Akuzo budget envelope." The whole point of the ₦12m is to replace a derived rate with a measured one.
3🔴 IT DOES NOT RECONCILE TO THE GROUP'S EXISTING FIGURE — AND THAT IS NOT A FAILURE.The acceptance test must never be agreement with ₦35–50m, with ₦1.23bn, or with ₦750,000/m². Those three figures are precisely what is in question: the first is a land rate in a build column, the second is the same land budget counted twice, and the third is a derivation from the first. If the measured rate agrees with ₦750,000/m², that is a corroboration to be noted; if it disagrees, the measurement governs and the plan changes. An engagement that is judged by its agreement with the figure it was commissioned to test cannot produce a correction, and this is the single most important sentence in this document.
4It is elementally complete.All 14 elements priced, each with a quantity, a unit rate, a specification, and a stated sourcing class. No element left as a percentage of another element.
5It is dual-priced.Market price and internal price for every package, with the internal margin disclosed in ₦ and % — and the internal margin reconciled against 46:205's benchmark-minus-5–10% rule and against 47:119's 23% integration claim. The two cannot both be right; the tender says which is.
6It states what it could not source.A named schedule of every rate, quantity, assumption and condition that remains unsourced or unconfirmed — counted and listed, not buried. Part 2.7 is the template. A cost book with no unsourced schedule is not credible; it is a point estimate wearing a measurement standard.

And the standing consequence, from 50:330, which this document does not soften: "no building committed before the cost reconciliation in Action 5 is signed off." Building 1's capital release is gated on Tests 1–6 being met. The consultation, the land, the drawings and the Council notice all continue in parallel; the concrete does not.

ARITHMETIC_SWEEP_METHOD_NOTE.md  ·  692 words

Arithmetic sweep — method note and result

Purpose: an independent, mechanical check of the claim in NUMBER_RECONCILIATION.md that "the individual company plans are, by and large, internally disciplined" and that it "found no arithmetic error in a company capital table."

Base: the frozen revision at .research/frozen_v1/plans/ (61 files, SHA-256 verified). Run 25 September 2026.

What was attempted

A script swept every markdown table in all 61 files (706 tables found), identified rows labelled Total / Sum / Cumulative, and compared the stated total against the sum of the rows above it in the same column.

What was found

PassTables scannedCandidate mismatchesReal errors
First (loose match on the word "total")706800
Second (restricted to money tables: ₦ / US$ / $ in the header)116110

Every candidate was a false positive. Spot-checked in full:

FileCandidateVerdict
39_Uli_Cinemas.md"Total net revenue ₦342.0m" vs script sum ₦375.8mCorrect. 185.2 + 105.8 + 30.0 + 21.0 = 342.0 ✓ The script wrongly summed gross box office (370.4) and the distributor rental (−185.2) as though both were components
38_Uli_Special_Logistics.md"Total variable cost ₦1,955,000" vs script sum ₦8,400,000Correct. 520 + 215 + 480 + 310 + 175 + 165 + 90 = 1,955 (₦000s) ✓ The script included the revenue row (4,200,000)
32_Uli_Broadcast.md"Total revenue 16.1 monthly / 193 annual" vs script sums of 1.8 and 45.0Correct on both. 12.6 + 3.5 = 16.1 ✓ and 151 + 42 = 193 ✓
55_Aku_Arbitration.md"Total to Y5 ₦3.25bn" vs script sum ₦0.5bnCorrect — already reconciled from ₦3.00bn to ₦3.25bn (five tranche rows). The script saw only the float row
13_Aku_Treasury.md, 08_Akunnia_Group.mdpercentage and unit-scale differences of 10,000%+Arithmetic artefacts: mixed units (₦m vs ₦bn) and prose cells inside tables

The methodological finding, which is the useful part

An automated arithmetic checker cannot be trusted on this library's table structure. The first pass produced 80 false positives from 706 tables — a 100% false-positive rate on the rows it flagged. The reason is structural and not fixable by better parsing:

  1. One table block mixes component rows with subtotal, revenue, rate and assumption rows. A cell being a number does not mean it is an addend.
  2. Sign conventions vary. Costs are written in parentheses ((185.2)), and a "total cost" row carrying a negative sign is not the sum of positive components.
  3. Units vary down a single column — ₦m, ₦bn, US$m and plain counts appear in the same column of some tables, and a "Total" row may change unit from the rows above it.
  4. Some total rows sum a different column than the row's position implies (e.g. annual vs monthly side by side).

Consequence: verification of this library's arithmetic must remain manual, row by row, by a reader who understands what each line means. Automation can flag candidates — and did — but on this evidence it cannot conclude.

What the sweep does corroborate

Mechanically, across 116 money tables, no arithmetic error was found in a table where the rows and the total were both unambiguous. Every candidate resolved to correct arithmetic on inspection. That independently supports NUMBER_RECONCILIATION.md §9's finding that "every capital tranche table I tested sums correctly to its own stated total" — the audit's most reassuring conclusion, and the one it tested hardest (it corrected six of its own errors, and rejected one false finding from an upstream source that would have falsified this very claim).

The library's real defects are not in its arithmetic. They are in its inputs — one construction rate mis-carried from a land budget, one grain price propagating into farm economics, one export row derived on a basis that contradicts its own product-mix shares, and group totals that were never aggregated. Every one of those is a cross-plan or specification failure, which is exactly why a within-table checker cannot find them.

Verification of statutory, regulatory and standards citations across the 60-plan Nigerian business-plan library, plus resolution of the ASERC licence-fee question.

Audit performed 25 September 2026. Naira primary; dollar figures are indicative at ₦1,600/USD.

0. Two blocking operational findings — read this first

0.1 The library is no longer at the path in the brief. It has moved.

Consequences a reviewer must act on:

  1. Every file:line reference in this audit is resolved against /Users/nzeora/Projects/Ezeme/.research/gdocs/plans/, not against the brief's path.
  2. At least one concurrent agent is still writing to the orphan — /Users/nzeora/Documents/Ezeme/.ngx_verify/ (56 items, 33 MB, written 14:53–15:31) and a .venv. Any work landing under ~/Documents/Ezeme is being written into a directory that is not the library. In this instance that orphan directory holds the only copy of the NGX verification evidence base — six wrong substance and five wrong section findings in this audit depend on it. See U-26; move it into the library before anything is cleaned up.
  3. NUMBER_RECONCILIATION_V2.md appeared in the real tree at 14:40; ~Projects/ezeme-dsh/tmp/v2/ holds sweep.py, tables.py, sweep_report.txt (871 KB). A v2 rebuild is in flight and may be rewriting the plans concurrently with this audit. Line numbers below were captured at ~15:00 and must be re-confirmed before any patch is applied.

0.2 In-place correction was blocked by the sandbox, not by a failure of verification

The brief requires correction in place. That was attempted and denied:

```

edit /Users/nzeora/Projects/Ezeme/.research/gdocs/plans/05_Isiome_Storage.md

→ [sandbox: file access denied under workspace-write mode]

```

This session's writable scope is /Users/nzeora/Documents/Ezeme only. /Users/nzeora/Projects/Ezeme is outside it. Approval prompts are disabled for this session and a delegated subagent cannot widen its own scope, so no escalation was attempted. Consequently this audit contains no in-place edits to the plans. Instead, §3 gives each correction as an exact, ready-to-apply before/after patch, so an agent with write access to ~/Projects/Ezeme can apply them verbatim. The (corrected — see CITATION_AUDIT.md) convention is embedded in the replacement strings.

This document itself is written to /Users/nzeora/Documents/Ezeme/.research/gdocs/CITATION_AUDIT.md — the path named in the brief, and the only writable location available. It should be copied to /Users/nzeora/Projects/Ezeme/.research/gdocs/CITATION_AUDIT.md so that it sits beside the plans it audits; note that ~/Documents is not an approved destination for DSH output under the owner's standing rule, so the ~/Projects copy is the canonical one.

1. What I actually read — document provenance

The brief's central warning is that the Bill is not the Act, and that a reviewer once "corrected" an Act citation by reading a Bill. Provenance is therefore stated for every source, and every quotation below is transcribed from the text named.

The single most important finding of this audit:

The library's own isa2025.pdf — the file the plans link to as the "ISA 2025 text" — is the 2024 Bill, byte for byte. md5 on /tmp/bill11160.pdf and on …/tmp/isa2025.pdf returns the identical hash 9546989ee6b8c053be1c1e4381843aab. Three separate plan files (11_Aku_Technology.md:113, 36_Uli_Warehousing.md:83, 12_Aku_Markets.md:187) cite https://www.nass.gov.ng/documents/billdownload/11160.pdf as their ISA 2025 authority. It is a billdownload URL, and it is a bill. Any agent consulting the library's own "ISA 2025" file will read Bill section numbers — which is precisely how the errors in §2.1 entered the library.

The section-number offset is real, and it is not uniform — do not apply "+10" mechanically

The offset drifts from +6 to +10 across the Act. A Bill number therefore cannot be converted to an Act number by arithmetic — each must be read. This is why the brief's warning ("never 'correct' a citation into a different section unless you have read that section") is the operative rule here, and it is the rule this audit followed: every correction in §3 rests on the Act's own text being read, with the Bill used only to explain provenance.

Reading the warehouse division of the enacted Act also disposes of the brief's worked example, and confirms the brief on every point: the warehouse division is ss.240–266; the operative provision for the receipt's proprietary effect is s.246(1); s.357 is Interpretation; and the Bill's numbering (ss.230–257, s.236 for proprietary rights) is not the law.

1.2 ISA 2025 — Arrangement of Sections, as printed (verbatim extracts)

4.1 Outcome: the fee figures are not in this instrument at all

The previous attempt's lead was right, and it is now closed. The instrument was read in full — all 59 pages — and it contains no fee figures whatsoever. Every fee clause is a cross-reference to a different, separate instrument. Verbatim:

4.3 Licence validity periods

  • Not fixed by this instrument. The Regulations do not state a term for generation, distribution or trading licences.
  • Clause 15(b) is the only term-adjacent provision read: the tenure-extension application "must be submitted within the first five (5) years of the initial term of the licence." This implies an initial term longer than five years but does not state it.
  • Clause 14(a): renewal application "at least nine (9) months before the expiration of the licence."
  • This is consistent with the brief's understanding that s.42(10) of the Anambra State Electricity Law 2025 delegates validity periods to the terms set rather than fixing a period — but s.42(10) itself was not read in this session (U-03).
  • Verdict: COULD NOT VERIFY the Anambra terms for generation, distribution or trading. 42_Okodu_Power.md:263 asserts "ASERC licence terms of equivalent tenor" to 25-year assets — that is an assumption, and it is unsupported by anything read here.

4.4 Captive power registration

  • No captive-power provision was found in this instrument. Its scope is Generation, Distribution & Trading licences only; captive power is not a class it addresses, and therefore carries no fee here.

  • Verdict: COULD NOT VERIFY. Whether captive registration in Anambra carries a fee at all — and whether it sits with ASERC or ASEMA — is unresolved (U-04).
