Aku Bank — is the deposit-funded lending thesis compatible with the rule that the bank never lends to another Aku financial entity? 16:15 states the purpose as funding the Group's credit business; 16:60 and the draft CBN ring-fencing rules forbid it. 08:410 says the case must be argued net of locked capital — has it been? (§6.3)
  5. Okodu Power — does 60% debt stand, or does the ≤40% gearing ceiling bind? 42:167 models 60%; 41:200 flags it as unresolved. The Group's own rule or the largest project's model must move. (§6.1)
  6. 11_Aku_Technology — is ₦5.92bn the ten-year requirement, or is the annual cost path in §7 the real one? The two differ by ₦7.6–11.4bn. Also settles whether tranche figures are programme budgets or annual rates. (exc. 26)
  7. 12_Aku_Markets — is the ₦0.40bn fidelity bond a cash cost inside T1 or a non-cash bonding capacity? The table's Total (3.90) does not equal its rows on either reading, and the same 3.90 is used for the T0+T1 cumulative. (exc. 4)
  8. 08_Akunnia_Group — which figure is the Bank's national-tier regulatory capital: ₦200bn or ₦332.5bn? ₦332.5bn is the whole four-stage programme (6.5+14+72+240). The Group's governing document currently overstates locked capital by ₦132.5bn. (§4.2)

  10. Akunnia — net the ₦120bn GP reserve once, and fix Fund I's target (USD 100m / 250m floor / 300–500m). Until then no Akunnia capital total is meaningful — the group's own §6 says so. Three candidate totals now circulate: ₦1,312bn (v1), ₦1,554bn (recomputed), and none defensible. (§4.2)
  11. Every group plan — add one sentence stating whether its tranche table is a phase budget or a full-life programme. This single clarification makes the ~50–90% gaps between groups and their companies interpretable instead of alarming. (§4.3)

  13. Insurance, hedging and FX: does the Group want a debt and FX register? §6.2 confirms the policy is stated everywhere, but no schedule exists to test compliance against — so "no unhedged USD debt" is currently unverifiable by construction.

  17. The 39 files not swept in §5 — commission the remaining arithmetic sweep before relying on any "clean" impression of them. (§5.1)
  18. 07_Isiome_Trading — reconcile the live file with the freeze. It is the single file that has moved since 2026-09-25 04:20 WAT. (§1.3)

9. Bottom line

9.1 What is now verified that v1 could not verify

  1. The evidence base is immutable, and the immutability is demonstrated. 66/66 hashes OK, exit code 0. v1's disqualifying problem — "ten files changed while it was auditing them" — cannot recur, and this run measured post-freeze drift rather than asserting its absence: exactly 1 of 61 plan files has changed, named. v1 could not have answered that question at all.
  2. The library's shared inputs are governed far more tightly than v1 could establish. All 61 files use ₦1,600/USD — 109 hits, no exceptions. Every group's financing section states gearing, hedging and ring-fencing rules. Collection efficiency agrees at 72% where stated. The cement and maize conflicts are real but self-flagged by the plans themselves.
  3. The ring-fencing and hedging rules are stated universally, not sampled. 132 ring-fencing hits across 47 files, 146 hedging hits across 51. v1 had to flag these provisionally; they are now swept.
  4. Both named corrections are verified present and arithmetically sound — and the Aku Credit one is independently corroborated twice, including by the companion row that would have refuted it (§5.5).
  5. The library's arithmetic is broadly sound where it is testable. ≈310 tables across 22 files produced 52 exceptions, most of them in derived ratio and unit cells rather than capital tables. v1's core reassurance largely survives — and, importantly, it was also partly falsified: 12_Aku_Markets.md:262 is a capital table whose Total does not equal its own rows.
  6. The author-modelled structure is honest where it matters. 51_Aku_Credit.md:141 heads its own table "⚠️ The table does not balance, and the shortfall is not explained" and sets out ₦5bn/₦15bn/₦30bn of unfunded capacity; 08's §6 refuses to state a total rather than state a double-counted one; 41 warns that it contradicts its own subsidiary; 46 names its own two cement ranges. The library's authors flag their defects more often than the audit finds unflagged ones.

9.2 What remains open

Open itemSize of the gap
14 of 61 files not swept for arithmeticDown from 39 after three further passes, which found material errors in files earlier passes had marked clean. No claim is made either way about the remaining 14
Group-vs-company reconciliationNot like-for-like: gaps of −53% to −91%, plus Akunnia not computable and Akuzo ₦0.00. One clarifying sentence per group would resolve most of it
Akunnia's capital totalThree candidate figures (₦1,312bn / ₦1,554bn / none defensible) with a known ₦120bn double-count unresolved
Okodu ₦196bn vs Okodu Power ₦684bn₦488bn of unexplained difference
41 escalations in §7.3Arithmetic certainly wrong; the correct side undetermined
A1–A4 not appliedSpecified precisely, verified absent from the live tree. The live tree is outside this session's writable workspace and approval is disabled, so the four one-line edits could not be made. This is a completed failure, not an open question — §7.2 gives the exact file, line, before and after for each
No FX/debt register exists"No unhedged USD debt" is currently unverifiable by construction
Market figures without reachable sourcesNamed as unverified; not invented, not averaged

9.3 The three highest-value actions

1. Complete the arithmetic sweep on the remaining 14 files — before any capital is committed on the strength of a "clean" library. Coverage rose from 22 to 47 of 61 files across four passes, and the exceptions found rose from 52 to ≈85. The marginal passes kept finding material errors — including one that overturned a "verified" claim in this report's own first draft (36:136, §5.4/§5.7) and a ₦1.0bn error in the bank plan's central thesis sentence (16:143). The unswept 14 are named in §5.1, and their absence from §5 is not evidence they are clean. This is now cheap: the freeze is in place, the method is proven, and coverage is measurable.

2. Answer decision items 1–3 — the three restatements that change numbers rather than wording.

  • Akuzo tranche 3 (₦222.00 vs ₦213.00) — is a ₦549.88m programme actually ₦540.88m?
  • Idenze Schools boarding (₦336m vs ₦696m) — on one of the two readings the school does not break even at any occupancy its own plan claims, which is a thesis-level question, not a cell.
  • Okodu ₦196bn vs ₦684bn — a ₦488bn question about the Group's largest commitment.

Each is a single adjudication; none requires a re-model.

3. Add the standard basis line to every group and company capital table: "this table is a [phase budget / full-life programme] and is stated on a [equity / debt+equity / total programme] basis." This is the one structural defect this audit found repeatedly and it is nearly free to fix. It explains the ~50–90% group-vs-company gaps, it would have prevented excc. 4, 12 and 26, and it is the same class of defect ARITHMETIC_SWEEP_METHOD_NOTE.md identified from the other direction: not bad arithmetic — two defensible bases and no statement of which one is in use.

9.4 Honest summary

The freeze worked, and it changed what could be claimed. v1's own recommendation was right, and executing it produced two things v1 could not: a measured drift figure (1 file in 61) and inputs that are swept rather than sampled — which was the exact defect v1 named in itself. Both Aku corrections verify. The core arithmetic is broadly sound.

But this report must not overclaim. It covers 22 of 61 files for arithmetic. It found no unambiguous errors in most of what it swept and 52 exceptions overall, of which only 4 were unambiguous enough to correct — a ratio that is itself the central technical finding: this library's numbers are rarely wrong by miscalculation; they are wrong because two defensible bases are in play and no file says which. Fourteen of the escalations would collapse with one policy sentence each.

And one v1 claim has been partly falsified, deliberately recorded here rather than quietly dropped: "I found no arithmetic error in a company capital table" does not survive 12_Aku_Markets.md:262. A report that corrects six of its own errors, as v1 did, earns the right to be tested — and this one tested it, found it mostly right, and says where it is not.

End of report. Frozen base: frozen_v1/, 66/66 SHA-256 verified, frozen at 2026-09-25 04:20 WAT. Post-freeze drift: 1 file (07_Isiome_Trading.md). Arithmetic coverage: 47 of 61 files, ≈685 tables. Exceptions: ≈90. Corrections unambiguous enough to apply: 4 — specified, not applied (the live tree is outside this session's writable workspace; §7.2, patch script prepared). Escalated for decision: 13 named items plus ≈63 numeric exceptions. Residual gap: 14 files, named in §5.1.

plans/00_Family_Business.md  ·  4,689 words

00 — FAMILY BUSINESS

Ezeme Group: the family enterprise plan

Naming: companies take the children's names plus a plain function — Ezeme Group is the mother company; Isiome · Akunnia · Idenze · Uli · Okodu Group are its five groups. See ../EZEME_NAMING_ARCHITECTURE.md (v5.0).

FX note: naira is primary throughout; dollar figures are indicative at the rate stated, and the library planning rate is ₦1,600/USD (spot ~₦1,328, CBN NFEM Sept 2026). Do not compare dollars across plans.

Horizon: 10–15 years for the milestones below, inside a longer multi-decade ambition.

Position in the programme: this is the first plan. It defines the family enterprise itself. The five domain plans follow in birth order — Isiome, Akunnia, Idenze, Uli, Okodu.

1. Thesis

The family business is not a company. It is three things stacked, and they must never be confused with each other.

LayerWhat it isWhat it doesWhat it must never do
FamilyThe House of Ezeme — the Charter, Assembly, Council, CourtMembership, values, succession, disputes, distributionsManage companies
OwnershipEzeme Family Trust → PTC → Ezeme Family Holdings (Mauritius) LtdHold the family's wealth indivisibly, in perpetuity-intent formTrade or operate
EnterpriseEzeme Group → five holdcos → operating companiesBuild, manufacture, move, lend, teach, generateDecide family questions

The single sentence that justifies the whole structure: a family with the right structure, the right sequence, and the right land can redesign not just a business portfolio, but an entire city — and the structure is what makes the wealth survive the people who built it.

Ezeme Group is the mother company. Every other group in this architecture — Isiome Group, Akunnia Group, Idenze Group, Uli Group, Okodu Group — is a subsidiary of Ezeme Group, and every operating company is a subsidiary of its group. One parent, one consolidated balance sheet, one Group Board, one name at the top. The five groups are how the work is organised; they are not independent enterprises, and no group holds equity that Ezeme Group does not ultimately control. Read the five group plans in that light: each is a division of one company, not a separate family business.

Why the separation is load-bearing, not bureaucratic. Every family enterprise that fails, fails at one of these joints: the family treats the company as a personal estate and it becomes uninvestable; or the company treats the family as staff and the bloodline fractures; or ownership is held personally and the first disengaged heir, death, or divorce scatters what four generations built. The three layers exist to make each of those impossible by construction.

2. The family

Founded by Somtoo Ezeme (Founding Principal) and Ifeoma Ezeme. Home base: Nkpor, Idemili North LGA, Anambra State. Motto: "Onye aghala nwanne ya" — let no one abandon their kin.

Child (birth order)OfficeDomains
1. IsiomeFirst Son — PatriarchAgriculture & Food Systems · Manufacturing & Industrial Production
2. AkunniaFirst Daughter — MatriarchFinance & Investment Systems · Governance, Law & Security
3. IdenzeSecond SonEducation & Human Capital · Healthcare & Pharmaceuticals
4. UliSecond DaughterCreative Industries & Information · Transport & Logistics
5. OkoduThird SonEnergy & Utilities · Construction & Real Estate

Group slogan: Five Children. Ten Sectors. One Empire.

The wider household. Beyond the seven-member nuclear family, the Akuzo development is sized for 100+ Ezeme cousin households. The Charter is deliberately scoped to the nuclear bloodline "rather than the extended kindred of Akuzo" — two concentric circles, governed differently and deliberately firewalled from each other.

3. The ownership layer

Ezeme Family Trust (Mauritius, Trusts Act 2001)

Settlor: the Founding Principal. Trustee: Ezeme Family Holdings PTC Ltd — a Private Trust Company, so trustee decisions sit with a family board rather than an external professional trustee. Protector: the Founding Principal, then the Family Council chair. Beneficiaries: House of Ezeme members per the Charter.

A Mauritius discretionary trust runs 99 years from creation — far beyond what Nigerian trust law reliably allows. It carries anti-forced-heirship clauses and a "flee clause" permitting the seat or governing law to move if a jurisdiction turns hostile. Multi-country footprint: Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa, Brazil, UAE, UK.

Ezeme Family Holdings (Mauritius) Ltd — GBC

Owned by the Trust. Holds controlling equity and reserved-matter rights in the Nigerian parent. Substance is mandatory, not decorative: Mauritius's 2018 Finance Act reforms require core income-generating activity performed locally, adequate resident employees and resident direction. A brass-plate GBC will be struck off and will destroy the Group's standing with every DFI it approaches. Budget for a real Port Louis office, two resident directors, and a Mauritius administrator and auditor.

Why only these three things move offshore — the Trust, the PTC, and the GBC. Operating companies, employment, tax residency, real-estate title and day-to-day governance stay in Nigeria. The one layer that must never be locally contestable is ultimate ownership and succession.

The rules that carry all the weight

1. The Capital-Source Ownership Rule. Any business funded by Group capital is a controlled subsidiary, unless the Family Holdings board expressly resolves otherwise in writing at the time capital is committed. No informal understanding, family custom or subsequent conduct establishes personal ownership. Every injection is characterised at the time as equity, shareholder loan, subsidiary formation capital, or JV contribution.

2. Reserved Matters requiring Family Holdings consent: change of name or brand disassociation from "Ezeme"; disposal or encumbrance of material assets above an annually fixed threshold; issuance of shares, dilution or admission of any external investor; any pledge or charge over shares; change of control, merger or listing; winding up; appointment or removal of external auditors.

3. Standing rights: a permanent non-removable Family Director on every subsidiary board; quarterly management accounts and annual audited statements; right of first refusal on share transfers; drag/tag-along restricted to intra-family or approved transfers. These sit with Family Holdings, not with any individual — so they survive succession automatically.

4. Cap-table hygiene. No entity anywhere issues equity to employees, operators or partners at Group or holdco level. Employee ownership exists only inside operating subsidiaries, capped, and never touching the Mauritius layer. This rule is the price of institutional capital.

5. Beneficial ownership is unconditional; operational control is not. Economic rights cannot be revoked for non-performance — an heir does not lose their stake by stepping back. But operational control is granted, not inherited, and a non-engagement trigger (set by the Family Council; comparable charters use 24–36 months) refers control to the Group Board, which appoints a steward. The disengaged heir keeps their economic entitlement in full. Nothing is confiscated. Control, not ownership, is what moves. Re-engagement is always possible.

4. Ezeme Family Office

The family office is the interface between the family and the enterprise — and its entire value is that it keeps the two apart while making both work.

FunctionWhat it does
Family governance supportSchedules and papers for Assembly, Council, Court, Business Board; maintains the Charter and its amendments; the Secretariat and Archive
Wealth stewardshipThe collective investment portfolio, emergency reserve, common property, education fund, philanthropy, intergenerational wealth
Consolidated reportingOne view of the whole family's position across every holdco and jurisdiction
Distributions and payroll of entitlementImplements Council decisions on distributions; distinct from employment pay
Heir developmentEducation funding, the rotation programme, domain activation on completion of a first Master's
Succession administrationProtector succession, trustee renewal, vesting schedules, the Family Director appointment roster
Records and historyBirth, marriage and property records; the family tree; the growing Ezeme Family Archive
Risk and compliance oversightEnsures the ring-fencing policy is actually observed — no cross-pledges between regulated entities

Cost discipline. A family office is the single easiest place for family money to disappear into overhead. It is budgeted at a fixed percentage of consolidated net assets, reviewed annually by the Audit & Risk Committee, with the founding generation able to veto increases.

Treasury is deliberately not here. Internal capital allocation, FX and banking relationships sit in Aku Treasury under Akunnia Group — because treasury is a commercial function serving the enterprise, while the family office serves the family. Mixing them is how families lose track of what is theirs and what is the company's.

5. The enterprise: Ezeme Group and the five holdcos

```

Ezeme Family Trust (Mauritius)

│

Ezeme Family Holdings (Mauritius) — GBC

│

EZEME GROUP (Nigeria — CAMA parent)

Group Board · shared services · treasury oversight

│

┌───────────┬──────────────┼──────────────┬───────────┐

▼ ▼ ▼ ▼ ▼

ISIOME AKUNNIA IDENZE ULI OKODU

GROUP GROUP GROUP GROUP GROUP

Agriculture Finance & Pharma & Creative Energy,

& Manu- Governance Education Industries Construction

facturing & Logistics & Real Estate

```

All ten sectors sit under one roof — one roof, one ledger, one name. Each holdco is a separately incorporated company with its own board, its own audit, and its own licensed subsidiaries. The pairing of two sectors per child is a management and reporting concept, not a legal boundary — every regulated activity occupies its own company, because that is how licences and liability actually work.

The Interdependence Rule

"No division is self-sufficient and none is meant to be. Isiome feeds the system. Akunnia funds and protects it. Idenze builds and sustains the workforce. Uli moves information and goods. Okodu powers and builds the physical world. Remove any one of them and the structure weakens. That vulnerability is intentional."

This is the Group's real competitive advantage: its businesses are each other's customers. Uli Freight carries what Azụmahịa and Idenze Pharma produce. Okodu Power powers every factory and campus. Okodu Construction builds every building. Mmụta and Idenze University train every operator. Aku Capital finances the whole thing. No standalone competitor can match that internal demand.

6. Governance — two tiers, strictly separated

The Charter governs a household of seven. It cannot govern a conglomerate. It has no Group CEO, no independent directors, no audit committee, and no decision path faster than a weekly Saturday Council. Running a continental group through family institutions alone is the most likely cause of failure, and it is the first thing institutional capital tests.

Tier 1 — Family governance (the Charter)

Assembly · Council · Court · Business Board · Treasury · Secretariat. Jurisdiction: membership, values, succession, disputes, family property, distributions, and the shareholder decisions reserved to the Trust. It appoints the Family Director. It does not manage companies.

Tier 2 — Corporate governance

BodyCompositionAuthority
Group Board3 family + 3 independent non-executives + Group CEOStrategy, capital allocation, risk appetite, CEO appointment
Group Audit & Risk CommitteeMajority independent, independent-chairedAudit, internal control, licence risk, related-party transactions
Remuneration & NominationsIndependent-chairedExecutive pay, board succession
Group Executive CommitteeCEO + five holdco CEOs + Group CFODelivery
Holdco boardsHoldco CEO + Family Director + 1–2 independentsSector strategy and performance
Subsidiary boardsMD + Family Director + sector CFOOperations, licensing, compliance

Why independents are non-negotiable: they are the price of entry to institutional capital, the only credible defence against related-party abuse between family entities, and what makes reserved matters and the non-engagement protocol enforceable rather than discretionary.

The firewall carries upward. The Charter's separation — the Court does not decide business questions; the Board does not adjudicate personal grievances — extends: family disputes never reach a Group Board, and board decisions are never litigated in the Family Court. Commercial disputes go to arbitration under the shareholders' agreements.

The one governance rule that protects the group's licences

Regulated functions report to the board, not to the operating executive. Quality assurance in pharma reports to the board; the CRO in finance reports to the Audit & Risk Committee, not the CIO. Both are regulatory requirements in their sectors and the structural defence of the Group's most valuable assets.

7. Capital structure and funding

SourcePurposeActive
Founding family capitalSeed: first plants, land, licensingYear 1
Operating cash flowPrimary reinvestment engineYear 2+
Bank and structured debtWorking capital, plant, fleet — ring-fenced per sector, never cross-pledgedYear 2+
Ezeme Diaspora Investment SyndicateIgbo diaspora private equity (UK, US, Canada) — infrastructure and pharmaYear 3–5
Development finance (DFI)AFC, InfraCredit, IFC, BII, DFC — health, education, energy mandatesYear 3+
Aku Infrastructure FundFirst third-party fund — Group pipeline as seed assets, subject to the 25%→15% Group-originated cap. Cannot be raised before a five-year audited track record exists, so this is Year 5–8, not Year 3–5Year 5–8
Pension and sovereign mandatesScale capital — the Aku Capital endgameYear 8+
Equity listing(s)Holdco IPOs, for investor liquidity and price discovery — not as acquisition currency; see principle 5Year 7+

Financing principles, stated once and applied everywhere:

  1. Gearing ≤40% — and it must be defined, because the phrase is meaningless otherwise. Gearing = debt ÷ (debt + equity) at the subsidiary's own ring, on the standard project-finance convention: ≤40% means debt never exceeds 40% of total capitalisation, i.e. ₦0.67 of debt per ₦1 of equity. Under the other common convention — debt ÷ equity — "40%" would mean only ₦0.40 per ₦1, materially tighter. Three plans in this library use whichever convention suits the number, which is how a ceiling becomes decorative. (Refined by the Uli Warehousing and Uli Cinemas plans.) And treat the ceiling as a ceiling, not a plan. At a ~13% unlevered yield against naira lending above 30%, 40% debt consumes essentially the entire net operating income in interest. Practical gearing in the Group's asset-backed businesses is 15–25%, with the balance funded by Aku Infrastructure Fund I on a 10–15 year tenor rather than bank debt. The cost of over-levering shows in break-even occupancy: 29% cash, 44% full-cost, 64% at 20% debt, and 79% at 40% debt. And no unhedged USD debt — the Neimeth precedent (₦1.7bn net loss driven by a ₦2bn FX loss on dollar debt) is the cautionary case from the Group's own state.

⚠️ The 40% rule does not fit a licensed lender, and the Group must decide the carve-out deliberately. 51_Aku_Credit.md is funded 71% debt in Stage 2, 71% in Stage 3 and 79% in Stage 4 — because leverage is not a risk appetite in lending; it is the product. A private credit book funded 40% debt and 60% equity earns an ROE close to its asset yield, before the leverage that makes lending a business at all. The correct treatment is not to force a lender under a rule written for asset-backed operating companies, but to replace the ceiling with the controls that actually govern a lender: a board-set debt/equity cap for that company alone, monthly regulatory-capital-headroom monitoring, wholesale funding maturity matched to loan tenor, no cross-guarantees into the bank or the insurer, and — the constraint that actually matters — a portfolio loss-rate gate, because a 2-point miss on losses costs roughly 30% of ROE while leverage only magnifies whatever the loss rate turns out to be. Okodu Power's 60% debt is the second breach and is a genuine one — a power company is an asset-backed business and the ceiling applies to it. Both are flagged in ../NUMBER_RECONCILIATION.md §5.

  1. Ring-fence financing per sector. A failure in one must never accelerate debt in another.
  2. Licences and land are the collateral; fee businesses are the margin engines. Never cross-pledge the two.
  3. Re-base FX quarterly.
  4. Equity cannot be issued above subsidiary level — and that has a consequence nobody costed. The rule protects family ownership and is why carried interest was deliberately placed at fund level rather than in Group equity. But it also means Ezeme Group, Akunnia Group and Aku Capital cannot issue shares to a seller. Listed holdco equity therefore cannot be used as acquisition currency — the mechanism Blackstone itself uses to buy capability. Consideration must be cash, hedged debt, or rollover equity inside the target company. Two implications: acquisition pace is capped by Aku Capital's own cash generation and borrowing capacity, which makes Aku Bank's deposit base strategically important rather than merely convenient; and the sector holdco IPOs contemplated for Year 7+ do not solve this unless the family accepts outside shareholders at holdco level, which the current rule forbids. Decide this deliberately rather than discovering it mid-negotiation. See ../EZEME_GROUP_OPERATING_ARCHITECTURE.md §10.

And the principle that governs every licence in the Group: a licence is acquired, not waited for. No business in this Group is deferred, reduced or omitted because it needs a licence. Where a licence is required, the plan states who issues it, what it costs to obtain directly — and how to acquire it instead: what kind of existing licensed entity to buy, roughly what that costs, and what the change-of-control process involves. In Nigerian and African markets a licence is frequently cheaper and far faster to buy than to obtain, because the incumbent is undercapitalised, the regulator's de novo process is slow, and an existing entity brings staff, systems, a customer base and a regulatory track record that a new applicant must build from nothing. The Group's stated routes are therefore acquisitions, not applications: acquire a licensed microfinance bank rather than apply for a banking licence (16_Aku_Bank.md); buy a licensed finance company for credit (51_Aku_Credit.md); buy an existing NGX dealing member (12_Aku_Markets.md); buy a licensed private guard company (54_Aku_Security.md); buy a registered fund manager and a shelf GBC (09_Aku_Capital.md); buy a certified or distressed factory rather than build and certify (61_Isiome_Manufacturing.md); buy already-perfected land under a Certificate of Occupancy rather than virgin communal land (59_Okodu_Housing.md); and buy an existing licensed hospital, school or polytechnic rather than accumulate accreditation from nothing (56_Idenze_Healthcare.md, 26_Idenze_Schools.md). Licence acquisition is a costed, dated action in the first ninety days of every licence-gated plan, not a caveat.

8. The people question

Professionalise before you need to. The most common failure of a successful African family enterprise is not competition — it is that the family outgrows its own management capacity while the founder is still the only decision-maker.

  • Membership is not employment. The Charter says it plainly: "family membership does not by itself entitle anyone to a role, a title, or a share of profit." Every family member in a job holds a real role, defined in writing, paid at market, and subject to the same appraisal as anyone else.
  • Domain activation is earned. Each child leads their domain only on completing their first Master's degree — until then, professional managers run it. The Group Master Plan's own assumption that all five begin activating "from approximately Year 22 onward" is the sequencing.
  • Rotation is mandatory. Between 18 and 30, each child works in at least two regions and spends structured time inside a sibling's sector, to prevent institutional blindness.
  • Non-family executives must see a path. Without equity at holdco level, the path is: real authority, board exposure, long-term incentive plans at subsidiary level, and the genuine prospect of running a holdco. A group that only promotes family will lose every good professional it hires.

9. The ambition, stated honestly

The target is Blackstone, not BlackRock. The distinction is not a matter of taste — the two firms make money in completely different ways, and the wrong model produces a structure that cannot execute the family's actual intention, which is "to buy entire companies, reshape industries, and make an astronomical amount of money doing it."

BlackRock — the wrong modelBlackstone — the right model
What it managesPassive money — index funds and ETFsControl stakes — it buys whole companies
Fee economics3–15 basis points1.5–2.0% management fee + 20% carried interest
Deciding skillCost, tracking, distribution scaleUnderwriting, operational improvement, exit timing
Scale engineAssets in, headcount flat (iShares, Aladdin)Funds raised, capital deployed, carry earned
HeadcountFlat per dollar managedGrows with capital deployed — people-intensive
AUM~$14 trillion~$1.3 trillion (Blackstone, 31 Dec 2025)

Why the arithmetic matters. Africa's entire capital stock is roughly $2 trillion. BlackRock at $14tn is therefore about seven times all of Africa combined — unreachable by any amount of African market share, which is why the old plan kept drifting into fantasies about replicating Aladdin and iShares. Blackstone at $1.3tn is about two-thirds of Africa's whole capital stock — demanding, and honestly still enormous, but imaginable, because alternatives AUM is capital deployed into a narrow set of control positions rather than every listed security on earth. The right ambition is measured against the right peer.

Why Blackstone fits this Group specifically — and this is the decisive argument. The Group already builds and owns hard assets: Okodu's generation and property, Isiome's farms and factories, Uli's corridors and warehouses, Idenze's campuses and plant. Blackstone's largest businesses — real estate and private credit — exist to acquire exactly that kind of asset. A financial buyer from New York must hire people to learn a sector; the Group already employs them. And a buyout model rewards operational improvement, which a conglomerate can supply from its own operating companies and a pure financial sponsor cannot.

The evidence that the African base is real: PenCom's Q1 2026 report shows Nigerian pension assets at ₦29.52tn, with 58.07% in FGN securities and only 3.95% in alternatives. PenCom's own risk register lists R1 as real returns below inflation and R3 as FGN concentration, and prescribes the mitigant as a shift into "alternatives, infrastructure, and inflation-linked instruments." The regulator is instructing pension funds to buy precisely what the Group builds, and almost nothing qualifying exists to buy.

The four stages, restated for the control model: Years 1–5 — the Group invests its own balance sheet, buying bolt-on companies that fit its five domains and building the audited track record that makes everything else possible. Years 5–10 — the first third-party fund closes, Aku earns management fees and carry on other people's money, and the platform passes roughly $1–3bn of AUM. Years 10–20 — the platform reaches $15–25bn, spanning private equity, private credit and real assets across Africa, with a perpetual vehicle alongside the closed-end funds. Years 20–50 — the manager becomes a global alternative asset manager raising non-African capital, and the operating conglomerate is one of its holdings rather than its whole identity. Listing is a step on the path, not the destination — Blackstone itself is listed, and stock is how it buys capability.

What this costs the family, stated plainly. The control model needs deal professionals paid like deal professionals — base at 60–70% of global-bank equivalents plus carry, which the Group has resolved can sit at fund level without ever touching Group equity. It needs a global hub in London or New York, because the LP capital that funds a $15bn platform does not sit in Lagos. And it means the Group's own businesses become, over time, a source of assets and deal flow rather than the destination of all the Group's capital. That is a real change in what the family enterprise is. It is also the only version of the ambition that the family's own words describe.

12. First ninety days

  1. Commission the audit of every existing entity's cap table. You cannot retire Igba Odibo or install reserved matters without knowing exactly where equity sits. This is the gating item.
  2. Draft the Group Board charter and the independence criteria; shortlist independent directors.
  3. Instruct counsel jointly — Nigerian (CAMA, Charter amendments), Mauritian (trust, PTC, GBC substance), and the sector regulators as each plan requires.
  4. Appoint the Group Regulatory Affairs lead. The Group's most valuable assets are licences; this function's whole job is holding them, and it is the most under-rated hire in the plan.
  5. Stand up the family office with the Secretariat and Archive — records first, because the family's history and decisions are otherwise lost to memory alone.
  6. Set the ring-fencing policy in writing and have the Audit & Risk Committee adopt it: which entities may never be cross-pledged.
  7. Adopt the FX convention (naira primary, ₦1,600/USD planning rate, quarterly re-base) as a board resolution, so every subsequent plan is comparable.
  8. Open the five domain plans in birth order — Isiome, Akunnia, Idenze, Uli, Okodu — using this document as the parent brief for each.

This is the first plan in the programme. It is the parent brief for the five domain plans that follow in birth order: Isiome Group → Akunnia Group → Idenze Group → Uli Group → Okodu Group.

01 — ISIOME GROUP

Agriculture & Food Systems + Manufacturing & Industrial Production — the first child's domain

Naming: companies take the children's names plus a plain function — Ezeme Group is the mother company; Isiome · Akunnia · Idenze · Uli · Okodu Group are its five groups. See ../EZEME_NAMING_ARCHITECTURE.md (v5.0).

FX note: naira is primary throughout; dollar figures are indicative at ₦1,600/USD (spot ~₦1,328, CBN NFEM Sept 2026).

Position in the programme: first child, first domain. Follows 00_Family_Business.md.
GroupIsiome Group — subsidiary of Ezeme Group (the mother company)
OwnerEzeme Family Trust (Mauritius) → Ezeme Family Holdings (Mauritius) Ltd → Ezeme Group → Isiome Group
HeirIsiome — First Son, Patriarch
SectorsAgriculture & Food Systems · Manufacturing & Industrial Production
CompaniesIsiome Seed · Isiome Machinery · Isiome Farms · Isiome Storage · Isiome Foods · Isiome Trading · Isiome Manufacturing
GeographyIdemmili belt (production) · Nkpor, Idemili North LGA (processing, manufacturing, HQ)
Horizon10–15 years, licensing and land front-loaded

1. Thesis

Isiome Group owns the food and industrial value chain from seed to packaged goods — and the machines that work the land in between.

The group's own words: "Isiome grows it, builds the machines that work the land, and then processes what comes off it. His edge is owning the equipment layer that every farm and factory in the empire depends on."

Why this is the right first domain. Three reasons, in order of weight:

  1. It is the only domain where the money is already moving. Nigeria's food demand is not a forecast — it is a present, growing, naira-denominated market with no import substitute available at scale. Agriculture needs no new licence category to begin.
  2. It feeds every other domain. Isiome feeds the Group: the university and hospital canteens, the staff estates, the hospitality and institutional contracts Uli Group will service, and — critically — the botanical and herbal inputs that Idenze Pharma's plant will consume. No other domain has that reach.
  3. It is politically and socially constructive. A group that raises yields, hires farm labour and supplies cheap food to its own workforce earns the community goodwill the Akuzo programme depends on. "The agricultural supply feeds all Ezeme staff estates across Nkpor, reducing living costs for workers and making Group employment a more compelling proposition than any competitor in the area."

The strategic principle: own the value chain, not the farmland. Africa's production is overwhelmingly smallholder; land ownership is neither available nor the source of margin. Inputs, mechanisation, offtake, processing, storage and logistics are — and that is where Isiome should be indispensable to every farmer it touches.

2. Market

The macro case

  • Africa imports over 70% of its medicines and, in agriculture, is a net food importer of staple calories despite holding most of the world's uncultivated arable land. Nigeria alone spends billions of dollars annually on food imports that its own soil could produce.
  • Nigeria is the largest economy and the largest population in Africa, with food demand rising faster than domestic output — urbanisation, population growth and a growing middle class all push processed-food consumption up.
  • Food inflation in Nigeria has been persistent and double-digit, which is simultaneously the problem Isiome addresses and the margin it earns. A business that shortens the chain from farm to shelf captures the spread that intermediaries currently take.

Where the margin actually sits

StepMargin characterIsiome's play
Inputs (seed, fertiliser, crop protection)High, recurring, sold before plantingIsiome Seed — sell to farmers, get paid first
MechanisationAsset-heavy, high utilisation sensitivityIsiome Machinery — lease and service, not just sell
Primary productionLow, weather- and price-exposedIsiome Farms — demonstration, R&D, and supply certainty
Storage & aggregationEvent-driven, huge in scarcity yearsIsiome Storage — buy at harvest, sell at the top
ProcessingStructurally high — this is the value stepIsiome Foods — garri, starch, palm oil, flour, canned
Trading & exportVolume-driven, FX-earningIsiome Trading — ECOWAS and AfCFTA corridors
Industrial goodsCapital-intensive, import-substitutingIsiome Manufacturing — packaging, tools, parts

The single most important commercial decision: the Group's own documents identify storage and offtake as the mechanism by which a farming region's value is captured. Buying at harvest when prices are lowest and selling into scarcity is the oldest and most reliable margin in agriculture. Isiome Storage is therefore the profit engine, not Isiome Farms.

Competitors and landscape

  • Smallholder farmers — the actual producers, and Isiome's customers and suppliers rather than its competitors.
  • Established Nigerian processors — flour millers, palm-oil processors, cassava processors. Fragmented at the top, informal at the base.
  • Importers — the incumbent for anything Nigeria cannot yet process, and the target Isiome displaces.
  • Trading intermediaries — the party Isiome's model removes, and the party most likely to oppose it commercially.

The gap: no integrated operator in the South-East combines inputs + mechanisation + offtake + processing + storage under one structure. Each step exists separately and informally; the integration is the moat.

3. Product & service lines

Isiome Seed — inputs and seed

Certified seed, fertiliser, crop protection, and the agronomic advice that makes them work. Sold on cash or seasonal terms to contracted smallholders. The strategic purpose is not the margin on inputs — it is that it makes the farmer a customer before the crop exists, and secures the offtake relationship.

Isiome Machinery — mechanisation

Tractor and implement fleet, leasing, service depots, and eventually light agricultural machinery assembly. Own the equipment layer. Utilisation is the entire economics: a tractor that is idle is a tractor that is losing money, so the business is a scheduling and service business disguised as a fleet.

Isiome Farms — production (Idemmili belt)

Target 100–200 hectares acquired over 15 years, developed progressively. Per the Group's own plan:

  • open farmland — cassava, maize, rice, vegetables, cash crops
  • greenhouses for year-round tomatoes, peppers, herbs and high-value exotic vegetables
  • fishponds and aquaculture
  • livestock — poultry, goats, pigs
  • on-site grain silos and drying infrastructure
  • irrigation systems and a seed bank
  • farm worker housing

Idemmili land is the cheapest in the corridor (₦5M–₦20M per plot), which is precisely why production belongs there and processing does not.

Two findings from the Isiome Storage plan that change this business materially.

1. Warehouse receipts now have statutory force. The Investments and Securities Act 2025 (Part XV Division B; s.246(1), which makes the receipt ""first proof of the holder having proprietary rights in the commodities"", with s.249(1) making it transferable by endorsement and delivery) recognises the warehouse receipt in statute for the first time — as "first proof of the holder having proprietary rights in the commodities", not a conveyance — and makes SEC registration of warehouse operators and collateral managers mandatory. So registration is Year-1 work, not Year-5 — and it is what makes receipts bankable as collateral.

2. Toll storage alone does not carry a hub this size — and the obvious fix creates a fraud risk. On the storage tariff alone, Year-5 break-even needs 82% utilisation, which fails the Group's own 75% ceiling for adding capacity. Blended with a trading book it passes, and full-cost break-even arrives Years 7–8 by growing the book, not by adding silo. But trading your own book while issuing receipts against third-party loan collateral is the classic commodity-finance fraud shape, and it breaks the standing ring-fencing constraint. So the plan splits the business: Isiome Storage Ltd (trade and store) and a separate SEC-registered collateral-management company with its own board, independent director, audit and insurer. Cost of carry is the driver — ~₦78,000/tonne over six months at 22–26%, larger than storage, drying, handling, insurance and shrinkage combined — so a four-point rate move swings ~₦13,000/tonne, roughly half the entire storage tariff.

Isiome Storage — storage, aggregation and offtake

Silos, cold chain, warehouse receipts, and the offtake contracts that make contracted farming bankable for the smallholder. This is the profit centre. Cold storage also connects directly to Uli Freight for Southeast and ECOWAS distribution.

Isiome Foods — processing and packaging

The Nkpor processing plant, per the Group's plan:

FacilityFunction
Agro-processing plantRaw produce into packaged goods — garri, starch, palm oil, canned tomatoes, milled flour
Cold storage & logistics hubPerishables storage; interfaces with Uli Freight
Packaging unitLabels and seals for retail, institutional and export
Quality control laboratoryTests produce at intake and after processing to institutional and export standard
Institutional sales & distributionDirect supply to Group schools, hospitals, staff estates and the Onitsha market

Isiome Trading — trading and export

Domestic wholesale, institutional supply, and export into ECOWAS and AfCFTA markets. The FX-earning line, and the one that turns Isiome from a Nigerian business into a West African one.

⚠️ Cross-cutting finding from the Isiome Machinery plan: the 2026 tariff regime weakens any import-substitution case that rests on tariff protection. Agricultural and manufacturing machinery went to 0% import duty on 1 July 2026 (2026 Fiscal Policy Measures, 127 tariff lines revised; a 192-line Import Adjustment Tax phasing to zero by 2036), and a Nigerian tractor manufacturer with 6,000 units/yr capacity is publicly weighing relocation to Rwanda over exactly this. Consequence for this domain: Isiome Manufacturing cannot assume it is protected from imported industrial goods. Its case must rest on proximity, logistics cost, service responsiveness and Group captive demand — not on a tariff wall that no longer exists. Zero duty is not zero landed cost (VAT and levies remain), but it is a structural change to the arithmetic.

Also noted: two capital lines risk double-funding the same iron. The Isiome Machinery plan's Tranche 1 supersedes this plan's "first tractor fleet" line, and its Tranche 4 overlaps this plan's "machinery assembly" line. Net these before Group capital is committed so the same equipment is not funded twice.

Isiome Manufacturing — industrial production

Zone A compound with expressway access. Converts agricultural raw materials and imported industrial inputs into packaged, export-ready goods — and ultimately into the machinery and parts the rest of the Group consumes. This is where Isiome's engineering education is deployed: an industrial engineer running a factory, not a farmer running a farm.

4. Operating model

The geographic split, which is the whole design

Idemmili produces. Nkpor processes. Idemmili land is cheap and plentiful; Nkpor land is far too valuable to grow on. So:

  • Idemmili — farms, greenhouses, ponds, livestock, silos, irrigation, worker housing
  • Nkpor — processing plant, packaging, QC lab, cold storage, corporate HQ in Zone C, and the interface to Uli Freight

The full vertical

```

Isiome Seed ──sells inputs to──► smallholders ──contracted offtake──► Isiome Storage

│ │

└──► Isiome Farms (own production, Idemmili) ──────────────────────────┤

▼

Isiome Foods (Nkpor processing)

│

Isiome Manufacturing ◄───────────────┬──────────────┘

▼

Isiome Trading ──► Uli Freight ──► ECOWAS

```

Quality and standards

  • NAFDAC registration for every packaged food product.
  • SON (Standards Organisation of Nigeria) conformity for packaged goods.
  • Export certification — phytosanitary and country-of-destination requirements for each market.
  • Traceability from farm to pack, which is both a regulatory requirement in target export markets and the basis of premium pricing.

Technology

Mechanisation telematics, farm management software and yield data are the operational backbone — and are exactly what Isiome's own education was designed to command: "Farm Management Systems (Granular, Trimble), IoT soil/climate sensors, drone and satellite imagery, commodity pricing platforms, cold chain logistics" and "MES and ERP systems (SAP, Odoo), quality control and defect tracking, supply chain visibility."

The Group rule, stated once for the domain: a licence is never a reason to defer or omit a business. Every licence below is either obtained directly or acquired with the entity that already holds it — and in Nigerian and African markets acquisition is frequently cheaper and far faster than a de novo application, because the incumbent is undercapitalised, the regulator's new-applicant process is slow, and an existing entity brings staff, systems, a customer base, a dealer or buyer network and a regulatory track record that a new applicant must build from nothing. Each company plan carries the licence-by-licence table with costs and change-of-control mechanics; this is the portfolio view. Where acquisition buys time rather than capacity: Foods and Seed, where the binding constraint is the regulator's clock, not money. Where acquisition does not apply at all: the NESREA EIA and effluent approval, which attach to a site and a process rather than to an owner — so buy the site, then file.

6. Capital requirement

Indicative, in tranches. Naira primary.

TranchePurpose₦~US$

Financing rules: gearing ≤40%; no unhedged USD debt; ring-fence Isiome's debt from the other four groups so a poor harvest year cannot accelerate obligations elsewhere. Working capital for offtake is best served by structured commodity finance against warehouse receipts rather than plain balance-sheet borrowing.

7. Unit economics

Presented as the shape of the economics, with the figures that must be verified locally flagged.

LineBasisNote
Inputs margin10–20% on seed, fertiliser, crop protectionRecurring, pre-planting, low credit risk on cash sales
MechanisationRevenue per tractor-hour against fuel, operator, maintenanceUtilisation is the whole game — break-even typically above 500 hours/season
Farm productionCost per hectare against yield × farmgate priceLowest-margin step; justified as supply certainty and demonstration

Break-even logic: the group reaches operating break-even when processing throughput covers the fixed cost of the plant, which in practice means securing anchor institutional offtake before commissioning the line. Selling to the Group's own estates, schools and hospital is the guaranteed base load — the same principle that makes Uli Freight's plan work.

Flagged for local verification: current farmgate prices by crop and state, processing line capex by equipment vendor, cold-chain energy cost, tractor-hour rates in Anambra, and achievable yields per hectare on Idemmili soils. None of these should be assumed from national averages.

8. Organisation

Leadership. Isiome leads on completing his first Master's. Until then, the Group's own rule applies: "each domain is managed by professional staff under Group oversight." Domain activation is earned, not inherited.

First ten hires

  1. Managing Director / General Manager (professional, pre-activation)
  2. Head of Agriculture (agronomy)
  3. Head of Processing (food technologist)
  4. Head of Storage & Offtake (commodity trading background)
  5. Head of Mechanisation (fleet operations)
  6. Quality Assurance Manager — reporting to the board, not the MD
  7. Head of Supply Chain & Logistics
  8. Finance Controller
  9. Sales & Institutional Accounts Manager
  10. HSE and Compliance Officer

Headcount trajectory: ~40 (Year 1) · ~180 (Year 3) · ~450 (Year 5) · 1,500+ (Year 10).

Hiring priority is agronomy and processing supervision — the two functions that determine whether output meets specification. Both are scarce in Nigeria and should be recruited early and paid above market.

11. Integration

This is the domain with the most connections in the Group, in both directions.

Supplies to:

  • Idenze Pharma — botanical and herbal inputs for pharmaceutical production. The Group's plan already notes Idenze's healthcare arm produces "herbal and manufactured medicines," and the agricultural base is where those inputs come from.
  • Uli Freight — a large share of Uli's captive base load. Isiome's output is what fills Uli's trucks in the early years.
  • Every Group estate — food supply that lowers the cost of living for Group employees across all five domains.
  • Idenze University and the hospital — canteen and catering supply, and a site for agricultural research and student placement.
  • Uli's hospitality and institutional contracts — food service content.

Buys from:

  • Okodu Power — electricity for the processing plant and cold storage, at Group rates
  • Okodu Construction — plant, silos, warehouses, worker housing
  • Okodu Real Estate — the Idemmili worker housing and Nkpor corporate premises
  • Aku Capital — working capital, commodity finance, treasury, insurance
  • Uli Freight — inbound inputs and outbound finished goods
  • Isiome's own training interface — Idenze Polytechnic programmes (corrected — see NUMBER_RECONCILIATION.md; "Isiome Polytechnic" is not a company in the v5.0 naming architecture) supply machine operators, QC technicians and engineering assistants years before a university exists

The internal-customer advantage: Isiome does not need to find its first customers. The Group's own estates, schools, hospital and factories are a guaranteed base load, and the Group's own logistics fleet moves the goods. No standalone agro-processor in Anambra starts with demand already contracted.

12. First ninety days

  1. Commission a land title audit and secure the first Idemmili tranche (30–50 ha) with Deed of Assignment and Governor's Consent. This is the item that must not wait — cheap land does not stay cheap.
  2. Commission an agronomic soil and water survey of the acquired land, and a yield-potential assessment by crop. Do not plant before this is done.
  3. Open NAFDAC's food-product registration pathway and identify the first five SKUs for registration.
  4. Tender the Nkpor processing line to at least three equipment vendors on fixed-price contracts with performance guarantees. Do not accept a single quotation.
  5. Sign the first institutional offtake letters with the Group's own entities — Idenze University, the teaching hospital, the staff estates — to establish base load before the line is built.
  6. Recruit the Head of Agriculture and the Head of Storage & Offtake. These two roles determine whether the group makes money in years 1–3.
  7. Design the contracted-farmer programme — input supply, agronomy support, guaranteed offtake price, and a written contract in the farmer's language and the local dialect. This programme is Isiome's real competitive moat: once a farmer is supplied and bought from, they do not switch.
  8. Set the FX and gearing policy for the group as a board resolution: naira primary, ₦1,600/USD planning rate, gearing ≤40%, no unhedged USD debt, re-base quarterly.
  9. Commission the domain licence-acquisition scan, and budget it — the action that makes the Group's rule real. Instruct counsel to build a priced acquisition pipeline, company by company: registered seed companies and agro-input distributors (02), a certified food processor with live NAFDAC registrations (06), an existing SEC-registered warehouse operator or collateral manager (05), an export trading house or licensed customs agent (07), a certified workshop or machinery assembler (03), and a distressed MANCAP-certified factory (61). Budget ₦200m across the domain — roughly ₦5–6m a target for legal, financial and regulatory-file diligence across some thirty candidates, plus valuations, one written view per regulator on change-of-control mechanics, and a single consolidated report to the Group board. The deliverable is a priced buy-list, and its purpose is the rule itself: no licence in this domain is ever a reason to defer a business.

plans/02_Isiome_Seed.md  ·  4,033 words

ISIOME SEED — Certified Inputs, Agronomic Advice & Farmer Origination

Naming: companies take the children's names plus a plain function — Ezeme Group is the mother company; Isiome · Akunnia · Idenze · Uli · Okodu Group are its five groups. FX: naira primary; dollars indicative at ₦1,600/USD, not comparable across plans.

Ezeme Group · Isiome Group · Isiome Seed Ltd (CAMA). Horizon 15 years · Year 1 = 2027. Ezeme Family Trust (Mauritius) → Ezeme Family Holdings (Mauritius) Ltd → Ezeme Group → Isiome Group → Isiome Seed. Geography: origination in the Idemmili belt, hub at Nkpor, last mile through agro-dealers, intake through Isiome Storage.

1. Thesis

Isiome Seed sells certified seed, fertiliser, crop protection and agronomic advice to contracted smallholders. The reason it exists is not the margin on any of them.

One sentence: it makes the farmer a customer before the crop exists.

  1. The input margin does not justify the business. Fertiliser is a near-commodity priced daily in the open market, and §7 shows the input business losing money at one hectare per farmer once advisory, credit loss and funding cost are charged to it.
  2. The offtake relationship it secures does. Once Isiome supplies a farmer's inputs on seasonal terms and guarantees his price in writing, he does not switch: the relationship is worth more than a spot price from a middleman.
  3. So Isiome Seed is Isiome Group's origination engine. Its output is not bags sold but contracted hectares that deliver to Isiome Storage.
  4. The credit is secured by the crop, not by cash — offtake deduction, not cash lending (§5, §10).

A competitor can undercut a bag; nobody undercuts a contract that has already put seed in the ground. Isiome Seed is where that moat is built.

2. Market

Nigeria's problem is a demand-side trust failure on a supply-side certification failure. Improved varieties cover only 16% of maize, 14% of rice and 6% of cowpea land area, and just 9% / 7% / 3% of those farmers buy certified seed (IFPRI LSMS); cassava and maize seed systems remain largely informal and farmers recycle maize seed for years (IITA). Most plant unknown genetics and cannot tell it from the genuine article.

Fertiliser is the second trust failure. Prices rose 11% into the 2026 season (BusinessDay); states are subsidising, Benue at 50% (BusinessDay) and Gombe by price cut (Independent NG). A rising, subsidised market is where adulteration flourishes. Blending sits largely in the North — about four plants across the West and South-East (PIND), so the South-East runs on distant blending and open-market repackaging: an opening for a soil-test-based blend at Nkpor, and the reason adulterated product is common here.

The gap. No operator in the Idemmili belt and Nkpor corridor bundles certified product + advice + a written guaranteed offtake price + deduction at intake. The real competitor is the open-market bag with no provenance; the incumbent in seasonal finance is the middleman who lends against a discounted harvest.

Flagged: no credible prevalence figure for counterfeit seed exists. NASC's own commissioned survey found it "does not have a clear idea" where counterfeiting is worst (IPA), and SeedSAT found no reported prosecutions as of 2021 despite penalties existing (SeedSAT). A plan quoting a specific "X% of Nigerian seed is fake" is unsupported; §12 measures local adulteration complaints rather than assuming a rate.

3. Product & service lines

  1. Certified seed — maize, rice, cowpea, soybean, cassava stems, vegetables: third-party certified varieties plus own multiplication from the NASC-registered seed bank at Isiome Farms. Yr 5: 30% of input gross profit — the best-margin line.
  2. Fertiliser — bulk from registered blenders, then soil-test-based blends from Nkpor. Yr 5: 34%.
  3. Crop protection — registered agrochemicals, safe-use discipline, no repackaging into unlabelled containers, ever. Yr 5: 22%.
  4. Agronomic advisory — soil testing, per-hectare protocols, planting dates, spacing, IPM, and a field officer accountable for the season rather than the sale. The differentiator, though it does not pay for itself (§7).
  5. Seasonal credit against offtake — the contracted-farmer package. An instrument, not a product.
  6. Offtake origination — a written forward purchase at a published floor price and grade, honoured by Isiome Storage at intake and invoiced as an origination fee — or the moat is invisible and the entity that builds it reports a loss.

Own brand or established brands? Distribute established registered products under a service brand of our own; manufacture own-brand only where we hold the genetics or the formulation — our own multiplied seed and soil-test-based fertiliser. Own-brand seed requires variety registration: 42–55 months and up to US$60,000 of trial cost (CESSA/Seed Sector Plan), so licence an already-released variety first and breed later.

4. Operating model

Sourcing. Seed is multiplied in a documented chain — breeder and foundation seed, contracted multiplication with the Isiome Farms seed bank and vetted multipliers, conditioning, sampling, testing, sealing — and every lot carries a batch number, a retained sample and a certification tag, because the tag is the product. Fertiliser is re-tested on receipt; crop protection only from NAFDAC-registered suppliers, in sealed packs.

Distribution. Nkpor holds bulk stock, the laboratory and the blending line; belt depots of 200–600 t sit within a day of the fields; agro-dealers are the last mile — the only route to a one-hectare farmer, bound by non-transferable agency agreements, consignment rather than credit stock, serialised receipts, published resale prices and a termination clause that is used.

Farmer origination and the contract, in writing and in the local language. Field officers recruit into 10-hectare cluster blocks — the minimum Isiome Machinery also enforces (03_Isiome_Machinery.md) — and each farmer is registered once with a single farmer ID shared across Seed, Machinery and Storage. Contracts are executed in Igbo with a certified English translation and state the input package and price basis, the published floor price and grade, the intake point, the deduction schedule and remedies. A contract a farmer cannot read is a trap he will escape the first time prices move.

Seasonal credit: offtake deduction, not cash lending. Inputs are booked as a receivable at planting; no cash is disbursed at any point. Repayment is a deduction at intake, executed by Isiome Storage on Isiome Seed's written authority. Controls: caps by hectares, a partial cash contribution, cluster group liability, no second season before clearance, monthly ageing to the board. Loss comes mainly from diversion to a middleman; an intake point inside the belt is the only control that works.

5. Licensing and acquisition pathway

  1. CAC. Isiome Seed Ltd, single-purpose; the input and credit books never sit inside another Group company (§10, risk 6).
  2. Seed — NASC, under the National Agricultural Seeds Act 2019 (NESG; AGRA): merchant registration; variety registration through the National Variety Release Committee for any variety we multiply; certification and quality control on every lot; a seed testing laboratory; SEEDCODEX labelling; import permits. Apply in Year 1 — the certification calendar, not the construction schedule, gates the first own-brand sale. Fees are trivial against the capital plan: licence tiers ₦15,000–₦60,000, certification tags ₦5.00 each, testing ₦1,250–₦1,500 a sample (NASC tariff; 2023-dated — re-confirm in writing).
  3. Fertiliser. Product registration and quality-control compliance; a blending licence before the Nkpor line runs; specification testing in and out; honest declared nutrient content.
  4. Crop protection — NAFDAC. Every product registered before it is offered, sold in original packs, the banned actives list a live item, no decanting. A shortcut is criminal and a poisoning risk.
  5. Weights and measures. Calibration of every scale and bagging line, declared net weight. A short bag is the cheapest way to lose a brand.
  6. State and local. Anambra State registration and input-dealer permits; alignment with the Anambra ADP (Anambra State); LGA premises consents.
  7. Settle before the first credit season. Repayment by deduction is trade credit; as cash plus interest it can be characterised as banking business requiring a CBN licence — so no cash, a documented seasonal price differential, the receivable factored to an Akunnia entity, counsel opinion first.

The licence is acquired, not waited for — and here the clock, not the fee, is the reason. NASC fees are trivial (§5.2: ₦15,000–₦60,000 in licence tiers, ₦5.00 a tag, ₦1,250–₦1,500 a test). What is not trivial is the certification calendar and the variety-release queue — which is exactly why §10, risk 5 treats NASC delay as the risk that gates own-brand seed. A registered seed company or agro-input distributor already holds the merchant registration, the product registrations, the dealer permits, and — most valuable of all — a dealer network and a regulatory track record. Buying one does not avoid the fit-and-proper test; it avoids the queue.

What is not verifiable, and it is the number that matters. No public price exists for a Nigerian registered seed company or licensed agro-input distributor — they are private, family-held, and transactions are undisclosed. None is invented here. What is verifiable is the structure of the value: replacement cost is trivial in fees and expensive in years, so the acquirer is buying time, registration and a dealer network, and the price is a first-ninety-days finding. The nearest public comparable class is listed-company acquisition of Nigerian agribusiness assets — for instance Ellah Lakes' share purchase agreement for ARPN Nigeria Limited (NGX filing) — with price terms [verify], and it is a proxy for the class, not a price for a seed business.

Working capital, not capex, matters: at Year 5 the seasonal book carries roughly ₦10bn of receivables against ₦7bn of fixed assets — a revolving seasonal book with a depot attached. The seed price is the one verified retail anchor — mainstream hybrid maize at about ₦4,000/kg across two independent retailers (Afrimash) — so the variety mix, not just volume, drives the package. Compete on fertiliser; earn on seed.

Advice costs ₦18,000 per farmer per year — an officer loaded at ₦7.2m serving 400 farmers at 1 ha, less ₦6,000–10,000 recovered. Advice does not pay for itself, and at one hectare per farmer the model cannot work: at 2–3 ha the same cost spreads over ₦600,000–900,000 of sales and the ratio turns. Advice forces consolidation — also why Isiome Machinery enforces a 10 ha cluster minimum.

Credit loss on seasonal receivables: 3–5% by design, 8–12% in an adverse season, 20%+ in a severe one. Bank of Agriculture attributes about 70% loan defaults to fragmented farming (BusinessDay) — why the credit is never cash. Loss comes mainly from crop failure or diversion to a middleman; mitigants are caps, group liability and credit cover via Aku Insurance.

Cycle. Inventory turns 90–120 days; receivables once a year at 150–180 days. Stock builds Jan–Feb, distribution peaks Mar–Apr — the peak funding need, harvest and deduction land Sep–Nov. Size the facility to the April peak, not the annual average.

11. Integration

It supplies Isiome Farms — inputs on Group terms, certified varieties by block, and the multiplication arrangement that returns certified seed from the farm's NASC-registered seed bank (04_Isiome_Farms.md) — and the contracted-farmer network, whose written contract and input package make a smallholder's season bankable.

The offtake it secures flows to Isiome Storage, and that is the whole point. Contracted tonnes are delivered to Storage's intake points, where the deduction is executed and the balance paid. Without Isiome Seed's contracts, Storage's intake points are buildings with no tonnage; with them, Storage has a forward book it can finance.

It supports Isiome Machinery's leasing customers — smallholder demand aggregates into 10-hectare cluster blocks (03_Isiome_Machinery.md), so the input contract is the machinery booking calendar.

It buys from Uli Freight (belt distribution — this company owns no long-haul fleet), Okodu Power (depot power at Group rates), Okodu Construction and Materials (depots and blending plant), Akunnia (Aku Capital structures the seasonal facility and origination fee; Aku Insurance covers credit and weather; Aku Technology runs the deduction ledger), Idenze Polytechnic (agricultural technology graduates as field officers — 25_Idenze_Polytechnic.md), and Idenze Research (soil and seed testing).

Boundaries. Seed owns the input relationship and the farmer registry; Storage the intake, receipt and trade; Machinery the machines; Foods the processing. Intercompany sales are priced to a published, board-approved schedule benched to belt market prices. Because Storage executes the deduction on Seed's behalf, the deduction authority is written into both contracts, minuted and audited.

12. First ninety days

  1. Commission the belt input survey — three seasons of prices by crop and LGA, certified-seed share, adulteration complaints, the agro-dealer map, the subsidised-bag price. Gates every later tranche.
  2. Instruct counsel on the credit structure. No bag on credit before the opinion is in hand.
  3. Open the NASC file — merchant registration and the variety-registration path. The certification clock is years, not months.
  4. Confirm the product position — NAFDAC status, the banned actives list, the blending licence, weights-and-measures calibration.
  5. Design the contract and guarantee — Igbo with a certified English translation; price basis, floor price and grade, intake point, deduction schedule. Tested on ten farmers before a hundred.
  6. Sign the first offtake contracts — 100 Idemmili farmers in 10 ha cluster blocks, with the deduction authority in both contracts.
  7. Appoint the first 20 agro-dealers on agency terms, consignment stock and published resale prices.
  8. Recruit the MD, Head of Agronomy, Head of Seed Supply & Certification and Credit Manager — the last to the board. Before the first credit sale.
  9. Fix the price card and the advisory ratio — published per-hectare prices, the 10 ha cluster minimum, a governed cost of advice per farmer.
  10. Set board policy: naira at ₦1,600/USD; gearing ≤40%; no unhedged USD debt; credit loss ceiling 5%; no cash disbursement ever; origination fee minuted.
  11. Open the licence-acquisition file — the acquisition action for this plan. Instruct counsel to identify the registered seed companies and licensed agro-input distributors in the South-East and South-South, establish which hold live NASC merchant registration, released varieties, NAFDAC product registrations and a working dealer network, and price them: NASC and NAFDAC file search per target, registry search, and a written opinion on whether registrations transfer with the entity. Budget ₦35m — ₦5m a target across up to six candidates, plus the opinion and one valuation. It runs beside the NASC filing in action 3 and delays nothing: if a licence can be bought by month four, the own-brand programme starts in year two rather than year four.
