Acquire versus build the South African entity — acquire. A de novo GACP+GMP site costs an estimated $8–15m (₦12–22.5bn) over 24–36+ months with no guarantee of award; a licensed but sub-scale or distressed entity is estimated at $2.5–7m (₦3.75–10.5bn) over 6–12 months, and delivers a licensed, inspected, operating site rather than an intention. Structure it as a share purchase of the licensed entity. These ranges are indicative planning assumptions, not valuations.

Financing principle. Funded by Family Holdings, ring-fenced in separate vehicles per jurisdiction with their own bank accounts and no cross-guarantees or cross-pledges with the university, hospital or any Akunnia entity.

7. Unit economics

Figures are indicative planning bands from public wholesale references, to be replaced with actual supplier quotes and local price research before any investment decision.

Cost of API. Commodity CBD isolate pricing has fallen sharply as global hemp capacity expanded; quoted spot ranges sit in the low hundreds to low thousands of dollars per kilogram by grade, purity and documentation (Hemp Benchmarks, wholesale guide). Planning band: $400–1,200/kg for GMP-certified, pharma-grade CBD isolate landed at Nkpor.

Cost of finished dose. A 30 mL bottle of 100 mg/mL CBD oral solution holds 3 g of CBD: at $800/kg, ≈$2.40 of API. Adding excipients, packaging, fill/finish labour, QC release and overhead: ≈$4–7 per bottle all-in at modest volume, falling to $2.50–4 at scale.

Price. Ex-factory in the Nigerian private market indicatively $12–25 per 30 mL bottle, retail at roughly 2–2.5× ex-factory. Epidiolex's US pricing runs into tens of thousands of dollars per patient-year, but that reflects a specific payer environment and is not transferable to Nigeria.

Margin. 60–75% gross margin at ex-factory once API is internally supplied. The group captures the extraction margin inside the South African entity and the finished-dose margin in Nigeria, so consolidated margin exceeds either node alone — the core commercial argument for the three-node structure, which is margin capture as much as regulatory necessity.

Break-even. The binding number is the fixed-cost base of the Nkpor suite plus minimum South African opex plus regulatory affairs: indicatively $2.5–4m (₦3.75–6bn) per year at modest scale. At 65% gross margin and ~$16 average net realised price, break-even is roughly 300,000–400,000 units per year, achievable in the Nigerian private and hospital channel alone if the product is registered and accepted by prescribers. Payback: 5–7 years to cumulative cash break-even.

8. Organisation

First ten hires — all paid as real roles with defined mandates, none appointed by right of family membership:

  1. Managing Director — pharmaceutical executive with controlled-substances experience.
  2. Head of Regulatory Affairs & Compliance — the single most important hire in this plan; owns the licence portfolio across South Africa, Ghana, Nigeria and every export market.
  3. Qualified Person / Head of QA (GMP) — acceptable to SAHPRA for the SA node; a separate Nigerian QP for NAFDAC release.
  4. Head of Quality Control — potency, purity, residual solvents, heavy metals, microbials, stability.
  5. Director, South Africa Operations — GACP cultivation and extraction.
  6. Head of Manufacturing, Nkpor — finished dosage form, controlled-substances suite.
  7. Head of Supply Chain & Controlled-Substance Logistics — import/export authorisations, chain of custody, gram-level reconciliation.
  8. Medical Director — in-house trials with the university and teaching hospital; pharmacovigilance.
  9. Head of Commercial — Nigeria and ECOWAS; formulary access, prescriber education, key accounts.
  10. Financial Controller (controlled substances) — narcotics inventory must reconcile to the gram; finance is part of the control framework, not a spectator.

Plus a Company Secretary/licensing administrator and secondees from Group Legal.

The compliance and regulatory affairs function. A standalone function with its own budget, reporting to the Idenze Therapeutics board with a direct line to the Group Audit & Risk Committee — not to the Managing Director alone. It owns a licence register (instrument, holder, jurisdiction, conditions, expiry, renewal lead time, named owner), a controlled-substances register (grams in, out, waste, reconciliation, variance escalation), a dossier register per market and an inspection calendar. It enforces a two-person rule on all controlled-substance movement and storage access, an independent annual audit separate from the group audit, a whistleblowing line to the Group Audit Committee, and an anti-bribery policy with a strict no-gifts, no-facilitation-payments rule. It may halt a shipment without seeking commercial approval.

9. Milestones

Year 1 — answers and foundations. Both NACOC questions answered in writing. Ring-fenced vehicle incorporated with its own board including two independent directors. Regulatory Affairs lead appointed. Ghana Indefinite Residence application filed. NAFDAC NCS pathway documented, with written confirmation on SAHPRA GMP acceptance. SA targets shortlisted, offers conditional on SAHPRA consent. No cultivation, no facilities, no procurement, no marketing spend.

Year 3 — licence, plant, first sale. SA licensed entity acquired and under group control with SAHPRA consent; API flowing. Nkpor suite facility-registered and validated. First NAFDAC product registration granted. First CBD oral solution and capsules sold in the Nigerian private and hospital channel. First in-house trial under way. Product-level break-even.

Year 5 — portfolio and footprint. Products registered in 5+ markets, each with its own narcotics import permit. Ghana licence granted and operating, or a genuine JV executed with real equity, risk and control for the partner plus an exclusive offtake and technical-services agreement for the Group. Domestic revenue at scale; three product families launched; first peer-reviewed clinical data published.

Year 10 — the reference manufacturer. West Africa's reference cannabinoid medicines manufacturer, with 10+ registered markets, operating as a net exporter of finished cannabinoid medicines. A second API source in Ghana; Malawi contract biomass only if volume demands it. The Nkpor plant's GMP capability serves the whole generics business. If Nigeria's reform bill is enacted, the group holds an application-ready Nigerian position — a licence-application capability, never a farm.

10. Risks

Ring-fencing, stated plainly. Idenze Therapeutics must sit in a separate legal vehicle with its own board, licences and audit — never in the same entity as Idenze University, the teaching hospital, or any Akunnia finance company. A licence suspension in one jurisdiction must never reach the Group's NUC accreditation, hospital licence, banking or fundraising.

11. Integration

Agriculture (Isiome) — nothing in Nigeria. No Nigerian cannabis cultivation, no hemp agronomy, no land banking premised on the reform bill passing. Isiome holds the group's agricultural value-chain capability (inputs, mechanisation, offtake, storage), relevant if and when the group cultivates directly in Ghana; in Nigeria its focus stays on non-cannabis agronomy and generics feedstock. Trigger to revisit: the moment the bill is enacted. Idenze Therapeutics holds the application readiness; Isiome does not spend against a bill.

Logistics (Uli — Uli Special Logistics). Structurally necessary, not merely useful. Controlled-substance movement requires export and import authorisations, transit permits where a shipment crosses third countries, sealed and reconciled shipments, chain-of-custody documentation in every jurisdiction, secured warehousing and specialist insurance. Very few African logistics operators hold narcotics authorisations — a genuine moat, and one Idenze Therapeutics's captive volume makes worth building.**

Finance (Akunnia). Idenze Therapeutics raises against its own licences and cash flows, never against group assets. Akunnia provides treasury and FX management, builds the specialist controlled-substances inventory accounting discipline, and may later hold a minority position through a fund vehicle.

Education (Idenze — Idenze University and teaching hospital). The structural advantage no competitor can replicate: in-house trials on chronic pain, inflammatory joint disease, spasticity, chemotherapy-induced nausea and refractory epilepsy; the teaching hospital as first prescriber and first real-world evidence site; pharmacy and medical schools as talent pipeline and prescriber-education channel. Honest caveat: if the group sponsors the trial and owns the site, governance must be visibly independent — a data safety monitoring board, an external statistician, ethics approval from the hospital's own review committee, and public trial registration — or regulators will not accept the evidence.

Distribution. Idenze Distribution's licensed wholesale network across ECOWAS is the route to market for branded and white-label product alike, giving the cannabinoid line the same salesforce, warehousing and hospital relationships as the generics business. This is the single largest commercial advantage of being inside the Group, and why the cannabinoid line must not precede the generics business.

12. First ninety days

The two regulator questions to NACOC — submitted in writing through Ghanaian counsel, and answered before any cannabis-related spend beyond legal and licensing work:

  1. Is eligibility for a medicinal cannabis licence limited to Ghanaian citizens, or does it extend to permanent residents — and specifically, does Ghanaian Indefinite Residence granted by the Ministry of the Interior satisfy the test? If it is citizens only, the residence route fails entirely and the strategy changes.
  2. Does the ownership test bind the licensee's shareholding, its directors, or both — and if shareholding, what minimum percentage must be citizen or permanent-resident held? This sets the cap table.

Legal work, commissioned in parallel:

  • Ghana counsel — the NACOC licensing instrument and 11-licence regime; applications, fees, timelines; eligibility and ownership tests read from the primary instrument, not the press.
  • Ghana immigration counsel — Indefinite Residence eligibility, the continuous-residence period, application, and how the status is maintained and lost (Ministry of the Interior).
  • South African counsel — SAHPRA GACP and GMP licence conditions; whether change of control requires consent and whether licences survive the transaction; conditions precedent; export authorisation procedure.
  • Nigerian counsel — the NAFDAC NCS pathway; Controlled Medicines Regulations 2019; whether a foreign GMP certification is accepted; import permit requirements; NDLEA's role alongside NAFDAC.
  • A written anti-front opinion covering the whole structure, confirming every licence is held by the entity that actually conducts and controls the licensed activity and that no nominee arrangement exists anywhere in the chain.
  • Corporate and governance — incorporate the ring-fenced vehicle with its own constitution, board (two independents) and bank accounts; adopt the licence register, controlled-substances register and anti-bribery policies; appoint the qualifying family member(s) by Business Board resolution with a defined mandate and real remuneration.
  • Acquisition diligence on the NCS and NDLEA set — a written opinion on whether any controlled-substances authorisation survives a change of control, with NAFDAC NCS and NDLEA correspondence attached, plus a named register of the entities holding each authorisation and whether any is acquirable or partnerable. Budget ₦95m (Nigerian and Ghanaian counsel). §5's conclusion — that this set is earned rather than bought — rests on this opinion, so it must be commissioned now, not assumed.

The freeze stands until both NACOC answers are in writing and NAFDAC has confirmed whether SAHPRA GMP certification will support a narcotics import permit. No cultivation, facilities, procurement or product claims anywhere until the licences exist to support them.

Idenze Consumer Health — OTC Medicines and Consumer Health Products

Naming: companies take the children's names plus a plain function — Ezeme Group is the mother company; Isiome · Akunnia · Idenze · Uli · Okodu Group are its five groups. See ../EZEME_NAMING_ARCHITECTURE.md (v5.0).

FX note: naira is primary here at ₦1,600/USD, the library planning rate. Dollar figures are indicative and not comparable across plans.

Business plan · Ezeme Group

Operating company Idenze Consumer Health Ltd (to be incorporated, Nigeria) · Holdco Idenze Group (Pharma & Education) · Chain Ezeme Family Trust (Mauritius) → Mauritius GBC → Ezeme Group Nigeria Ltd → Idenze Group → Idenze Consumer Health · Manufacturing Idenze Pharma, Nkpor, Idemili North LGA · Distribution Idenze Distribution, moved by Uli Freight.

Ring-fencing. A commercial company, not a regulated manufacturer: it owns brands, registrations and the sales call, with its own board, audit and P&L. It shares no premises, personnel, brand or supply-chain touchpoint with Idenze Therapeutics — the Group's rule that the cannabinoid entity is ring-fenced binds this company too.

1. Thesis

This is the cash engine that funds the institutional business while it builds. Institutional and tender supply has long sales cycles, tender risk and payment delays — Idenze Distribution plans on 90–120 days for institutional receivables. Consumer health is the opposite: retail and pharmacy channels, higher margin, paid on delivery or in days, with brand loyalty that compounds.

Why this company exists. Idenze Pharma's Phase 1 Nkpor line has ~500m tablet/capsule units of nameplate, a Year-3 fixed-cost base near ₦3.1bn and break-even around 220m units (18_Idenze_Pharma.md §7). NAFDAC-registered oral solid capacity is capital-intensive and an idle line loses money every day. On the arithmetic in §7, Consumer Health's Year-5 pack volume alone approaches the plant's whole Phase 1 nameplate: this is the plant's base load, not a side business.

And consumer health is where brand trust is worth money. Where substandard and falsified medicines are structural (WHO), a serialised, registered, advertised pack is a risk reduction the buyer can see. Tenders pay for price and inspection record; consumers pay for certainty.

The Group owns the advertising capability — no competing Nigerian OTC maker owns its own film, music and broadcast companies, so Uli Group makes our radio and activations in-house.

2. Market

Size. The IFC/World Bank diagnostic anchors Nigerian pharmaceutical sales at US$2.03bn (2023), growing 9.1% compound, with industry capacity utilisation of only 40–50% and about 15% of manufacturers GMP-compliant (IFC/World Bank CPSD 2025). Consumer health is the fastest-turning slice. Planning band: ₦650bn–1.0tn (US$0.4–0.6bn) a year — a derived band, not a market report. Read Euromonitor's Consumer Health in Nigeria and Analgesics in Nigeria before trusting any volume model.

Why the money is at the counter. Health spending is overwhelmingly out-of-pocket (World Bank): the buyer decides, in cash, at a price point they can meet today. Most medicines — especially antimalarials — are bought from patent and proprietary medicine vendors (PMVs) and kiosks rather than pharmacies (IDS), so a pharmacy-only model misses most of the volume.

Counterfeit, and why it is the opening. WHO estimates 1 in 10 medical products in LMICs is substandard or falsified (WHO); the ACPN's widely quoted "over 50%" is an advocacy figure, not a measurement (Punch Healthwise). Anambra traders have been jailed for repackaging paracetamol as antimalarials (Punch Healthwise). Brand trust is therefore the differentiator in Nigeria, and it is bought with verifiability, not claims: serialisation, scratch-and-verify codes, the registration number printed large, tamper-evident seals, and a price point that leaves an undercutter no room.

3. Product & service lines

Antimalarials, honestly. ACTs are OTC-adjacent — policy intent is prescription, practice is counter sale. Register for the channel we can lawfully serve, and treat tighter classification as a planning assumption: if enforcement moves, the line shifts to pharmacy and institutional and the portfolio absorbs it.

Brand architecture — two tiers, one rule. Tier 1: Idenze endorses every pack as the quality mark, beside the NAFDAC number, batch and serialisation code; the endorsement is what makes a new SKU credible and a recall retrievable. Tier 2: neutral product names. The rule: a product name must be neutral, because medicines regulators restrict names and advertising that imply efficacy, promise a cure or claim superiority — the Drug and Related Products Advertisement Regulations 2021 bar statements claiming or implying superlatives such as "most effective" or "least toxic" (S.I. 63 of 2021, NAFDAC advert guidelines). Convention: neutral token + non-proprietary name or category + strength — "Idenze Paracetamol 500 mg Tablets", "Idenze ORS Sachets" — with neutral house sub-brands (Care, Daily, Pure, Fresh) carrying range identity and never a claim. Screen every name on four questions before design: does it name a disease, imply speed or superiority or cure, or read as an efficacy claim to a regulator who knows nothing about us? If yes, reject it. A rejected name costs a design fee; a banned advert costs a campaign.

Packaging and sachet economics. For low-value solids, packaging — not the API — is the largest variable cost line, typically 35–50% on a paracetamol tablet (18_Idenze_Pharma.md §7). The sachet is a distribution strategy, not a margin strategy: best entry price and impulse purchase at the kiosk, worst cost per tablet in the portfolio (§7). Artwork must satisfy prepackaged-goods quantity and net-content rules plus the relevant Nigerian Industrial Standard (SON); confirm the instrument, tolerance schedule and standard number with SON and the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment before artwork is finalised.

Distribution channels — pharmacies and chains (credibility and margin mix), PMVs (the volume), supermarkets and modern trade (visibility, pack-size experimentation) and kiosks (sachets and trial). Advertising and trade promotion: radio and market-level activation outrank digital in reach and trust, so the mix is radio first, activation second, outdoor third, digital as a measured experiment (NDHS 2024). Trade promotion — bonus packs, price-off, retailer incentives, market storms — is 60–70% of A&P spend, because the retailer's recommendation is the last metre of marketing.

4. Operating model

Asset-light by design. This company does not manufacture and holds no wholesale licence; it owns brands, registration assets and demand, and buys everything else inside the Group under written agreements: manufacture from Idenze Pharma; wholesale and logistics from Idenze Distribution with movement on Uli Freight; media and creative from Uli Group.

Who holds the registration. For a made-in-Nigeria product the certificate attaches to the facility and the named applicant (NAFDAC registration guidelines). The certificate is a commercial asset, not paperwork — it decides who is named on the pack and who may move the brand to another plant. Settle holder status in the first agreement.

Route to market. Direct national sales management for key accounts, modern trade and pharmacy chains; a distributor network for the open market, PMV and kiosk channels, with exclusive territories and enforced price lists. We sell only to licensed distributors and licensed outlets — never to unlicensed sellers. That stance is a brand asset as much as a compliance position.

Quality and recall. We are the recall-facing party: a named pharmacovigilance officer (a registered pharmacist), a complaint and adverse-event log reporting into NAFDAC, and an annual tested recall against Idenze Distribution's 24-hour outlet reach.

5. Licensing and acquisition pathway

  • Product registration, per SKU. DR&R-GDL-014-03: 240 working days from acceptance, and the clock stops whenever NAFDAC issues a compliance query — failure to answer within 90 working days closes the application. Certificates run 5 years, renewals on a 90-working-day clock. Budget 12–18 months per SKU and run dossiers in parallel.
  • Facility eligibility sits upstream. No drug may be made in Nigeria without an Authority to Manufacture after pre-production inspection (DER-GDL-008-02) — our launch is gated on Idenze Pharma's licence, not ours.
  • Classification is a decision, not a detail. Whether a vitamin, supplement or personal-care item registers as a drug or under the food-supplement or cosmetic route changes dossier cost and timeline materially. Get it in writing before formulations are locked.
  • Advertising approval is separate from registration — registration confers no advertising permit. Approval is per advert, valid one year and renewable, and bars superlative, curative or misleading claims (S.I. 63 of 2021); advertising-standards vetting also applies (APCON). File 30–90 days ahead of media booking.
  • Standards and measures. Nigerian Industrial Standards (and SONCAP for imported components) apply to products in scope; prepackaged-goods quantity and tolerance rules bite hardest on sachets, the smallest and likeliest-to-recall pack.
  • NAFDAC is not PCN. NAFDAC registers the product; PCN regulates pharmacy premises and practitioners (PCN Act 2022, PCN guidelines 2025). A salesforce is not a pharmacy and never carries prescription-only stock.
  • Traceability. NAFDAC Traceability 2.0 makes GS1 DataMatrix serialisation a market-access prerequisite — the same investment as our anti-counterfeit proposition.
  • Group constraints that bind. Production heads in this chain must be registered pharmacists, and QA reports to the board, not the MD. Mirror it: Regulatory and Quality report to the board, and no claim, name or advert ships without Regulatory clearance. No commercial override.

Nothing here waits on a registration — and the fastest registration is one already granted. Registration is per SKU, 240 working days, with the clock stopping on every compliance query; certificates run five years and lapse if not renewed. That asymmetry is the whole acquisition argument: the asset worth buying in consumer health is not a factory, it is a registered portfolio with shelf space behind it. Nigeria's OTC and personal-care market is crowded with small, under-capitalised brands whose owners cannot fund advertising — which is precisely the supply the Group wants.

Buying a consumer-health brand brings NAFDAC registrations, the trademark, approved artwork, the distributor and retailer relationships and, in most cases, existing shelf space — the last of which cannot be bought with a registration or a salesforce, only inherited. The diligence gate is the certificates themselves: a registration not renewed within its five-year validity — but note this file cites the 5+5 policy elsewhere: an initial five years plus a five-year renewal. (corrected — see CITATION_AUDIT.md) has lapsed, and a lapsed registration is worth nothing but the artwork. Verify every certificate number, its expiry and its renewal status against NAFDAC's register before a single naira is offered.

Budget ₦65m — ₦40m brand brokerage and valuation, ₦15m trademark and NAFDAC registry search, ₦10m legal drafting of a template share-purchase agreement and change-of-ownership filings [verify]. Buying one registration-rich brand is worth more than a year of dossier work, and it is the only route into retail shelf space the Group cannot otherwise buy.

Cost per pack, not per tablet, decides a listing. Distributor takes 6–10%, retailer 12–20%, PMV a hybrid of both; total consumer price lands at roughly 1.45–1.7× ex-factory. Topicals and supplements carry materially higher gross margin than analgesics — analgesics are volume and traffic, not the profit pool. Blended gross margin 42–46%; A&P 12–16% of revenue in Years 1–3, falling toward 8–10% by Year 5; contribution after A&P 26–30%.

Break-even. Year-3 fixed base — brand team, regulatory, national sales management, shared warehousing and freight, base media — ₦1.6bn a year; at ~28% contribution that is ₦5.7bn of revenue, ≈5m packs at a blended ₦1,150 ex-factory.

Working capital cycle. Finished-goods cover 45–60 days; distributor terms 21–30 days (short on purpose: consumer channels pay fast and this company's job is cash); supplier terms 30–60 days. Target cycle ~30 days at steady state, against 78 days in Idenze Distribution's Year 1 — that gap is why the Group holds both companies.

The governing rule: FMCG margin comes from brand and distribution reach, not from price. A price rise that clears the kiosk counter loses more volume than it recovers and hands the shelf to an informal undercutter.

The capacity consequence. Year-5 revenue of ₦18bn at ₦1,150 blended is ~15.6m packs; at ~30 tablet-equivalents per pack that is ~470m tablet units — close to Idenze Pharma's whole Phase 1 nameplate and more than twice its break-even. That assumes a tablet-heavy mix, so a product-level volume model is required before it is used for capacity planning.

8. Organisation

First ten hires, real roles with defined mandates, none by right of family membership: (1) Managing Director — FMCG/OTC general manager with a brand P&L; (2) Head of Regulatory Affairs — owns the registration and advert-approval calendar, reports to the board, the single most important hire here; (3) Brand Manager, Analgesics & ORS — the flagship P&L; (4) Head of Trade Marketing — activation design and retailer economics, the discipline that moves volume in Nigeria; (5) Head of Sales — distributors, territories, price-list enforcement, key accounts; (6) Product Development Liaison — formulations, cost of goods and packaging with the plant; (7) Supply Chain & Demand Planning Manager — S&OP; forecast accuracy is this company's real production function; (8) Quality & Pharmacovigilance Officer — a registered pharmacist owning complaints, adverse events and recall execution; (9) Consumer Insights & Media Manager — brand tracking and the Uli Group interface; (10) Finance & Commercial Controller — SKU profitability and a hard A&P budget.

11. Integration

  • Manufactured by Idenze Pharma at Nkpor — the plant supplies the Authority to Manufacture, the GMP file and the pharmacist-led production chain, and our volume absorbs its fixed cost (§1).
  • Distributed by Idenze Distribution, a NAFDAC GDP-licensed wholesaler whose warehouse, FEFO discipline and 24-hour recall reach we use instead of building. The transfer price between the two companies is a Group allocation and must be documented, or both P&Ls are fiction.
  • Moved by Uli Freight on the Nkpor–Lagos and Nkpor–Onitsha–Aba legs, with Uli Warehousing at the corridor hubs; freight cost per case is a board metric.
  • Advertised through Uli Group's media and creative businesses — jingles, radio and activations in-house, an advantage no competing Nigerian OTC manufacturer has. Caveat: Uli quotes against an external benchmark so the saving is visible, not asserted.
  • Buys power from Okodu Power through the plant: the same plant runs at roughly ₦780/kWh on a diesel baseline against a blended near ₦150/kWh (22_Idenze_Distribution.md §4), which reaches our cost of goods.
  • Employs Idenze Pharma's pharmacists for production, QA and pharmacovigilance, drawing later on Idenze Polytechnic's technician pipeline.
  • Financed by Akunnia Capital — naira facilities matched to the stock cycle, with insurance and guarantees through the Akunnia companies.
  • Isiome Group supplies packaging-adjacent inputs and later cassava-derived starch excipients if they reach pharmacopoeial grade. Not a Phase 1 dependency.
  • Ring-fencing stands. Idenze Therapeutics shares no brand, salesforce, warehouse slot or endorsement with this company. A cannabinoid headline must never reach a paracetamol brand.

12. First ninety days

  1. Incorporate the company and constitute its board with two independent directors — one with Nigerian OTC and trade depth, one with regulatory depth — and Regulatory and Quality reporting to the board.
  2. Appoint the Head of Regulatory Affairs before anything is designed. The §5 classification decision gates everything downstream.
  3. Hold the NAFDAC pre-application meeting and get written answers on the registration route per candidate SKU; classification as drug, supplement or cosmetic; who may be registration holder under contract manufacture; and the advert-approval sequence. This written response is the quarter's most valuable output.
  4. Run the six lead SKUs through the four-question name screen and clear the shortlist with counsel. No packaging design starts on an uncleared name.
  5. Sign heads of terms with Idenze Pharma (supply price, quality, lead times, registration holder) and Idenze Distribution (fees, service levels, transfer pricing).
  6. File the first six dossiers with a compliance-query protocol: named owner, 15-working-day internal deadline against NAFDAC's 90.
  7. Commission the channel and price audit in Anambra, Enugu and Lagos — shelf and kiosk prices, margins actually taken, outlet counts by type, radio listenership by daypart. Size the order book, not the market.
  8. Run one paid pilot campaign on a single category with Uli Group, measured against a plan agreed before spend: it tests the activation model, not the brand.
  9. Confirm sachet tolerance and quantity-statement rules with SON and the weights and measures authority, then lock artwork.
  10. Negotiate the shared-salesforce and A&P cost-sharing agreement with Idenze Distribution before any joint call.
  11. Commission the branded-portfolio screen — five acquirable consumer-health brands, each with its full NAFDAC registration schedule verified against the register, trademark and artwork ownership, distribution list, shelf position and asking price. Budget ₦65m. A registration already granted beats 240 working days of dossier work, and shelf space cannot be bought any other way.

The day-90 gate. Proceed to T1 only if all four hold: written NAFDAC confirmation of route, classification and registration holder; four lead SKUs name-cleared and dossier-ready; packaging specifications costed and compliant; and the Managing Director and Head of Regulatory Affairs appointed. If any fails, delay T1 by two quarters rather than launch a brand on an unregistered product.

Counterfeit prevalence figures vary widely and must not be quoted as measurements.

Idenze Sterile & Injectables — Sterile Manufacturing

Naming & FX: companies take the children's names plus a plain function — Ezeme Group is the mother company; Isiome · Akunnia · Idenze · Uli · Okodu Group are its five groups (../EZEME_NAMING_ARCHITECTURE.md, v5.0). Naira is primary at ₦1,600/USD, the library rate in plans/README.md; dollars are indicative and not comparable across plans — 18_Idenze_Pharma.md used ₦1,400/USD.
EntityIdenze Sterile & Injectables Ltd (RC to be obtained), wholly owned by Idenze Group
SiteNkpor campus, Idemili North LGA, Anambra — own building and utility stack, separate from the oral solid plant
ScopeLarge-volume parenterals and IV fluids, small-volume injectables, ophthalmics, sterile topicals
Horizon15 years. Year 1 = 2027 by convention; this company's clock starts at the sterile gate in 2032, once Idenze Pharma is EBITDA-positive
Ring-fencingOwn NAFDAC file, board, audit and sterility-assurance accountability; gearing ≤40% by policy, 15–25% in practice; no unhedged USD debt

1. Thesis

One sentence. Nigeria imports most of the injections, IV fluids and ophthalmics its hospitals use, because sterile manufacture needs clean rooms, water for injection, sterility-assurance discipline and a NAFDAC route few Nigerian entrants can hold — and Idenze Sterile & Injectables is a family-funded, hospital-anchored plant entered once the Group's oral solid business can pay for it.

Sequencing, bluntly. Oral solids are Phase 1: cheaper, faster to license, where the volume is. Sterile is a different business with a much higher barrier — clean rooms, aseptic processing, terminal sterilisation, water systems, environmental monitoring, a harder NAFDAC route. The Group's domain plan states the rule: sterile injectables are a separate clean-room capital step, never a line extension. An idle sterile line costs depreciation plus a running WFI loop, 24/7 HVAC and a quality function that cannot be stood down.

Why do it. Many oral solid licensees, few sterile ones, and a 500 ml IV bag carries about forty times a paracetamol tablet's contribution. Against: IV fluids are a commodity with thinner margin than a paracetamol tablet; the premium sits in SVP, ophthalmics and topicals; an LVP-only plant never breaks even (§7); and one non-sterile batch is a recall.

2. Market

The IFC/World Bank Nigeria Country Private Sector Diagnostic anchors pharmaceutical sales at US$2.03bn (2023), growing 9.1% a year. Africa imports over 70% of its medicines (Gavi); Nigerian import dependence is put near 60% by NAFDAC and above 70% by the PSN (BusinessDay).

No published Nigerian figure separates sterile from non-sterile demand — the number to verify locally first, with NAFDAC DER and the Federal Ministry of Health. A 15–20% sterile share implies US$300–900m a year: a derived estimate, not a market report (§12). Buyers: teaching hospitals, federal medical centres, state ministries, NHIA/HMO schemes, outbreak response. Local capacity is limited (Juhel in Awka, 150-plus products; Unique, Fidson, Swiss Pharma); Indian and Chinese exporters set the landed-cost ceiling.

3. Product & service lines

Selection runs route first, volume second, margin third.

WaveTimingLines
1 — VolumeSterile Y1–3Sodium chloride 0.9%, dextrose 5%, compound sodium lactate; WFI ampoules; paracetamol and metronidazole infusion — terminal moist heat
2 — MarginSterile Y3–5Aseptic vials (ceftriaxone, cefuroxime, gentamicin, dexamethasone); ophthalmics; sterile topicals — cephalosporins need a segregated block
3 — Scale, exportSterile Y5+Lyophilised vials, prefilled syringes, IV admixtures, contract fill, ECOWAS and WHO-prequalified SKUs

Excluded for the first decade: vaccines, biologics, cytotoxic aseptics, blood products, controlled substances — this is not a vaccine plant and must never be sold as one.

4. Operating model

Classification and design follow ISO 14644-1, WHO sterile GMP, Annex 2 to TRS 1044 and PIC/S Annex 1: 10–15 Pa cascades, airlocks, one-way flow.

GradeISO at rest / operationUseLimits (air / settle)
AISO 5 / ISO 5Aseptic filling, open vials; unidirectional flow<1 CFU/m³ · <1 CFU/4 h
BISO 5 / ISO 7Background to Grade A; gowning entry<10 CFU/m³ · <5 CFU/4 h
CISO 7 / ISO 8Terminally sterilised filling<100 CFU/m³ · <50 CFU/4 h
DISO 8 / —Gowning, component handling<200 CFU/m³ · <100 CFU/4 h
  • Terminal versus aseptic. Terminal sterilisation — moist heat to F₀ ≥ 12 min at SAL ≤10⁻⁶, or dry heat to depyrogenate — wherever product and container survive the cycle; aseptic, with no kill step, where the active is heat-labile. IV fluids, paracetamol and metronidazole infusion and most ophthalmics go terminal; ceftriaxone, cefuroxime and heat-labile vials go aseptic.
  • Isolators versus conventional rooms. Isolators with VHP bio-decontamination remove the human from the critical zone, where sterile plants actually fail; use RABS or a gowned room only where a product cannot run in an isolator.
  • Water for injection. Multi-column distillation with pure steam; stored hot and circulated continuously in a 316L loop — no dead legs — with conductivity, TOC, microbial and endotoxin limits at each point of use. The WFI loop is the process; stopping it is stopping the plant.
  • Monitoring, quality, power. Particle counting in Grades A and B, glove and gown monitoring, and a contamination control strategy owned by a named person; sterility to USP <71>, endotoxin to USP <85>. Batch release is a positive act by a named person who can stop the plant; as the Group requires, Quality Assurance reports to the board, not the MD. Own feeder, UPS on criticals and own generation.

5. Licensing and acquisition pathway

StageWindowContentRisk
PremisesM0–3CAC; PCN premises registration and superintendent pharmacist (PCN Act 2022; PCN inspection guidelines 2025)Low
NAFDAC pre-applicationM2–6DER and inspectorate on the sterile route: classification, aseptic-versus-terminal expectation, sterility-assurance package — in writingMedium
Authority to ManufactureM22–34Under DER-GDL-008-02 nothing may be made until inspection confirms GMP compliance: Site Master File, layout with classifications and pressure differentials, Quality Manual, Validation Master Plan, contamination control strategy and media-fill programme, qualification data and three consecutive media fills per aseptic line and shift. A failed inspection stops the clockHigh
GMP certificationOverlapsAgainst the NAFDAC GMP Guidelines effective 26 November 2024 read with the sterile annex — longer and more technical than the oral solid siteHigh
Product registrationM26–44240 working days from acceptance (DR&R-GDL-014-03), the clock stopping on every compliance query; certificates run five yearsHigh

PCN: the head of production must be a registered pharmacist in Nigeria; production and quality heads must be independent. Standards: Ph. Eur. 5.1.1; USP <71>, <85>, <788>, <1207>; ICH Q1A Zone IVb; the WHO and PIC-S sterile annexes. NAFDAC's contract manufacturing guideline is the optional bridge for filling hero SKUs before our clean room is licensed.

A citation the plan must get right, because Nigerian tender and dossier documents routinely get it wrong. WHO's sterile GMP text is Annex 2 to TRS 1044 — WHO good manufacturing practices for sterile pharmaceutical products (WHO) — not Annex 1, and not the PIC/S Annex 1, which is a different instrument issued by a different body. The sterile annex was carried in earlier TRS editions at different annex numbers, and the PIC/S text is the one most often quoted in vendor literature. Quote the correct instrument in the User Requirement Specification and in every dossier.

The acquisition route — and the honest answer on what such a facility costs.

No licence here justifies deferring the business: the Group obtains it or buys the site that holds it. But this is the one place in the domain where the second half of the rule is genuinely constrained, and the plan should say so. The scarce input in sterile manufacture is not the clean room — it is the inspection and media-fill history of a licensed sterile site, and the people who ran it. A Nigerian facility holding a live NAFDAC sterile manufacturing licence and a GMP certificate to WHO standard is among the rarest assets in the country's pharmaceutical industry: if around 15% of Nigerian manufacturers hold GMP certification at all (see 17_Idenze_Group.md), the sterile subset is a handful of names.

Licence / accreditationIssuerDirect route — cost and timeAcquisition route — what you buy, cost, transfer process, timeRecommended
Sterile manufacturing licence — Authority to ManufactureNAFDACM22–34 under DER-GDL-008-02: three consecutive media fills per aseptic line and shift, contamination control strategy, a failed inspection stopping the clockBuy the licensed site — share purchase carries the licence, the validation files and the media-fill record. No reliable public transaction figure exists for a Nigerian sterile facility [verify]. On the Group's own pharmacy benchmarks (a functioning licensed oral-solid plant is indicatively US$12.6m of T1 capex to build) an acquired sterile site would price at a premium to net assets, not at a discountAcquire if one is available; otherwise the contract-manufacture bridge
GMP certification to WHO standardNAFDAC, against the WHO-GMP basisLonger and more technical than the oral-solid site; the gap to WHO prequalification is Years 5–9 and needs a WHO-inspected siteAttaches to the site and its inspection history — which is exactly what makes an acquired facility worth a premium. WHO prequalification is granted to a product made at a named site, so a change of ownership requires WHO notification and re-inspection; do not assume it survives [verify]Acquire the site, then earn prequalification on our own products
PCN premises and superintendent pharmacistPCNM0–3; the head of production must be a registered pharmacistRe-issued to the new superintendent pharmacist; otherwise the establishment transfers with the entityAcquire with the entity
Product registration, per SKUNAFDAC240 working days from acceptance per SKU, clock stopping on queriesA share purchase carries the acquired site's existing registrations — and for a sterile business the registered portfolio is often worth more than the buildingAcquire with the entity
ISO 13485, if devicesAn accredited certification body9–18 months to build a compliant QMS and certifyCertificates are issued to a legal entity, so a change of ownership triggers re-issue and a fresh audit [verify] — the system transfers, the certificate does notAcquire the system; recertify in our own name

Is acquiring more realistic than building and certifying from scratch? Yes — if a target exists, and the plan must establish whether one does before assuming either answer. The build route here is already the longest and most capital-intensive in the Group (§6 puts T1 at ₦41.6bn), and its critical path is an inspection the Group cannot influence. Buying converts an uncertain regulatory sequence into a diligence problem, and it brings the two things that cannot be recruited in a Nigerian sterile market: a validated aseptic history and a Head of Sterility Assurance who has run one. The counter-argument is equally real: there may be no such facility in Nigeria that is willing to sell, in which case the plan's own contract-manufacture bridge is not a compromise but the correct answer — it is a purchase of capacity, not of a licence, with the permit-holder remaining the licensee of record and the Group holding its registration where the guideline permits. It buys the market years before the clean room exists, and it de-risks the ₦41.6bn commitment rather than substituting for it.

First ninety days — commission the sterile capacity register. Every Nigerian facility holding a live NAFDAC sterile manufacturing licence: capacity by line, dosage forms, current GMP status, media-fill history, ownership, and whether it is for sale or for tolling; plus firm tolling terms from three for the two hero SKUs, priced per batch with qualification, tech-transfer and release responsibilities assigned. Budget ₦70m — ₦35m regulatory, technical and valuation advisers, ₦25m tolling negotiation and tech-transfer scoping, ₦10m supplier audits [verify]. This register decides whether sterile injectables is a build or a buy, and it is the only work in the quarter that can change T1's size.

6. Capital requirement

2.1× the oral solid plant's capital for a comparable order of revenue — the consequence of clean rooms and sterility assurance.

TranchePeriodPurpose₦ bn~US$ m
T0 — Feasibility and gate2031–32Feasibility, NAFDAC pre-application, design, URS, first four senior hires1.81.1
T1 — Clean rooms, first lines2032–34Building, Grade A/B/C/D clean rooms, WFI and pure steam, HVAC, LVP and SVP filling, terminal sterilisation, labs, power, validation41.626.0
T2 — Margin lines, launch2034–36Ophthalmics and topicals lines, component stock, dossiers, working capital12.88.0
T3 — Scale and export2036–42Lyophilisers, second fill hall, prefilled syringes, contract fill, WHO-PQ package, ECOWAS dossiers28.818.0
Total85.053.1

Clean rooms and water dominate capex. Within T1: clean rooms — panels, HVAC, terminal HEPA, cascades, airlocks — US$4.4m, civil and GMP fit-out 5.0, WFI and pure steam and water loop 2.8, filling, sealing and isolators 4.2, terminal sterilisation and labs 3.0, power and clean utilities 2.4, the rest 4.2. Clean rooms, the water systems and the civil and power works serving them are US$14.6m — 56% of T1 (4.4 + 2.8 + 2.4 + 5.0); process machinery is under a fifth. Per unit of capacity this is 8.6× the oral solid plant (§7).

FX. 85–90% of T1 equipment — isolators, fillers, autoclaves, WFI stills, HVAC and HEPA — is imported and dollar-denominated against naira revenue: carry a 15% FX contingency inside T1 and price-lock at order. No unhedged USD debt — ₦2bn of FX loss on foreign-currency loans turned Neimeth's viable business into a loss-maker (BusinessDay). Funding: Trust equity for T0–T1; the diaspora syndicate and Akunnia Capital for T2; Afreximbank/BOI debt thereafter. Gearing 15–25%, never above 40%.

7. Unit economics

Illustrative Year-5 model, not a quotation; a costed bill of materials per SKU is a pre-gate deliverable.

ProductPackEx-factory ₦Variable ₦Contribution ₦GM
Sodium chloride 0.9%500 ml bag1,45090055038%
Paracetamol infusion 1 g100 ml bottle1,70090080047%
Ophthalmic chloramphenicol10 ml dropper1,30060070054%
Silver sulphadiazine 1%50 g sterile jar2,8001,3001,50054%

Where the premium is. SVP, ophthalmics and topicals carry 47–54% — a real premium over oral solids, from fewer licensed competitors and hospital acceptance. IV fluids do not: 38% is below a paracetamol tablet. Weighted 46–52% against 44–60% for oral solids, with 20–40× the contribution per unit.

Capacity governs everything — it is the metric to watch above revenue, margin and headcount.

Capacity metricFirst phase
Nameplate120m units a year — 30m LVP bags, 90m SVP/ophthalmic/topical units
Fixed cost, Sterile Y5₦26bn (US$16.3m)
Weighted contribution₦430 per unit
Break-even~60m units — 50% of nameplate
Rejects and sterility3–5% LVP, 2–3% SVP; zero positive units per media fill

The design-governing number: 30m LVP bags at ₦550 cover ₦16.5bn against ₦26bn of fixed cost — an LVP-only plant breaks even at 47m bags, more than it can make. Below 45% utilisation it burns cash; at 70% it earns its cost of capital.

Why only after oral solids. Oral solids reach first commercial batch on ₦21bn in 24–30 months, break even at 44% utilisation and cost ₦42 of capex per annual unit of capacity; sterile needs ₦43.4bn, 30–36 months, and ₦362 per annual unit — 8.6×, breaking even at 50%. The oral solid plant funds this one; this one can never fund the oral solid plant.

8. Organisation

FunctionSterile Y1 (build)Sterile Y3 (commercial)Sterile Y5 (scale)
Executive and governance246
Production, incl. operators158132
Sterility assurance and microbiology21226
Quality Assurance and Control43060
Engineering, utilities, regulatory, supply chain43878
Sales and institutional tenders11432
Finance, IT, HR, admin21020
Total16166354

By Sterile Y10 the site carries 550–650 staff on two shifts. Sterility assurance, microbiology, QA and QC are 42 of 166 staff at Year 3 — 25% of headcount, against 18% at the oral solid plant.

First ten hires: (1) Managing Director, sterile facility inspected to national GMP; (2) Head of Quality Assurance, independent of production and reporting to the board, not the MD; (3) Qualified Person equivalent — no statutory EU-style QP exists in Nigeria, but the function must: a registered pharmacist certifying batch release who cannot be overruled commercially; (4) Head of Sterility Assurance — contamination control strategy, media fills, cycle validation, EM trending; the scarcest hire here; (5) Head of Microbiology; (6) Head of Production, sterile — a registered pharmacist in Nigeria; (7) Engineering and Utilities; (8) Validation; (9) Regulatory Affairs; (10) Sterile Components and Supply Chain.

Scarcity binds. Nigeria has a few hundred people with solid-dosage GMP experience and a few dozen with genuine sterile experience; sterility assurance and microbiology specialists are countable on one hand. Hire above market; take senior Indian or South African figures on knowledge-transfer contracts with named successors. Governance: own board (chair, one Idenze Group nominee, the MD, two independents), own licence, audit and insurance; no apprentice-equity share model in the cap table.

9. Milestones

Company years; dates assume the gate opens in 2032.

Sterile Y1 (2032)Sterile Y3 (2034)Sterile Y5 (2036)Sterile Y10 (2041)
RegulatoryPCN premises registered; NAFDAC pre-application confirmed in writingAuthority to Manufacture; 4–6 SKUs registered; GMP certificate12–16 SKUs; clean media-fill and EM records20–28 SKUs; WHO prequalification for one product
CommercialZero revenue, by design₦16bn (~US$10m); Idenze Distribution agreement; two hospital contracts₦52bn (~US$33m); utilisation 55–65%₦88bn base / ₦120bn stretch; utilisation 78–85%
FinancialT0+T1 committed — ₦43.4bn (US$27.1m)Contribution-positive; break-even visible at 50%EBITDA-positive; gearing ≤25%Net margin 12–16%; no unhedged USD debt

Discipline. No revenue before the Authority to Manufacture and three passing media fills. No further capital until utilisation reaches 65% of nameplate; below 45% at Sterile Y4, fix the mix — do not build more clean room.

10. Risks

#RiskMitigation
1Sterility failure and product recall — the catastrophic risk: one released batch means recall, suspension and possibly a deathTerminal sterilisation where possible; isolator filling; media fills per line and shift; batch release independent of the MD; recall cover
2Clean-room contamination — failures are environmental and human, not mechanicalNamed contamination control strategy; VHP decontamination; glove and gown monitoring; EM trending
3Equipment and utilities failure — the WFI loop, autoclaves and HVAC run continuously, so a power event is a rejected batchOkodu Power contract with penalties plus own generation; UPS on criticals; duplicate autoclaves
4Talent scarcity — a few dozen genuinely qualified people nationally, and Lagos firms hire from the same poolHire the top four early and above market; expatriate contracts with named successors
5NAFDAC licensing delay — no published inspection day-count, and registration clocks stop on every queryWritten pre-application confirmations; SMF, validation plan and contamination control strategy ready before inspection; six months' contingency
6FX on imported equipment — 85–90% of T1 equipment is dollar-denominated against naira revenue15% FX contingency inside T1; price-lock at order; no unhedged USD debt
7Capacity under-utilisation — ₦26bn of fixed cost a year whether the fillers run or notAnchor volume from Idenze Distribution before equipment orders; hospital tenders from design; contract fill
8Imported competition — landed Indian and Chinese cost sets the ceiling, and the 5+5 policy is adding local capacity (88 plants under construction, March 2026)Compete on inspection record, lead time and hospital service; the tender channel where an import file disqualifies

11. Integration

Integration is mandatory here more than anywhere in the Group. Idenze Distribution takes committed volume from first commercial batch under a supply agreement with a price formula and payment undertaking; Idenze Consumer Health takes sterile topicals and ophthalmics. Idenze University's teaching hospital is the anchor institutional customer — but it is built in the university's T-C tranche (Years 9–11), so it does not exist as a buyer in our first commercial years: design for it, do not plan on it, and treat other teaching hospitals and state schemes as the Years 1–5 market. Okodu Power supplies power under penalty terms, because a power event here is a rejected batch; Okodu Construction builds, with a carve-out: clean-room construction is a specialist discipline (ISO 14644 envelope integrity, panel systems, HEPA installation, slope-to-drain piping), and if it cannot meet that standard the package goes to a specialist contractor — the licence outranks the synergy. Insurance, FX and treasury come from Akunnia Group; financing from Aku Capital; freight and cold chain from Uli Group; stability work from Idenze Research; technicians from Idenze Polytechnic.

Ring-fencing. This entity needs its own board, audit and quality system; sterility-assurance accountability cannot be delegated, and there are no cross-guarantees to the university, the hospital, Idenze Pharma or Akunnia Group. A quality failure here must be containable within this company's own licence and balance sheet.

12. First ninety days

The pre-gate quarter — the work that decides whether T0 is authorised.

  1. Constitute the entity and board; start the search for two independent directors.
  2. Confirm the gate in writing: Idenze Pharma EBITDA-positive for four quarters — or the quarter ends here.
  3. Hold the NAFDAC sterile pre-application meeting on classification, route per product, sterility-assurance package and inspection standard — the quarter's most valuable output.
  4. Commission the route and selection study for fifteen candidates, each assigned terminal or aseptic, with supplier quotes; and verify the market number with NAFDAC DER, the Ministry of Health and a teaching hospital, since §2's figure is derived.
  5. Issue RFQs to three clean-room and fill-line contractors with a separately priced clean-room and WFI package; build the bottom-up cost model for the top six SKUs.
  6. Open the four critical searches — MD, Head of QA, QP equivalent, Head of Sterility Assurance.
  7. Secure anchor demand: heads of terms with Idenze Distribution and two teaching hospitals.
  8. Confirm power and construction with Okodu Power and Okodu Construction — including whether the Group's contractor can deliver an ISO 14644 envelope.
  9. Cost the contract-manufacturing bridge for two hero SKUs, and establish the ring-fencing record with a re-cut Group T5 envelope.
  10. Commission the sterile capacity register — every Nigerian facility holding a live NAFDAC sterile manufacturing licence, with line capacity, GMP and media-fill history, ownership, and whether it is for sale or for tolling — plus firm tolling terms from three. Budget ₦70m. This decides whether sterile injectables is a build or a buy, and no other work in the quarter can change the size of T1.

The day-90 gate. Proceed only if: Idenze Pharma is EBITDA-positive for four quarters; NAFDAC confirms the sterile licence pathway in writing; proposals land within ±20% of the ₦41.6bn T1 budget with the FX contingency; the four critical hires are identified; anchor volume covers 40% of Sterile Y3 nameplate; and the Group Board confirms the re-cut T5 envelope, this entity's own board and audit, and gearing within 15–25%. If any fails, delay twelve months.

Prepared for the Ezeme Group Board and Idenze Group. Market, regulatory and standards figures carry source links; capital, unit-economics, headcount and utilisation figures are planning estimates at ₦1,600/USD requiring local verification — the Nigerian sterile-market size, current clean-room and fill-line quotations, and NAFDAC's inspection timing for sterile facilities — before any capital commitment. Sequenced behind 18_Idenze_Pharma.md: sterile is a separate clean-room capital step, never a line extension.

Idenze Distribution — Pharmaceutical Wholesale & Distribution

Naming: companies take the children's names plus a plain function — Ezeme Group is the mother company; Isiome · Akunnia · Idenze · Uli · Okodu Group are its five groups. See ../EZEME_NAMING_ARCHITECTURE.md (v5.0).

FX note: naira is primary; this plan uses ₦1,600/USD, the library planning rate in plans/README.md. Spot was ~₦1,328/USD (CBN NFEM, Sept 2026). Dollar figures are indicative only and are not comparable across plans — 18_Idenze_Pharma.md used ₦1,400/USD.
EntityIdenze Distribution Ltd (RC to be obtained), wholly owned by Idenze Group
OwnershipEzeme Family Trust (Mauritius) → Ezeme Family Holdings (Mauritius) Ltd → Ezeme Group Nigeria Ltd → Idenze Group → Idenze Distribution Ltd
SiteNkpor distribution centre, Idemili North LGA, Anambra State, beside the Idenze Pharma plant; leased satellite hubs Lagos, Kano, Aba/Port Harcourt
ScopeNAFDAC-licensed pharmaceutical wholesale, cold chain distribution, controlled-substance distribution, institutional tender supply and third-party logistics across Nigeria and ECOWAS
Horizon2026–2041
Ring-fencingIts own licence (NAFDAC GDP Regulations), its own board, its own audit. Controlled substances sit in a ring-fenced account with an independent accountable officer; a diversion or licensing failure here must never reach the Group's banking or the university's accreditation.

1. Thesis

One sentence. Nigeria's medicines reach patients through a fragmented, largely informal wholesale layer that cannot hold a temperature, cannot prove a custody chain and cannot be inspected — and Idenze Distribution is a licensed, GDP-compliant, cold-chain-capable wholesaler that is both the guaranteed route to market for the Group's own plant and a standalone margin business selling third-party products through the same warehouse and trucks.

Why distribution is the pharma plant's insurance policy. Nigeria's manufacturing weakness is well documented; its distribution weakness is worse, because a correctly made medicine becomes a substandard one in an uncontrolled warehouse. This company takes a committed share of Idenze Pharma's output from launch. That does one specific thing: it converts the plant's first eighteen months of demand from a sales problem into a logistics problem. A defined volume is already contracted to a distributor the Group controls, under a supply agreement with a price formula and a payment undertaking. Base-load throughput is the single most important commercial protection in the pharma programme, and it lives here.

Why it is also a business in its own right. A distribution asset is a fixed-cost asset. Once the Nkpor DC is built, GDP-validated and staffed, every additional manufacturer's line loaded onto it improves the economics of every other line, at almost no incremental fixed cost. The same cold room, qualified staff and licensed fleet serve Group and third-party product alike. Third-party volume is therefore not a side activity — by Year 10 it should be the majority of revenue, and it is what makes the anchor commitment cheap rather than a subsidy.

Why now. NAFDAC issued revised Good Storage and Distribution Practice Guidelines effective 26 November 2024 and retains WHO Maturity Level 3. Inspection of the distribution layer is tightening while the layer itself stays informal — so a licensed wholesaler with a clean file becomes the only counterparty many manufacturers and institutional buyers can use.

2. Market

Size. The IFC/World Bank Nigeria Country Private Sector Diagnostic anchors pharmaceutical sales at US$2.03bn (2023) growing at a 9.1% seven-year compound rate; some estimates reach US$4.5bn. There is no published figure for the wholesale margin pool. On a 12–18% all-in wholesale margin the derived pool is roughly US$240–370m a year before cold chain and controlled substances carry their premium. That is a derived estimate requiring local verification, not a market report.

Structure and informality. Supply runs through a few concentrated open drug markets — Onitsha's Ogbo-Ogwu/Iweka cluster, Idumota in Lagos, Aba, Kano's Sabon Gari — where thousands of stalls trade in physical cash with no continuous temperature control and a chain no regulator can fully trace. Nkpor sits within a few kilometres of the Onitsha medicine market: the Group's greatest distribution advantage and its biggest reputational hazard, since proximity to the informal trade is an optics problem as well as an opportunity.

The open drug market problem. Efficient on price, defective on quality: no cold chain, no expiry discipline, no batch traceability to the patient, no meaningful barrier to a falsified pack entering a legitimate shelf. NAFDAC seizures continue at scale — ₦1.3bn seized at Kano alone (Guardian Nigeria) — and research on substandard and falsified medicines finds harm concentrated in exactly the categories this company will carry: antimalarials, antibiotics, maternal medicines.

Hospital and institutional supply. Teaching hospitals, federal and state ministries, NHIA and the HMOs, and mission networks buy on tender against inspection records, batch documentation and delivery reliability. Most existing wholesalers cannot produce the file. This is the channel where a compliant distributor wins on qualification rather than price — and it pays in 90–120 days, a working-capital burden the Group can carry and an informal competitor cannot.

ECOWAS export corridors. Nigeria holds roughly 60% of ECOWAS drug manufacturing (IFC/World Bank), so the flow is Nigerian product moving west and north: Benin, Togo, Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire, Niger, Cameroon. Export needs WAHO/ECOWAS harmonised dossiers plus destination-country registration and a licensed local importer (WAHO harmonisation work). The corridors are the ones Uli Freight is building (35_Uli_Freight.md) — which is why an export desk is credible here and expensive for a standalone wholesaler.

4. Operating model

Distribution centre. Phase 1 at Nkpor: ~4,000 m² — ~350 m² validated 2–8 °C cold room, ~150 m² controlled ambient, ~1,200 m² racked ambient storage, quarantine and returns segregation physically and documentarily separated, a controlled-substances vault to NAFDAC/NDLEA specification, and goods-in/goods-out bays on a one-way flow. Phase 2 (Y3–5) expands ambient to ~8,000 m² and cold to ~900 m². Satellite hubs in Lagos, Kano and Aba are leased and cross-docked, never owned, until volume justifies a second site.

Why Nkpor. Captive power from Okodu Power is decisive, and it is a cold chain fact rather than a real-estate preference: a validated cold room burning diesel at Okodu's ₦780/kWh baseline has a materially worse cost base than one on a blended supply near ₦150/kWh. Nkpor also sits beside the plant, on the Onitsha trade cluster and at the head of the Uli Freight corridor.

GDP compliance. The system is the NAFDAC Good Storage and Distribution Practice Guidelines (Nov 2024) read with the GDP Regulations, aligned to WHO guidance: a Quality Manual; SOPs for receipt, put-away, picking, dispatch, returns, recall and destruction; temperature mapping of every cold and controlled-ambient volume; qualification and validation of equipment and processes before use and after any significant change (stated explicitly in the guidelines); change control; training records per person, not per department; self-inspection; and supplier and customer qualification files. The Responsible Pharmacist and Quality Manager report to the board, not the Managing Director — the same reporting-line logic that protects the Pharma plant's licence.

Cold chain equipment and monitoring. Redundant condensing units with automatic changeover and alarm; validated 2–8 °C and 15–25 °C walk-ins; refrigerated vehicles with pre-trip validation and data-logger verification; validated passive shippers with conditioned phase-change packs for last-mile; continuous electronic monitoring, alarmed to an on-call rota, with documented excursion investigation and CAPA. An excursion that cannot be evidenced is a batch that must be destroyed. Every consignment leaves with its own time-temperature record — that printout is the product.

Inventory and stock control. One WMS on one ERP with batch and expiry at pallet, case and unit level; FEFO picking enforced by the system, not by memory; a rolling 90-day expiry report to the board with a defined quarantine and customer-credit policy; cycle counting by ABC class and a monthly full count in controlled substances; a stock-loss provision reviewed monthly. Expiry, not theft, is the practical cost of this business, and the system is designed around that.

Order to delivery. Order capture via field app or portal → credit check → allocation against batch and expiry → FEFO pick → GDP-compliant secondary packing recording the temperature log and serialised consignment note → dispatch manifest → delivery with signature, timestamp and temperature log retained → proof of delivery reconciled to invoice within 24 hours → returns disposition within 72 hours. Target: order-to-dispatch under 8 working hours for stocked SKUs, next-day delivery in the South-East, 48–72 hours nationally.

Fleet. Own a small core — 4 refrigerated and 6 dry vans for last-mile and the South-East loop. Everything else is bought as a service: linehaul on every corridor from Uli Freight, whose Corridor 1 economics run near ₦92/tonne-km against a ₦48 cost base (35_Uli_Freight.md), better than this company could achieve on its own steel. Buying freight keeps this a distribution business rather than a trucking business. No controlled-substance movement ever runs on a subcontracted unlicensed vehicle.

Traceability. GS1 DataMatrix scanning at receipt, pick and dispatch, integrated with the Pharma plant's serialisation so a batch can be followed from Idenze Pharma's line to the outlet that received it. NAFDAC's Traceability 2.0 framework makes serialisation a market-access prerequisite, not an option. Target recall reach: a specific outlet identified and contacted within 24 hours of a recall decision.

What a purchase delivers, and the one thing that decides whether it works. A licensed wholesaler brings registration, state licences, a fleet, a trained workforce, an institutional and HMO customer list and existing manufacturer credit lines — the last two being what a new distributor spends three years earning. Two diligence gates decide the deal. Budget ₦80m — ₦45m advisory, valuation and registry search, ₦20m legal opinion on premises-registration transferability, ₦15m for site inspections and cold-chain condition surveys [verify]. It buys the coverage this plan otherwise spends three years building, and it is the fastest route to the institutional and HMO accounts §7's margin depends on.

Break-even. Year-3 fixed costs are estimated at ₦7.9bn a year — ₦660m a month (DC, cold chain energy and maintenance, staffing, WMS, insurance, security, compliance, depreciation, finance). At blended contribution of 10.5%, break-even is ~₦75bn of annual revenue, roughly ₦6.3bn a month and about 15,000 orders. That is unreachable at Year-1 volumes, which is why this company is structurally loss-making until Year 3. The path to break-even is not price; it is third-party volume loaded onto a fixed cost base — the reason the third-party line in §3 is strategic rather than incidental.

Steady state (Y8–10): gross margin 12–15%, EBITDA 5–8%, net 3–5%. Distribution is low-margin and high-turn; returns come from capital efficiency and scale, not margin. Revenue: ₦1.6bn Y1; ₦13bn Y3; ₦34bn Y5; ₦95bn by Year 10 (≈US$59m).

The sensitivity that dominates. Not FX directly: inventory is naira, and depreciation revalues stock upward while raising replacement cost. The exposure is interest rates and expiry together — a 22% naira cost of funds on a 45-day cycle plus stock loss above 1.5% of revenue consumes the entire net margin. Both are managed monthly, not annually.

Days 31–60 — make the cost numbers real.

  1. Commission the cold chain and freight cost survey with Okodu Power and Uli Freight: actual ₦/kWh at Nkpor, cold room plant consumption and redundancy specification, reefer operating cost, and Uli's corridor tariff applied to our real shipment profile. Replace every imported cost estimate in §6.
  2. Specify and tender the Nkpor DC — two architectural/engineering bids, a cold room specialist bid, and a layout meeting NAFDAC GDP and controlled-vault requirements. Do not build before NAFDAC has seen the layout.
  3. Select the WMS/ERP with GS1 DataMatrix serialisation, batch/expiry/FEFO control, temperature-monitoring integration and traceability reporting; confirm it accepts Idenze Pharma's serialisation output.
  4. Commission the demand survey across the South-East, Lagos and the North-West: candidate outlets, cold chain accounts, institutional and HMO pipelines, and current distributor terms. Size the real order book, not the market.
  5. Publish the internal control framework — two-person rule, vault protocol, 24-hour discrepancy reporting, no cash handling by drivers — before anyone is hired, so the culture exists before the habits do.

Days 61–90 — commit or defer.

  1. Recruit the first four hires: Managing Director, Quality Manager (GDP), Cold Chain Manager, Finance and Credit Controller.
  2. Approach manufacturers — three Nigerian manufacturers and two importers or authorised agents — for third-party distribution terms and opening credit; secure letters of intent for two external agreements, the T2 release condition.
  3. Run site and route reconnaissance with Uli Freight on the Nkpor–Lagos and Nkpor–Onitsha–Aba legs and cost the last-mile loop against real road and levy conditions.
  4. Open NCS/NDLEA engagement in writing, name the intended accountable officer, and confirm the evidence of trading history the authorisation will require.
  5. Day-90 board gate: release T1 only if counsel has confirmed the NAFDAC/PCN pathway in writing, the Idenze Pharma supply agreement is signed or in final form, and cold chain and construction costs have been verified by live survey. If any of the three fails, hold the build, run a leased cross-dock for two quarters, and re-test. The licence is the business — never build a warehouse around an assumption.
  6. Open the wholesaler acquisition track in parallel with the build. Commission the register of every PCN-registered wholesaler in Anambra, Enugu, Lagos and Kano — premises registration and currency, state licences actually held, cold-chain capability, fleet, customer concentration, revenue and asking price — and take two non-binding approaches. Budget ₦80m. State-by-state coverage takes three years to build and one share purchase to buy, and the institutional and HMO accounts §7's margin rests on travel with the acquired entity.

23 — IDENZE RESEARCH

Clinical, Analytical & Formulation Research

Naming: companies take the children's names plus a plain function — Ezeme Group is the mother company; Isiome · Akunnia · Idenze · Uli · Okodu Group are its five groups. See ../EZEME_NAMING_ARCHITECTURE.md (v5.0).

FX note: naira is primary; dollars indicative at ₦1,600/USD, flat in nominal terms (spot ~₦1,328, CBN NFEM, Sept 2026) and not comparable across plans. See plans/README.md.

Ezeme Group · Idenze Group (Pharma & Education) · Entity Idenze Research Ltd (CAMA), subsidiary of Idenze Group Ltd (Idenze) · Horizon 15 years · Year 1 = 2027.

Companions: 17_Idenze_Group.md · 18_Idenze_Pharma.md · 19_Idenze_Therapeutics.md · 24_Idenze_University.md. Sterile & Injectables, Consumer Health and Distribution appear as interfaces only — separate companies and boards.

Position: this plan converts the Group's two most expensive assets — a GMP pharmaceutical plant and an accredited medical school with a teaching hospital — into evidence no competitor can buy. It is the most defensible advantage in the Group, and the easiest to destroy.

1. Thesis

One sentence: The Group owns both halves of the evidence machine — manufacturers (Idenze Pharma, Idenze Therapeutics) and an accredited medical school with a teaching hospital (Idenze University) — so it can run bioequivalence, stability, formulation and clinical studies in-house, converting commodity generics and cannabis-derived extracts into evidence-backed brands; and precisely because the Group owns both halves, the evidence will be disbelieved unless research is governed in a visibly independent way.

Why both halves is unreplicable. Nigeria has manufacturers — about 190 firms, including Fidson, Emzor, May & Baker and Neimeth (NAFDAC via Radio Nigeria, 2026) — and it has medical schools with teaching hospitals. No competitor owns both, and the reason is structural: a manufacturer will not fund an accredited medical school through twelve deficit years, and a university will not raise ₦300bn+ to build a GMP plant and hold a NAFDAC manufacturing licence. Each half is a decade-long, licence-gated, capital-destroying project before it earns. The Group has both in the programme. So its marginal cost of a bioequivalence study or an investigator-initiated trial is a fraction of market price — and its queue position is zero. A competitor waits nine to eighteen months for a foreign CRO slot and pays US$120k–400k per molecule (18_Idenze_Pharma.md).

Why that converts commodities into brands. A generic paracetamol tablet competes on price, set by whoever shaves the thinnest margin. The same molecule with an in-house bioequivalence package, an ICH Zone IVb stability dossier and — for cannabinoids — a completed trial in a named Nigerian indication is a product with evidence behind it. Evidence buys a cleaner NAFDAC registration, prescriber and hospital-channel preference that does not collapse on a ten-kobo price difference, and an export dossier a foreign regulator can assess.

The price of being believed. When the sponsor owns the trial site, regulators, ethics reviewers and journal editors ask one question: whose evidence is this? That is the standard problem of sponsor-controlled research everywhere, and its answer is procedural, not rhetorical. Idenze Research therefore needs a research ethics committee with an external majority, a documented conflict-of-interest policy, publication rights resting with investigators, registration before first enrolment, and data-integrity and retention standards meeting international expectations. Getting this wrong destroys the entire advantage, because evidence that is not accepted is worth nothing — it wastes the capex and contaminates every later filing. §4 treats this as the design constraint, not a compliance annex.

2. Market

Read together, the market question answers itself. The continent carrying a quarter of the world's disease burden runs under 5% of its registered trials, and three-quarters of even that is two countries. Nigeria — 220 million people, the largest manufacturing base in ECOWAS — contributes 457 studies and 42 industry-sponsored ones. The constraint is not demand for evidence. It is supply of credible sites, accredited laboratories and investigators who have run a GCP trial.

The nearest and most certain market is bioequivalence and stability testing for Nigerian manufacturers. The NAFDAC Guidelines on the Investigation of Bioequivalence 2025 (effective 5 May 2025) require in vivo demonstration outside the biowaiver classes, mandate randomised two-period crossover designs and set a floor of 12 evaluable subjects per treatment. The BCS biowaiver form waives the in vivo study only where solubility, permeability and dissolution data justify it — so every ineligible molecule needs one, and the NAFDAC bioequivalence implementation plan shows the Agency intends to enforce rather than waive. Every one of those ~190 firms has a registration calendar whose critical path runs through a laboratory that does not exist in Nigeria at scale.

The specific gap: a Nigerian laboratory and clinical pharmacology unit that NAFDAC will accept, ISO 17025 will accredit, and a foreign regulator will not discount. The gap is not "Africa needs research" but "a Nigerian manufacturer cannot get a bioequivalence study done in Nigeria by a laboratory whose data an assessor will take at face value."

The CRO landscape — and the honest limit. Africa's contract research market is small, fragmented and thin at the bioanalytical layer (6Wresearch), with capacity concentrated in South Africa, Kenya and Egypt. The third-party market alone would not justify this capex — Nigerian BE volume is hundreds of studies a year, not thousands, and must be sized by a manufacturer pipeline survey before Tranche 2 is released (§6). Hence §7: Idenze Research is not a CRO that happens to have a parent with a factory. It is the Group's evidence function, which sells its spare capacity.

3. Product & service lines

#LineScope

2Analytical testing & method developmentAssay, related substances, dissolution at pH 1.2/4.5/6.8, residual solvents, elemental impurities; bioanalysis validated to ICH M10
3Stability studiesICH Zone IVb (30 °C/75% RH) and accelerated; long-term, intermediate, photostability; shelf-life assignment
